title: Dolphins veteran Austin Jackson: Jeff Hafley practices are fun, like Brian Flores practices
summary: Dolphins offensive tackle Austin Jackson has been in Miami since he was the team's first-round draft pick in 2020, which means Jeff Hafley is his third head coach.
full_text: Dolphins offensive tackle Austin Jackson has been in Miami since he was the team's first-round draft pick in 2020, which means Jeff Hafley is his third head coach. And Hafley's training camp practices are reminding him of his first head coach. Asked what practice was like after the Dolphins opened camp, Jackson said it reminded him of Brian Flores, the Dolphins' head coach in Jackson's first two seasons. "It was fun. It was fun. It was kind of similar to how Brian Flores ran practices, very similar," Jackson said. "We just got to team right away. Not as many seven-on-sevens, hardly any seven-on-sevens, really, with Flo I don't remember any. Definitely, it was nice." Asked how Hafley's approach differs from former coach Mike McDaniel, Jackson said he likes having the whole team together under Hafley. "It was a little bit more reps, more team reps in practice, which is nice," Jackson said. "Previous coach was a lot more segmented and very intentional on certain things." Since signing a three-year contract extension late in the 2023 season, Jackson has struggled with injuries, missing most of 2024 with a knee injury and most of 2025 with a toe injury. The most important thing for Jackson at training camp is that he's healthy enough to be on the field.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deebo Samuel returns to the 49ers on a one-year deal
summary: It's reportedly a one-year deal worth up to $7 million.
full_text: At a time when a 49ers receiver badly wants to join the Commanders, a former Commanders receiver is rejoining the 49ers. Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Deebo Samuel is returning to San Francisco . It's a one-year deal worth up to $7 million. (The base value has not yet been disclosed.) A second-round pick of the 49ers in 2019, Samuel became a first-team All-Pro and a Pro Bowler in his third season, with 1,405 receiving yards and 365 rushing yards in 2021. Things got ugly between Samuel and the 49ers in the 2022 offseason, with Samuel asking to be traded. He eventually signed a three-year, $73.5 million extension. Before the final year of the deal in 2025, the 49ers traded Samuel to the Commanders for a fifth-round pick. He also agreed to a reduced contract, with a $17 million base salary and up to $3 milion in incentives. With 2024 first-rounder Ricky Pearsall's season in doubt due to the lingering effects of a knee injury, the 49ers needed help at the position. Samuel joins a depth chart that includes Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowling, and Demarcus Robinson. Samuel, 30, has one career 1,000-yard season. Last year in Washington, he caught 72 passes for 727 yards and five touchdowns.
author: Mike Florio

title: Inside the Jalen Carter deal
summary: Earlier this week, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter became the highest-paid interior defensive lineman in NFL history.
full_text: ' Earlier this week, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter became the highest-paid interior defensive lineman in NFL history. The full details are now out. Here's the breakdown, per a source with knowledge of the terms: 1. Signing bonus: $22.5 million. 2. 2026 base salary: $1.145 million, fully guaranteed. 3. 2026 weight bonus : $250,000, fully guaranteed (but must be earned). 4. 2027 option bonus: $14.94557 million, fully guaranteed. 5. 2027 offseason workout bonus: $500,000, fully guaranteed (but must be earned). 6. 2027 base salary: $1.26 million, fully guaranteed. 7. 2027 weight bonus: $250,000, fully guaranteed (but must be earned). 8. 2028 option bonus: $27.435 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2027. 9. 2028 offseason workout bonus: $500,000, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2027. 10. 2028 base salary: $1.305 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2027. 11. 2028 per-game roster bonus: $510,000 total, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2027. 12. 2028 weight bonus: $250,000, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2027. 13. 2029 option bonus: $33.39 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 14. 2029 offseason workout bonus: $500,000, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 15. 2029 base salary: $1.35 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 16. 2029 per-game roster bonus: $510,000 total, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 17. 2029 weight bonus: $250,000, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 18. 2030 option bonus: $35.26 million. 19. 2030 offseason workout bonus: $500,000. 20. 2030 base salary: $1.48 million. 21. 2030 per-game roster bonus: $510,000 total. 22. 2030 weight bonus: $250,000. 23. 2031 option bonus: $35.215 million. 24. 2031 offseason workout bonus: $500,000. 25. 2031 base salary: $1.525 million. 26. 2031 per-game roster bonus: $510,000 total. 27. 2031 weight bonus: $250,000. The four-year extension has a base value of $152 million, for a new-money average of $38 million per year. The contract includes a $4 million escalator for 2030 and a $4 million escalator for 2031, pushing the total potential value to $160 million. With two remaining years and a payout of $30.85057 million, the total base value over six years is $182.85057 million. That's a per-year average from signing of $30.475 million. The structure makes the first two years — $40.85057 million — fully guaranteed. The timing of the 2028 an 2029 guarantees makes the first four years — $106.85057 million — guaranteed as a practical matter.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals RB Tyler Allgeier on welcoming Jeremiyah Love: "There's no point being a jerk"
summary: It's the second time in Allgeier's career that his team has used a high first-round pick on a running back.
full_text: ' As a rookie with the Falcons, Tyler Allgeier ran for 1,035 yards — and then the Falcons used the eighth overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft on running back Bijan Robinson. This year, Allgeier left the Falcons for the Cardinals in free agency — and then the Cardinals used the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft on running back Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier says he's fine with that. Talking to reporters for the first time since Love's arrival in Arizona, Allgeier said he's doing everything he can to help the rookie acclimate to the NFL, even though he knows Love is being groomed as the starter and Allgeier will get a lesser role in the offense because Love was drafted. "It's not like there's any bad blood, we're just building that relationship and we're pretty close right now," Allgeier said. "There’s no point in being a jerk about it. That's not going to get you anywhere in life, in this business, in this sport." Allgeier said he knows the Cardinals drafted the player they think can most improve the team, and he embraces that. “The front office has their reasons and I think it's another weapon on the offensive side. I think it was a great pick, great player, great competition in the room," Allgeier said. "I knew what I was getting into."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jalen Carter's deal has a $250,000 annual "weight bonus"
summary: After signing defensive tackle Jalen Carter to a record-setting deal, Eagles G.M.
full_text: After signing defensive tackle Jalen Carter to a record-setting deal, Eagles G.M. Howie Roseman said he has no off-field concerns about the player. Based on the contract details, the team has at least one. Per a source with knowledge of the terms, Carter's contract contains an annual "weight bonus" in the amount of $250,000. The weight limit, and the timing for compliance, aren't currently known. Carter is officially listed at 314 pounds. That was his weight at the 2023 Scouting Combine. (At his Pro Day the following month, he was nine pounds heavier .) While $250,000 represents a relatively small piece of Carter's financial puzzle, the issue was significant enough for the Eagles to bargain for a specific incentive for Carter to keep his weight under a specific maximum. The term is an unusual one. Over the years, we've broken down many veteran contracts. Not many include a weight bonus.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dak Prescott, Cowboys nickname their offense "Greatest Offense There Is"
summary: The Cowboys are talking the talk.
full_text: The Cowboys are talking the talk. Can they back it up? Dak Prescott showed up to training camp wearing a Super Bowl XXX championship T-shirt. That's the last Super Bowl the franchise won, which came more than 30 years ago. "It's just a manifesting thing," Prescott said Thursday, via Fox 4. "Going into year 11, I'm not going to shy away from it. When you don't have it, it sucks. "Why shy away from that now? Why shy away from asking people to hold me to the same standard that I believe I can accomplish and that this team can accomplish?" Prescott also revealed the nickname for the team's offense this season: GOTI. It stands for: Greatest Offense There Is. Prescott presented the idea to the offensive skill players during their annual bonding trip, which this summer was held in Park City, Utah. It was well received. “We were close to some historic things last year,” Prescott said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “And when you have the guys [on the offense], why can’t we be? Let’s be the Greatest Offense There Is. You’ve heard of the Greatest Show On Turf and all of the other nicknames. We take pride in it, and it’s the way we’ve been practicing.” The Cowboys finished second in total offense (391.9 yards per game) to the Rams last season, and Dallas was seventh in scoring (27.7 points). The Cowboys have their entire starting offense back this season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jeff Ulbrich's wife, Cristina, dies after a battle with cancer
summary: Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich has been absent from the start of training camp for personal reasons.
full_text: Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich has been absent from the start of training camp for personal reasons. The team announced Thursday night that Ulbrich's wife, Cristina, has died. "The Atlanta Falcons are heartbroken by the passing of Cristina Ulbrich, beloved wife of defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, after her courageous battle with cancer," the Falcons said in a statement. "Cristina was a devoted wife, mother, and friend whose strength, grace, and resilience touched all who knew her. She was a constant source of love and support to Jeff, their family, and the broader Falcons community. "On behalf of the entire organization, we extend our deepest condolences to Jeff, their children, and all who loved Cristina. "During this incredibly difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with the Ulbrich family. We ask that their privacy be respected as they grieve this profound loss, and we stand with them in support and remembrance of Cristina's life." Our thoughts and prayers go out to the Ulbrich family and the Falcons organization.
author: Charean Williams

title: George Pickens appreciates Jerry Jones' kind words
summary: George Pickens heard Jerry Jones' comment from Tuesday about the wide receiver potentially being "a Cowboy for the rest of his career."
full_text: George Pickens heard Jerry Jones' comment from Tuesday about the wide receiver potentially being " a Cowboy for the rest of his career ." Pickens appreciated it. " Super excited ," Pickens said, via the team website. "I'm always super happy when someone thinks highly of me, so shoutout to Jerry." The Pro Bowler has put his head down and gone to work despite being disappointed about not getting a long-term deal. He will play this season on the one-year, fully guaranteed $27.3 million franchise tag. "I left it up to agents, so I was, even when we were nine, 10 months from training camp, I was already thinking about ball. I was already training," Pickens said. "I kind of leave that to the people that can do that. For me, I just make catches, make plays, be a playmaker." Pickens had a career year in his first season in Dallas, with 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. With another season like last season, Pickens will get paid handsomely by someone. He and the offense expect to be even better than they were in 2025. "That's the thing, the limitations and the nuance of a limitation, you shouldn't put that on yourself," Pickens said. "You can really do anything you want. I feel like as an offense, that's one thing and one mindset that we have. Just trying to be through the roof."
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills sign WR Dante Pettis
summary: The Bills worked out veteran wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge, Dante Pettis and Isaiah Whitehead.
full_text: The Bills worked out veteran wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge, Dante Pettis and Isaiah Whitehead. Shortly thereafter, the team announced it has signed Pettis to a one-year deal. In a corresponding move, wide receiver Jalen Virgil was waived with a non-football injury. Pettis, 30, has eight years of NFL experience with four different teams, most recently playing for the Saints the past two seasons. In 2025, Pettis played eight games, seeing action on 114 offensive snaps and 53 on special teams. He totaled nine catches for 127 yards and averaged 23.4 yards on 15 kickoff returns and 6.1 yards on 13 punt returns. In his career, Pettis has 92 receptions for 1,231 yards and 13 touchdowns across 66 games. Pettis entered the league as a second-round pick of the 49ers in 2018.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens RB Derrick Henry has no thoughts of retirement
summary: Ravens running back Derrick Henry is 32.
full_text: ' Ravens running back Derrick Henry is 32. That's 2 years beyond where most running backs are run off. Henry, though, is defying the odds. In the two seasons since he turned 30 and joined the Ravens, Henry has rushed for 3,516 yards, averaged 5.6 yards per carry and scored 32 touchdowns. Henry is entering his 11th season with no thoughts of his career ending any time soon. “I don’t try to enter another season thinking about retiring and have that on my mind,” Henry said after the Ravens’ training camp practice Thursday, via Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com. “ That’s not even my mindset . My mindset is: How can I get better, be the best I can be so we can be the best team we can be? But no, I haven’t thought about retirement at all.” The five-time Pro Bowler, who has put together a Hall of Fame resume, still has plenty left to accomplish. He has never won a Super Bowl ring, which he says is "the No. 1 goal, always," and he has a chance to move up on the NFL's all-time rushing list. His 13,018 rushing yards rank 10th, and with another 1,500-yard season, he can pass Eric Dickerson (13,259), Jerome Bettis (13,662), LaDainian Tomlinson (13,684) and Curtis Martin (14,101) into sixth place. Emmitt Smith, the NFL's all-time leading rusher, was 35 years old in his final season of 2004. Henry isn't thinking about how long he's going to play, but has no thoughts of retirement. “I love the game, and once I feel like that love is gone, then I’ll hang it up," Henry said. "But I’m just focused on getting better.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Packers to sign WR Kaden Prather
summary: Wide receiver Kaden Prather is going from the UFL to the NFL.
full_text: Wide receiver Kaden Prather is going from the UFL to the NFL. Prather's agent told NFL Media that his client is signing with the Packers. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that Prather tried out for the team on Thursday. Prather was a Bills seventh-round pick out of Maryland in 2025, but he was waived off of injured reserve ahead of the start of the regular season. He moved on to Louisville in the UFL and contributed nine catches for 148 yards to the league champions. The Packers also worked out long snapper Cal Adomitis, wide receiver Elijhah Badger, tight end McCallan Castles, wide receiver Elijah Cooks, long snapper John Ferlmann, tight end Brandon Frazier, long snapper Brent Matiscik, wide receiver Titus Mokiao-Atimalala, and tight end Briley Moore.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sam Darnold after Super Bowl season: "I think I can always get better"
summary: Quarterback Sam Darnold made the most of his first year in Minnesota.
full_text: Quarterback Sam Darnold made the most of his first year in Minnesota. Which gave him an opportunity in Seattle. Where he absolutely made the most of it, winning the Super Bowl. So what's his personal plan for 2026? “I think I can always get better," Darnold told reporters on Thursday. "There were a lot of things for me like moving on in my progressions and working from one field to the other. I felt like I was throwing behind some targets, especially if I was going left to right. "There were a couple throws in the Super Bowl that I'd like to have back, and then not only during the Super Bowl, but before that as well, where I just missed some guys going through my progressions. So I think just being calm with my feet and making sure my feet don't get super wide. A lot of guys like to keep their base wide, but my base has always been wide, and sometimes I get too wide. So, just making sure that I keep my base with the hip width apart, is going to make me a little bit more accurate. Just working on little things like that and always working on the deep ball every offseason as well.” Darnold sees getting better as an annual challenge. "There's always going to [improve]," he said. "This game is so tough, so difficult, and there's so much that goes on for us as quarterbacks mentally. I think making sure when we get to the game that everything physically is just muscle memory, and that's why you work so hard in the offseason so that you're not thinking about those things when you get out there on Sunday.” It worked for Darnold last year, erasing the narrative that he can't show up in the biggest moments. Not that it mattered to him. “For me, I never paid attention to stuff like that," Darnold said. "I've been very confident in myself. I've been very confident in my teammates and the coaches that I have. I don't allow myself to really pay attention to anything like that. If I do catch wind of it, I have my process on how to handle that. Like I said, it's just about handling my process and doing it my way, so that when I get out there, it’s not about what I've done or what I'm going to do, it's about what I'm doing right now. I think if I just continue to have that mindset as we go on, we'll be just fine.” Even so, he continues to be on a year-to-year arrangement in Seattle, with no new contract (yet) despite last year's Super Bowl win. He'll make $27.5 million this year, with up to $5 million available in incentives. Even if Darnold earns every penny, he's still barely north of 50 percent of the top of the market. Unless he gets an extension, 2026 becomes an important year for Darnold. Regress, and the Seahawks could swap him out for, say, Baker Mayfield (who lit up the Seattle defense during the 2025 season). Perform well again (with a new offensive coordinator), and Darnold could get the kind of contract that will secure his future in Seattle.
author: Mike Florio

title: T.J. Watt embracing a chance to play both sides: You're going to see us move around
summary: Steelers outside linebacker T.J.
full_text: '' Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt has played mostly on the left side in his career. He took only 10 snaps on the right side last season, leaving that side to Alex Highsmith. Watt indicated in the offseason that he would move around more, and according to Bob Labriola of the team website, that has been the case in training camp. Watt played both sides in Thursday's practice, per Labriola. The four-time All-Pro, who has admitted being resistant to playing the right side, has embraced a chance to move around this season in Patrick Graham's defense. " Very dynamic , very elite group," Watt said about his position group. "I think you're going to see us moving all around. I know I say it every year, but I think you're truly going to see us moving all around this year. It's a better problem to have when you have guys who are really capable to aﬀect the game in any area. I think that if we do things that we really set out to do in this training camp and get this thing like a well-oiled machine with us three, it'll be special. "I'm just trying to be open-minded, just trying to do anything to aﬀect [the opposing offense], whether it's how they are doing protection schemes, how they're running the ball. Wherever I can move around or just knock down inside, be able to allow [Nate] Herbig to come outside, whatever it takes to win football games, whatever it takes to mess up the oﬀensive scheme, I'm willing to do." Watt led the NFL in sacks with 19 in 2023. He has only 18.5 over the past two seasons, including seven in 2025 when he missed three games.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers worked out three RBs after Jordan James' injury
summary: 49ers running back Jordan James was competing with Kaelon Black — a third-round pick this spring — for the primary backup job behind Christian McCaffrey until his injury on Monday.
full_text: 49ers running back Jordan James was competing with Kaelon Black — a third-round pick this spring — for the primary backup job behind Christian McCaffrey until his injury on Monday. James' rib fracture has the 49ers looking at free agent running backs. The 49ers worked out Raheem Blackshear, Khalil Herbert and Owen Wright on Thursday, according to the NFL's personnel notice. Blackshear entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Bills in 2022. He has played 41 games for the Panthers, rushing for 203 yards and three touchdowns and catching 16 passes for 138 yards. Herbert was a sixth-round pick of the Bears in 2021. He has appeared in 63 games, with 13 starts, totaling 1,957 rushing yards and nine touchdowns. Herbert has also caught 54 passes for 316 yards and two touchdowns during stints with the Bears, Bengals and Jets. Wright signed with the Ravens as an undrafted free agent in 2023 and has appeared in four career games with the Ravens and Buccaneers. He has 6 rushing yards on three carries.
author: Charean Williams

title: Palo Alto police won't release bodycam video or 911 call from Kyle Shanahan crash
summary: Some information has been released by the authorities in connection with 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan's recent car accident.
full_text: Some information has been released by the authorities in connection with 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan's recent car accident. More information will not be. The Palo Alto Police Department will not be releasing bodycam footage, the 911 call, or the accident report, according to Tony Farmer. Via TMZ, the PAPD said the information is " exempt from disclosure " under the California Public Records Act. "Nothing will be released related to this accident," a PAPD spokesperson told TMZ. Which means we'll now be taking a closer look at whether the PAPD's position holds water . The 49ers concealed the July 14 accident for 11 days. After a " clerical error " attributed fault to the other driver, Shanahan told reporters that he caused the crash after taking his eyes off the road to retrieve his phone, which had fallen from his lap. Shanahan suffered multiple injuries, including a severe concussion that has kept him from fully participating in 49ers training camp.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chris Olave agrees to four-year extension with Saints
summary: Olave's deal is worth $132 million with $90 million guaranteed.
full_text: Saints wide receiver Chris Olave didn't do team drills in the team's first training camp practice for what head coach Kellen Moore called business reasons, but there won't be any reason for Olave to limit his participation for the rest of camp. Olave's agents Drew and Jason Rosenhaus told ESPN that Olave has agreed to a four-year extension with the Saints. The deal is worth $132 million with $90 million in guaranteed money. The agreement comes a couple of days after General Manager Mickey Loomis said that the team was hopeful to lock up the 2022 first-round pick beyond the fifth and final year of his rookie deal. Loomis also noted that Olave's injury history, which includes multiple concussions and last year's blood clot in his lung, as " an element " of the negotiations. Given the size of the commitment the Saints are making, Olave's production — 291 catches for 3,728 yards and 19 touchdowns — was a bigger element and Olave is set to have five more years to build those numbers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Free agent S Jordan Whitehead visits Steelers
summary: The Steelers hosted veteran safety Jordan Whitehead for a free agent visit on Thursday, according to the NFL personnel notice.
full_text: The Steelers hosted veteran safety Jordan Whitehead for a free agent visit on Thursday, according to the NFL personnel notice. Whitehead, who played at the University of Pittsburgh, recently was cleared to resume his football career. He also has worked out for the Colts and the Texans. Whitehead missed all of last season after being seriously injured in a two-vehicle car crash in Tampa on Jan. 4, 2025. He underwent neck surgery, putting his future in doubt. Dr. Alex Vaccaro, the Eagles' spine specialist, signed off on Whitehead's return to play in 2026. Whitehead, a fourth-round pick in 2018, played five years for the Buccaneers and two for the Jets. He has played 105 games with 101 starts, totaling 557 tackles, 11 interceptions, 45 passes defensed and two forced fumbles.
author: Charean Williams

title: Aidan Hutchinson: It's "extremely liberating" to focus on football with injury behind me
summary: A year ago, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was full-go in training camp, but he was still focused on recovering from the broken leg that had ended his 2024 season.
full_text: ' A year ago, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was full-go in training camp, but he was still focused on recovering from the broken leg that had ended his 2024 season. This year, Hutchinson has put the injury completely behind him. Hutchinson said today at Lions training camp that it is "extremely liberating" not to be thinking about his injury the way he was a year ago. "I feel like a new person," Hutchinson said. "Physically, mentally, I feel like there was a lot looming last year going into the season. It feels good. Everything's settled and I can just focus on football, keep what's important in front of me" Asked how high his goals are for 2026, Hutchinson said they're sky-high. "Every year," Hutchinson said, "we're shooting for the stars."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Chase Claypool tried out for Colts on Thursday
summary: The Colts brought in a familiar name for a tryout, but it doesn't appear as if it was successful.
full_text: The Colts brought in a familiar name for a tryout, but it doesn't appear as if it was successful. Via the league's daily transaction wire, Chase Claypool was among a group of four players who tried out for Indianapolis on Thursday. But the Colts ended up signing the other receiver who was a part of it — undrafted rookie Liam Clifford. Claypool has not appeared in a regular-season game since 2023 when he played for the Dolphins. He spent time with the Bills in 2024. Running backs Jermar Jefferson and Roydell Williams also tried out for the Colts on Thursday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jets sign WR Quincy Skinner
summary: The Jets shuffled up their wide receiver group on Thursday.
full_text: The Jets shuffled up their wide receiver group on Thursday. They announced the signing of Quincy Skinner to their 90-man roster. Jalen Walthall was waived with an injury designation to make room for Skinner. Skinner signed with the Falcons after going undrafted last year and had three catches for 29 yards in the preseason. He had 66 catches for 809 yards and eight touchdowns during his time at Vanderbilt. Walthall signed with the Texans after going undrafted out of Incarnate Word this year and signed with the Jets after being waived in June. He'll revert to the team's injured reserve if unclaimed and could eventually be released with an injury settlement.
author: Josh Alper

title: Andy Reid on Patrick Mahomes: You see the strength in his legs, which is important
summary: It continues to sound like Mahomes will be ready to start the season after suffering a torn ACL in December.
full_text: While Patrick Mahomes suffered a torn ACL in December, all indications have been that the quarterback is on track to start Week 1 when the Chiefs play the Broncos. Mahomes did not start training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list and started working with the team's rookies last week. With veterans now on the field as well, head coach Andy Reid told reporters on Wednesday that Mahomes has continued to look good in practice. "Yeah, he looked pretty good today, I thought. Strong,” Reid said in his press conference, via transcript from the team. “You see the strength in his legs, which is important with a leg injury. You kind of look at that first. See how his feet are moving, feet are moving well. So, I thought it was positive. I mean, I thought he looked well.” Reid, of course, is watching Mahomes intently throughout camp as the quarterback returns from a major injury. “I’m obviously giving a close eye on him. I’m not the doctor, but I'm keeping a close eye on the small things, technique-wise,” Reid said. “But he's prepared for those things and [assistant athletic trainer] Julie [Frymyer] has done a great job with him, with his rehab of really giving him opportunities to push off, whether it's lateral or straight ahead to make sure he can escape as needed. “He’s got good strength. You make good strength through the practice he’s been in, where he can still bend and throw and he trusts the leg to drive on it. So, I think those are all important things. I stand right behind him. So, we talk.” The Chiefs did bring in Justin Fields to be a high-level backup for the club this season. But it seems like Mahomes is still on the path to starting Week 1.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Undrafted rookie QB Jack Strand working with Falcons' first-team offense
summary: In 2024, the Falcons signed Kirk Cousins in free agency and then drafted Michael Penix in the first round.
full_text: In 2024, the Falcons signed Kirk Cousins in free agency and then drafted Michael Penix in the first round. They moved on from Cousins and signed veteran Tua Tagovailoa this offseason. Yet, it's Jack Strand currently running their offense. The undrafted rookie got a phone call from Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt the night before the first training camp practice. Van Pelt informed Strand that Tagovailoa would miss some time with a back injury and Penix was not cleared for team work, leaving Strand as the only quarterback on the roster. " I didn’t think about it too much ," Strand said after Thursday's practice, via Will McFadden of the team website. "I'm coming into training camp and everything just trying to take it day by day. Keep attacking every day. Keep getting better every day, whether I'm getting a bunch of reps or I'm not getting as many reps. Whatever reps that I do get, whether it's in Indy, whether it's in RVA, whether it's in team, anything, I'm just going to try to attack those reps and try to keep getting with those, and then also from watching the guys around me." The Falcons have since signed veteran Cooper Rush, and Tagovailoa did some light throwing during the individual periods on Thursday. So, Strand might not have much longer with the first-team. But the former Minnesota State-Moorhead is focused on getting better every day, no matter where he is on the depth chart or in the rotation. "That's something that I've been telling myself a ton: Be where your feet are. Enjoy the moment," Strand said. "Don't look in the past. Don't dwell on any mistakes or any success that you might have had. Don't look to the future and wonder what's going to be happening in two weeks, in three weeks, in a couple of months or anything. Just be where your feet are."
author: Charean Williams

title: Colts sign WR Liam Clifford
summary: The Colts have added a receiver.
full_text: ' The Colts have added a receiver. Indianapolis announced the team has signed Liam Clifford. An undrafted free agent, Clifford participated in the club's rookie minicamp on a tryout basis. Clifford played his college ball at Penn State, catching 42 passes for 530 yards with one touchdown over 52 career games with 15 starts.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Malik Nabers: When I'm ready, I'm ready
summary: Nabers said he feels great, but isn't setting any target date for a full return.
full_text: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers is practicing with the team at training camp, but he's not ready to make any guarantees about being in the lineup against the Cowboys on the first Sunday night of the regular season. Nabers is working in individual drills after tearing his ACL in late September 2025. Nabers said on Wednesday that he feels great and that his hope is to keep having good days until he feels prepared to do everything. “Mindset is just keep stacking days," Nabers said, via Charlotte Carroll of TheAthletic.com. "Trying to get back out there with my teammates. If I can keep on stacking days with the training staff and they continue to see improvements with my body, continue to see improvements with my knee and where I'm at, it just gives me more confidence to go out there and play. . . . No target dates. Just continue to listen to the training staff and they continue to ask me questions. When I’m ready, I’m ready ." The start to camp has been encouraging for Nabers and an extended run without complications should have him on track to be catching passes from Jaxson Dart early in the regular season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Veteran DT Johnathan Hankins retires
summary: Veteran defensive tackle Johnathan Hankins has hung up his cleats.
full_text: ' Veteran defensive tackle Johnathan Hankins has hung up his cleats. Hankins, 34, told Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report that he is retiring after 12 seasons. Hankins did not play for the Seahawks last season, going on the non-football injury list after injuring his back in the 2025 offseason. The Seahawks released him from NFI on Dec. 3, and he has been a free agent since. He signed with Seattle in 2024 and appeared in all 17 games with eight starts. In what turned out to be his final season, Hankins recorded 30 tackles, with five tackles for loss, two quarterback hits and a sack. He also made the first interception of his career. A second-round pick of the Giants, he also played for the Colts, Raiders and Cowboys. Hankins appeared in 169 career games and was among the league’s premier run-stuffing interior defensive linemen, with 433 tackles, including 44 for loss.
author: Charean Williams

title: Nick Bosa suggests Joey Bosa won't play this season
summary: Defensive end Joey Bosa remains a free agent and apparently it's going to remain that way for the foreseeable future. 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa said May 28 that his older brother was "working on his golf game" and not thinking about football.
full_text: ' Defensive end Joey Bosa remains a free agent and apparently it's going to remain that way for the foreseeable future. 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa said May 28 that his older brother was " working on his golf game " and not thinking about football. That hasn't changed, Nick Bosa said on the Murph & Markus Show this week. "Joey might need to start training if that's going to be the case," Nick Bosa said, suggesting Joey Bosa was nine holes into his golf outing on Monday. Nick Bosa added, "No, probably not," when asked if news could be coming about Joey Bosa returning to the NFL. Joey Bosa, 31, has not had a double-digit sack season since 2021. The five-time Pro Bowler has only 19 across the past four seasons, including five in 2025 for the Bills. He was 35th on PFT's list of top-100 free agents this offseason. The only question left is: Is Joey Bosa retired or would he consider joining a contender late in the season or next season?
author: Charean Williams

title: UFL will relocate Houston, Birmingham franchises
summary: As expected, the UFL announced on Thursday that it will relocate the Stallions from Birmingham.
full_text: ' As expected, the UFL announced on Thursday that it will relocate the Stallions from Birmingham. As not expected, the UFL announced on Thursday it will relocate the Gamblers from Houston. "Two new replacement markets will be added for 2027, and the league plans to expand to 10 teams by 2028, including the addition of Oklahoma City," the UFL said in a press release. "The UFL has been actively evaluating markets across the country interested in bringing professional spring football to their city. The UFL has targeted a 12-team league by 2030, but with strong interest from prospective markets and league momentum that timeline may be accelerated to 2029." UFL co-owner Mike Repole attributed the decision to secure the future for the league. “My mission is to build a league that is not only sustainable today, but also successful and thriving for decades to come," Repole said. "Building a spring football league has required discipline and difficult decisions, which have been guided by our clear long-term vision. Every market evaluation begins with the same three principles I have said since day one — the right market, the right sized venue, and a passionate fan base.” He blamed the decision to leave Birmingham on the size of the venue; put simply, it was too big. Repole attributed the Houston decision to different factors. “Houston played an important role in reestablishing modern spring football, and we’re grateful to the fans, partners, and community who supported the Roughnecks and Gamblers," Repole said. "Houston is a great sports city, and Shell Energy Stadium has been an outstanding partner and venue. The reality is that we did not give this market the consistency it deserved. Between venue changes, team-name changes, and different approaches, we made it difficult to build lasting momentum.” Last year, the UFL moved three teams from old markets (Memphis, Michigan, and San Antonio) to new ones (Columbus, Louisville, Orlando). In 2027, the UFL will have two new markets.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rome Odunze clarifies "new normal" comment: "My foot feels amazing"
summary: Bears receiver Rome Odunze raised some concerns about his foot when he told reporters during the offseason program that his “new normal” is going to be dealing with some sort of discomfort.
full_text: Bears receiver Rome Odunze raised some concerns about his foot when he told reporters during the offseason program that his “ new normal ” is going to be dealing with some sort of discomfort. But on Thursday, Odunze clarified that’s not exactly how he’s feeling as he’s entering his third training camp. "I really didn’t articulate it well, honestly. That’s not really what I meant ,” Odunze said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "I just kind of meant that I had an injury. That’s it. That’s football. My foot feels great. My foot feels amazing. The training staff here, the training staffs I work with in the offseason, all the work that I’ve put in to get it right, honestly it’s not even really something that I think about anymore which I think is the best thing I think you can have after an injury. “I know ‘new normal,’ that has a bunch of connotations of chronic and severe, like it’s never going to be the same. It’s not like that at all. I’m completely fine. I went through my process of recovery and rehab, and it’s been great. Obviously I do my due diligence and all those things. Being out sucks. That really is the No. 1 thing as a football player, any athlete, you all know, you don’t want to be out — practice, game, whatever it is. Went through my process of getting that right, and I feel amazing.” That’s positive news for a Bears team that’s likely going to feature Odunze in a larger role in 2026 after trading DJ Moore to the Bills. After catching 54 passes for 734 yards with three touchdowns as a rookie, Odunze caught 44 passes for 661 yards with six TDs in 12 games last year.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: If Ricky Pearsall requires surgery, it will keep him out for all of 2026
summary: 49ers wide receiver Ricky Pearsall is out of practice due to swelling in his knee related to the PCL injury he suffered during the 2025 season and the 49ers said on Wednesday that they are considering all options to address the injury.
full_text: 49ers wide receiver Ricky Pearsall is out of practice due to swelling in his knee related to the PCL injury he suffered during the 2025 season and the 49ers said on Wednesday that they are considering all options to address the injury. One of those options would be a surgical procedure and going that route would reportedly lead to a long absence for the 2024 first-round pick. Matt Maiocco of NBCSportsBayArea.com said on KNBR that Pearsall will miss the entire season if the injury requires a surgical fix. Maiocco said that Pearsall and the 49ers "made a calculated attempt to hope that thing would heal on its own" this offseason, but the swelling after a few days of practice suggests that the injury did not heal as hoped. He also notes that Pearsall likely would have missed the season if he had surgery in March and that further time spent waiting to see if it heals on its own that still leads to surgery could impact Pearsall's availability and/or readiness for the 2027 campaign. None of that creates much confidence that Pearsall will be contributing to the 49ers this fall. It also makes the need for second-round pick De'Zhaun Stribling to contribute right out of the gate that much greater for the 49ers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks rookie DT Deven Eastern back on active roster
summary: The Seahawks activated rookie defensive tackle Deven Eastern from the active/physically unable to perform list on Thursday after he passed a physical, the team announced.
full_text: The Seahawks activated rookie defensive tackle Deven Eastern from the active/physically unable to perform list on Thursday after he passed a physical, the team announced. The Seahawks made Eastern a seventh-round pick out of the University of Minnesota, the 242nd overall choice. He missed much of the offseason program with an undisclosed injury. Eastern will compete for a roster spot at nose tackle, with Brandon Pili the only true nose tackle on the roster. Jarran Reed and Byron Murphy II also play the position. Defensive back Nick Emmanwori and running back Zach Charbonnet are the only players the Seahawks have left on PUP.
author: Charean Williams

title: Deebo Samuel reunites with 49ers amid injuries to wide receivers Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk
summary: Samuel spent the first six years of his career with the 49ers before playing for the Commanders last season
full_text:
Deebo Samuel and the 49ers are reuniting, with the do-it-all offensive weapon agreeing to a one-year, $7 million deal with a San Francisco team in need of wide receiver reinforcements, per ESPN/NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .
Samuel, 30, spent the first six years of his career with the 49ers, who selected him in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft . Samuel's outstanding ability with the ball in his hands came to a peak in 2021, when the South Carolina product had 1,405 receiving yards, 365 rushing yards and 14 total touchdowns, earning him All-Pro and Pro Bowl honors. Samuel was a key part of two NFC Championship-winning teams during his time in San Francisco.
Samuel spent last year with the Commanders , catching 72 passes -- his most since 2021 -- for 727 yards and five touchdowns. He led Washington in all three categories.
Samuel's return to the Bay Area comes as the 49ers are dealing with multiple injuries in their receiving corps. Ricky Pearsall , a 2024 first-round pick, is dealing with knee swelling related to the PCL injury he sustained last year. He has appeared in just 20 of a possible 32 regular-season games since joining the team. Christian Kirk , acquired this offseason, suffered a calf injury on the opening day of training camp.
That's left the 49ers with free-agent signing Mike Evans and second-round rookie De'Zhaun Stribling as the top wide receivers on the roster. Veteran Demarcus Robinson would likely be next in line.
Samuel is expected to slide into the "Z" receiver spot for the 49ers, per The Athletic's Matt Barrows , where he thrived during his time in San Francisco. Though Samuel won't handle as heavy a workload as he did during his prior stint with the team, he showed last year he can still bring value as a yards-after-catch receiver, and coach Kyle Shanahan has lined him up in the backfield plenty, too.
Samuel was the No. 53 free agent in this class according to Pete Prisco .
author: Zachary Pereles

title: 2026 NFL free agency tracker: Deebo Samuel to rejoin 49ers, seven of top 100 free agents still unsigned
summary: Several notable veterans remain on the market as the NFL offseason continues through the summer months
full_text:
NFL training camps are underway. The newcomers that arrived on their respective teams during the first major waves of free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft have settled into their new environments and will now spend the coming weeks gearing up for their debut seasons in new uniforms.
As teams introduce their rookies to the pros and weave in their veteran pickups, they also continue to look to improve on the periphery. Not every roster hole was filled in March and April, after all, and there is a notable advantage to signing free agents after the NFL Draft: They no longer count against the NFL's compensatory picks formula. That resulted in a slight uptick in the spring, but most of the post-draft signings will continue to trickle in this summer as still-unsigned vets start finding new homes during training camp.
Each of the top 36 players on Pete Prisco's annual free agent ranking has signed, but there is still plenty of quality talent available as the NFL calendar moves through its quietest months. Most recently, Deebo Samuel reportedly agreed on a one-year deal with the San Francisco 49ers worth up to $7 million.
Samuel's return to the Bay Area comes after two years with the Washington Commanders and takes him back to the place where he emerged as a star. With his addition, the 49ers add necessary weapons around quarterback Brock Purdy with Brandon Aiyuk all but certainly done and Ricky Pearsall experiencing lingering effects from last season's knee injury. The signing also leaves eight of the top 100 players still on the market.
We are keeping track of every top 100 signing below.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Saints reward Chris Olave for career year by making him one of NFL's highest-paid WRs
summary: Olave is signing a four-year extension worth up to $132 million after earning second-team All-Pro honors in 2025
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints closed the 2025 season with an up-and-coming offense and took a major step Thursday toward securing its young core for the long term. The team agreed to a four-year contract extension with wide receiver Chris Olave worth up to $132 million, his agents told ESPN . Olave's deal includes $90 million guaranteed.
The Saints already picked up the fifth-year option on Olave's rookie contract, so the new deal will take effect in 2027 and keep the former first-round pick in New Orleans through the 2030 season.
Since arriving in New Orleans as the No. 11 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft , Olave has done nothing but shine as the leader of the receiving corps. He topped 1,000 receiving yards in each of his three healthy seasons and was on pace to do so in 2024 before missing nine games because of multiple concussions.
Olave's injury history is effectively the only knock against him as a rising star. He suffered four concussions in his first four NFL seasons, raising concerns about his long-term future. The Saints appear willing to take on that risk, making him the sixth-highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL.
Olave's production remained consistent despite constant change on offense. In just four years with the franchise, he has played under three different offensive coordinators and two full-time head coaches while catching passes from a revolving door of quarterbacks that included Andy Dalton , Derek Carr , Jameis Winston , Spencer Rattler , Jake Haener and, most recently, Tyler Shough .
It was with Shough that Olave and the Saints built momentum at the end of the 2025 season. While it took a few weeks for everything to click, New Orleans won four of its final five games, and the Olave-Shough connection went wild in Weeks 16 and 17. The two connected 18 times over those games as Olave totaled 148 yards and two touchdowns against the New York Jets , then added 119 yards and another score against the Tennessee Titans .
By season's end, Olave had set career highs in receiving yards (1,163) and touchdowns (9). He also became just the second player in Saints history, joining Michael Thomas , to record at least 100 receptions in a season. The Ohio State product earned second-team All-Pro honors for his performance.
In addition to securing Olave's reliable presence in the receiving corps, the Saints signed free agent running back Travis Etienne earlier in the offseason to add another weapon to what is quickly becoming a promising offense. The pressure Etienne and Olave take off Shough's shoulders could help him make a leap as a second-year quarterback. If that happens, New Orleans should be in the mix for a division title in the wide-open NFC South.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Bengals training camp takeaways: Bold defensive gamble might pay off, Shemar Stewart avoids serious injury
summary: Plus, how getting run over by a truck gave one Bengals tight end a major confidence boost
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- The Bengals were one of the busiest teams in the NFL this offseason, especially when it came to adding players on the defensive side of the ball. Over the past three months, they made several key free-agent signings , adding players like Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook , while also pulling off a stunning trade to bring Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati.
The Bengals brought in reinforcements at almost every defensive position -- well, except one. The team didn't sign or draft any linebackers, which certainly raised some eyebrows around the NFL. Last season, the Bengals threw rookies Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight into the deep end, and in a sink-or-swim situation, they both sank. Both players struggled during their first year on the job, but instead of bringing in competition this year, the Bengals doubled down and made it clear that Carter and Knight would be their starting linebackers in 2026.
It's a bold gamble, but after two days of training camp, the early returns on Carter and Knight have been impressive. During the team's second practice Thursday, the two combined for one of the defensive highlights of the day: Knight picked off Burrow on a pass intended for Ja'Marr Chase .
Burrow was forced to throw after Carter blitzed him, and Knight made a diving play on the ball to come away with the interception.
Joe Burrow's first interception of the day: He's picked off by Demetrius Knight, who makes a pretty athletic play. That's definitely what the Bengals want to see from their 2nd year linebacker. #Bengals #Trainingcamp #NFL pic.twitter.com/C55lyIz0KB
"I saw Ja'Marr running the higher route, so I'm just playing underneath him," Knight said after practice. "Don't think [Burrow] saw me underneath, he just kind of saw the guy trailing Ja'Marr and kind of fell into that window. Right place at the right time."
It wasn't just the passing game, either. Knight also stormed into the backfield on several running plays.
Demetrius Knight Jr coming downhill, knifing through the OL and potentially making this TFL. Vid from @BengalScoutJoel pic.twitter.com/I4v9IVoFfP
On Carter's end, there was one play where he sniffed out a screen and likely would have leveled Chase Brown if the Bengals had been tackling Thursday.
Big day for Barrett Carter here he blows up a screen pass to Chase Brown pic.twitter.com/ryVfq2khkP
This is exactly what the Bengals wanted to see from the duo when they decided to hand them the starting jobs this year instead of bringing in competition.
In 2025, the Bengals defense gave up the most rushing yards in the NFL, the second-most total yards and the third-most points during an ugly season. The linebackers were a big part of the problem, but the coaching staff showed confidence in the unit by deciding to move forward with Knight and Carter as its main guys.
"That gives us a ton of confidence," Knight said of the team's decision not to add any linebackers. "Of course, we were prepared if they did bring one in. We weren't going to run from it. Barrett and I are competitors. We competed against each other in college. We competed together this past season, and we're competing together now."
The Bengals beefed up the defensive line with the additions of Lawrence, Mafe and Jonathan Allen , and the team's belief is those additions will have a trickle-down effect that helps the linebackers.
"Probably the best thing we did for our linebacker room is what we did for the D-line room, and that's going to elevate those guys," Bengals de facto general manager Duke Tobin said earlier this offseason . "I have real belief in the guys that we have. They have full seasons under their belt. They had really good production for rookies, and they're going to grow in our scheme, and they're going to be really good players. I think we have depth behind them."
Carter and Knight were ready to compete if the Bengals had brought in another linebacker, but in the end, the front office and coaching staff believed they had seen enough improvement over the course of the 2025 season to stick with the duo.
"We're all on the same train," Knight said. "There's no hard feelings. At the end of the day, we want to get back to SoFi [for Super Bowl LXI], so if that meant bringing in another backer, then that's what we got to do. Obviously, they didn't, which shows that they trust us, which only elevates our play, our attention to detail and focus, and only increases our leadership."
The linebacker unit is the biggest defensive question mark on the team right now, and after two days of practice, the early returns suggest the Bengals' defensive gamble might pay off. In Cincinnati, the offense is so good that if the defense can play even average football, the Bengals will be a Super Bowl contender. So far, the defense appears to be on its way to holding up its end of the bargain.
"We'll just continue to keep stacking each day, pushing each other, to push this defense, to push this team, to be great," Knight said.
The Bengals got a huge scare Wednesday when Shemar Stewart went down with what appeared to be a serious knee injury, but as it turns out, he might not miss any regular-season games. Bengals coach Zac Taylor revealed Thursday that the 2025 first-round pick suffered a hyperextended knee and will only be out for several weeks.
Shemar Stewart is NOT out for the season. He hyperextended his knee in practice in Wednesday and will be out for several weeks pic.twitter.com/qicMnoF7Uz
Taylor didn't put an exact timeline on Stewart's return, but the Bengals still have six weeks until their season opener against the Buccaneers . If "several weeks" is the timeline, there's certainly a chance Stewart will be on the field in Week 1.
The injury happened during an 11-on-11 drill Wednesday when Stewart's knee buckled underneath him while he was trying to rush Joe Flacco .
🎥 Video of Shemar Stewart’s injury: Fair warning… It’s not a fun watch 😕 #Bengals @WCPO pic.twitter.com/IPjcI2Qhlx
After Stewart was carted off the field, there was immediate concern he might miss a substantial amount of time, but that doesn't appear to be the case.
The Bengals have high hopes for Stewart, who's heading into his second season. As a rookie, he missed most of training camp because of a contract dispute. Although he eventually made it back to the field, he wasn't there for long. He injured his ankle in Week 2, causing him to miss four games, then missed another five games with a separate knee injury. He appeared in just eight games during his rookie campaign.
The Bengals drafted Stewart's former college teammate, Cashius Howell , in the second round this year, and the team hopes the duo can become a nightmare tandem on defense.
Stewart won't be back on the field anytime soon, but he was back in the locker room Thursday wearing a brace on his left leg.
When it comes to training camp battles, there isn't much to watch among the Bengals' offensive starters. The only real competition is at the No. 3 wide receiver spot. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the top two players on the depth chart, but the third receiver job isn't set in stone. Andrei Iosivas has basically spent his entire career battling to be the Bengals' No. 3 receiver, and he's in for another competition this year.
Iosivas has been in Cincinnati for three seasons, and although he was the No. 3 receiver last year, there's no guarantee he'll hold onto the spot this season. The Bengals used a fourth-round pick on former Georgia receiver Colbie Young , and they also have two more talented receivers on the roster in Mitchell Tinsley and Charlie Jones .
Based on what happened at Thursday's practice, this could turn into a tight competition. Iosivas made one of the best catches of the day with a tiptoe grab along the sideline that thrilled the thousands of fans in downtown Cincinnati.
Andrei Iosivas...sideline catch king. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/QgysUdnMHd
Not to be outdone, Young also made a nice catch during a 7-on-7 drill.
Seems like every…
author: John Breech

title: Deion Sanders makes surprise visit to Browns camp, here's what he discussed with Todd Monken
summary: Monken said the chat was mostly swapping stories with a little Browns talk about Shedeur sprinkled into his time with Deion
full_text:
Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders was quarterback Shedeur Sanders ' coach his entire life until the Cleveland Browns selected him in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft .
However, Deion still can't help but maintain the football connection he shared with his son for all those years, which is why he stopped by Cleveland's training camp on Thursday to chat with new Browns head coach Todd Monken. Deion said back in May on " Barbershop with Garrett Bush " that he wanted to tell Monken "a few things about how to get him [Shedeur] going." While some coaches may have found the chat overbearing, Monken loved his time with the elder Sanders.
"Forget that it was Shedeur's dad. First of all he did an unbelievable job with Shedeur, great kid. ... Obviously an elite football player [Deion]. Hell, baseball player. Then, as a coach and everything he has achieved. That was awesome," Monken said Thursday . We really almost didn't get into any football."
Monken, who coached college football for over a decade before getting his first taste of NFL coaching experience, said he and Deion swapped stories about their coaching and football careers before saying Deion "gave me a little bit of insight" into how Shedeur approaches processing at the quarterback position. Monken said he felt "we've been able to see" much of what Sanders was saying, and he told Deion "what a great job Shedeur has done since I've been here in terms of his development."
"It was good. Part-coach, part-father, which is what it should be," Monken said.
Now, it's up to Shedeur to earn first-team quarterback reps over Deshaun Watson in the Browns' training camp competition to be Cleveland's Week 1 starting quarterback to kick off the 2026 season.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Nic Scourton, Shemar Stewart, Chris Brazzell II and more
summary: Scourton and Brazzell are out for the season with knee injuries, while Stewart was carted off the practice field Wednesday
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski announced Wednesday that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve Friday after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
The former first-round pick is currently not practicing after experiencing swelling that is related to the PCL injury that he sustained last season. Pearsall is currently being evaluated by the team.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Cowboys sound open to (get this) extending a star player early: The price of keeping Quinnen Williams
summary: Stephen Jones said Williams is "at the top of the list" of players Dallas wants to keep, and the star DT says he'd "love to be here for the long haul"
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have their sights set on their next big contract extension target, and no, it's not franchise-tagged wide receiver George Pickens .
That would be four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . Dallas invested heavily to acquire Williams at the 2025 trade deadline, shipping the more favorable of its own or the Green Bay Packers ' 2027 first-round pick, a 2026 second-round pick and former first-round defensive tackle Mazi Smith to the New York Jets .
At 28, Williams is in the midst of his prime and fresh off a 2025 campaign in which he was one of only two defensive tackles to rank in the NFL's top 10 in both pass rush win rate and run stop win rate, along with Osa Odighizuwa , per ESPN.
He is under contract with Dallas through the 2027 season, but the Cowboys may want to extend him sooner rather than later after the defensive tackle market jumped this offseason. The Tennessee Titans extended All-Pro Jeffery Simmons on a three-year, $105.828 million contract ($35.276 million per year) at age 29, and the Philadelphia Eagles extended two-time Pro Bowler Jalen Carter on a four-year, $152 million deal ($38 million per year) at age 25.
That's why it may save the Cowboys money down the road if they opt to be proactive and get a deal done now. While that's typically not how they operate , they might treat Williams differently.
"We're very open to that," Cowboys COO Stephen Jones said Sunday at Dallas' opening training camp press conference . "We want Quinnen here for the long haul. Obviously, we've got a lot of resources tied up in him. He knows what we think about him, we've had some discussions with the agent about how to go about the process.
"Certainly he's one of the best in the business, and we know kind of what that market is. Obviously, it evolves and changes with each new deal, which is the case at any position. Certainly he's at the top of the list in terms of the people that we want to keep around here long term, and there's other players on the roster that we may take a look at as well."
It takes two to tango, but Williams said he "definitely would enjoy and love being here for the long haul" when asked this week about signing an extension with the Cowboys.
"For sure, man," Williams said Wednesday . "Especially being here with these guys, man. You've got a phenomenal group, a phenomenal staff, organization-wise, it's unbelievable. And then having guys that you can call and lean on, like DeMarcus Ware is one of my guys, it's unbelievable, man.
"Like I said, I'm not focused on no contract, I definitely want to be here for the long haul, I definitely would enjoy and love being here for the long haul, but I want to win, and that's kind of the only thing I'm really focused on."
Dallas positioned Williams as the new All-Pro heart of its defense after trading edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Packers a week before the 2025 season began, and that belief is one of the driving reasons Williams is so open to remaining a Cowboy.
"When somebody believes in you, to know that, 'Okay, you're one of the guys I feel like can help us win and help us achieve the goal that we always want to achieve.' So as soon as I got traded, I wanted to be here, I wanted to be here for the long haul," Williams said. "I didn't want to just come and play around, I want to be here and win, I want to win for the organization."
However, he's well aware that the defensive tackle market continues to rise. Williams said he and three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark were joking about how the market has evolved. They recalled the days when Fletcher Cox and Aaron Donald were among the NFL's highest-paid defensive tackles, and now Carter ($38 million per year) and Simmons ($35.276 million per year) have nearly doubled those salaries on their new deals.
Carter is also one of the players Williams has studied this offseason since new Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker arrived after spending the past two seasons with the Eagles as their defensive backs/defensive passing game coordinator.
"He's well deserving of every penny he's got and earned," Williams said of Carter. "It's fantastic watching him on film, trying to see what I can take from his game and put in the same scheme that we're kind of running right now.
"It's just phenomenal to see the impact that my position, defensive tackle, is making. You always see the teams that are in the Super Bowl have D-tackles with Seattle [Byron Murphy and Leonard Williams ], the Eagles [Carter and Jordan Davis ] and Kansas City [ Chris Jones ] in a few years. Those guys have been very effective and things like that. That's all I focus on, just focus on bringing an impact to this team, bringing an impact to this defense and trying to get this team going in the right direction so another D-tackle will be in the Super Bowl."
After the Cowboys defense ranked last in the NFL in scoring defense in 2025 -- allowing 30.1 points per game in one season under now-fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus -- Williams' focus is mastering Parker's new scheme. He aims to help his side of the ball play closer to the level of Dallas' offense, which averaged the NFL's seventh-most points per game (27.7) last season.
"I want to win for not only me, myself personally, but guys like Dak Prescott who works his tail off and has been here 10 years and deserves a Super Bowl," Williams said. "And guys like CeeDee [Lamb], who's a five-time Pro Bowler and been here for five years, and who deserves a Super Bowl. You just see those things like that, and you just see how great they were last year, and the defense wasn't so great. It just urges me, personally, to get this defense together so the hard work that they put in won't just be going to waste anymore."
So where do things stand between Williams and the Jones family regarding a potential extension? The 2022 first-team All-Pro defensive tackle is taking a page from Prescott's playbook and letting his agent handle the negotiations.
"I truly don't know," Williams said. "I'm just truly enjoying being here, I'm enjoying being on the Dallas Cowboys. First training camp, first time in Oxnard, first time kind of being in a sense where we can get better and trying to get better on defense, especially with the new guys coming in, with the new staff coming in. Just focusing on getting this going in the right direction."
If Stephen Jones meant what he said about being willing to do a deal during training camp, it would likely be three years in length, with the 28-year-old still having two seasons remaining on the four-year, $96 million contract he signed in 2023. The deal could be worth $115.5 million over three years for an average annual salary of $38.5 million, putting Williams atop the defensive tackle market.
If the Cowboys opt to slow-play the market, they could get burned with two-time Pro Bowler Vita Vea , three-time Pro Bowler Leonard Williams, Pro Bowler Daron Payne and three-time Pro Bowler DeForest Buckner all set to hit free agency next offseason. Williams could then become the first defensive tackle to earn $40 million per year.
It may be time for those in Dallas to buckle up because the Jones family is once again primed to enter its least favorite arena: the negotiating table with its star players' agents.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Baker Mayfield feels 'disrespected' by lack of contract extension ahead of training camp
summary: Mayfield set a deadline for contract talks, and it came and went without a deal being reached
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield set a deadline for contract extension talks with the team, and that deadline -- the start of training camp -- has now come and gone without Mayfield getting a new contract. Speaking at camp on Thursday, Mayfield emphasized that his contract talks are now over and expressed his disappointment with the lack of a deal and the quality of the offers he received from the team.
"Disappointing in that regard to feel disrespected a little bit," Mayfield said, per Pewter Report . "That's really the disappointing part of it is feeling undervalued after thinking you've earned it. This is not a 'poor me' thing. There's a lot other people that have it way worse off, but I can sit here and look at other quarterbacks and peers and evaluate myself based on that and put myself in certain categories that I deserve to be compensated for that. I think I'm a franchise quarterback, I've been told I'm a franchise quarterback. It's been said publicly from ownership down here and so to not have a deal done is very disappointing."
There appears to have been a significant gap between the valuation Mayfield expected and what the Bucs were willing to offer, both in the length of the contract extension and the dollar amount. Mayfield told ESPN that the Bucs offered him a two-year deal that was "pretty far" from putting him in the $50 million-per-year club, which is where he wanted to be.
Most "franchise quarterbacks" sign deals lasting at least four years. The shorter-term contracts are typically meant for bridge quarterbacks or those who still need to prove themselves. Surefire starter types have also generally signed for at least $40 million and most times $50 million per year, while those that are bridge starters or prove-it guys sign in the $20 million to $35 million range, which is where Mayfield resides right now.
Baker Mayfield didn't get a new contract with the Bucs this offseason ... So @PriscoCBS handed him a taped up $20 bill and got the details of what really happened. pic.twitter.com/BU7ibM89JE
There are currently 12 quarterbacks making at least $50 million per year: Patrick Mahomes , Dak Prescott , Joe Burrow , Matthew Stafford , Trevor Lawrence , Jordan Love , Josh Allen , Brock Purdy , Jared Goff , Justin Herbert , Lamar Jackson and Jalen Hurts . All of them, except for Stafford, are on contracts that were at least 4 years long when they were signed.
If Mayfield feels that he's a franchise quarterback and the Bucs weren't prepared to pay him like one, it's not surprising that a deal wasn't reached before his self-imposed deadline of the start of training camp.
"It feels like I'm having to prove my worth yet again ... the disappointing part is I feel like I've earned that contract." Baker Mayfield explains to our @PriscoCBS what his mentality is right now during his contract impasse with the Bucs. pic.twitter.com/dT39wotvdM
This is a tougher question.
Mayfield has been in Tampa for three seasons, completing 66.3% of his passes at an average of 7.3 yards per attempt, with 95 touchdowns and 37 interceptions. He's gone 27-24 as a starter and made the Pro Bowl in two of his three seasons.
His 2024 campaign, though, looks like a bit of an outlier compared with the other two. Under former offensive coordinator Liam Coen (now head coach of the Jacksonville Jaguars ), Mayfield completed 71.4% of his passes at an average of 7.9 yards per attempt, with 41 touchdowns and 16 interceptions. In his other two seasons, he has completed 64.3% and 63.2% of his passes, averaged 7.1 and 6.8 yards per attempt, and combined for 54 touchdowns and 21 picks.
In other words, Mayfield has had one season where he looked like a surefire franchise quarterback, sandwiched by two seasons where he looked more like a bridge starter type who is worth a sizable contract but not necessarily one that pays him at or near the top of the market. He's also 31 years old and coming off a season marred by injuries, and he's on a team that doesn't look like a near-term contender, which makes a deal at the level he's pursuing pretty unlikely.
Taking Mayfield at his word, contract talks with the Bucs are over, and he will play out the season on the final season of his three-year, $100 million contract. That deal pays him a base salary of just $10 million for the 2026 season, but he has a roster bonus of $17 million and another bonus worth $1 million, while his prorated signing bonus counts on the books for $11.975 million, so he carries a cap hit of $39.975 million for this year.
Mayfield will be counting on a better season under new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson , under whom he played during his short stint with the Rams back in 2022. (Robinson was the passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach under Sean McVay and offensive coordinator Liam Coen.) Trying to recapture some of the magic that Mayfield had during the 2024 campaign makes sense, though it remains to be seen whether the Bucs can do so.
If Mayfield has a season like that, he's going to hit that magic $50 million per year mark, whether he gets such a deal from the Bucs or some other team. However, if he still can't come to an agreement with Tampa after a season like that, it would be shocking if the Bucs didn't use the franchise tag to retain him.
If Mayfield has another season like last year or the one he had in 2023, though, things could get more interesting. The Bucs could try to bring him back on another contract like the one they're offering now, or move on and look for a long-term answer in the draft or on the free-agent market. Mayfield would then potentially be looking at a deal like the one Sam Darnold signed with the Seahawks last offseason, or perhaps like the one Daniel Jones got with the Colts this year.
