title: Tyler Bass injury: Bills kicker good to go in 2026 training camp
summary: A season removed from an injury that cost him all of the 2025 NFL season, Buffalo Bills place kicker Tyler Bass is ready to go for training camp. If the Bills are going to reach their loftiest goals this season, they’ll need Bass to help them get through the difficult moments. Many have wondered what’s […]
full_text: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: Tyler Bass #16 kicks a field goal from Mitch Wishnowsky #19 of the Buffalo Bills during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images A season removed from an injury that cost him all of the 2025 NFL season, Buffalo Bills place kicker Tyler Bass is ready to go for training camp. If the Bills are going to reach their loftiest goals this season, they’ll need Bass to help them get through the difficult moments. Many have wondered what’s going on with Bass since he was shelved with a pelvic injury and replaced by steely veteran kicker Matt Prater days before the first game of last season. It’s fair to say it’s been a long road for Tyler Bass, who spoke with reporters during Thursday’s practice . Bass noted that he’s in a good place, and excited to return to action as the only kicker on the team’s current roster, stating “we’re ready to go, we’ve worked really hard, and we’re excited to be here.” When asked about the struggles from last season, Bass didn’t hold back, saying “it was tough, it was tough. A situation I’ve never been in, being injured. But, again, really grateful for how they kinda handled it and I’m grateful for, honestly, Prater coming — and he did a great job, and I learned a lot from just being around him.” In recalling that his eventual season-ending injury reared its head during Buffalo’s final preseason game last summer, Bass stated that “I think we were just still battling through it. I was still kind of hurting in that game and it just never was gonna get better, and we just decided it was time to get it fixed and go from there. Bass did admit it was a huge challenge to overcome when the time came to shut things down and properly take care of the injury. “I wouldn’t say it was a relief, but you know I finally had an answer to the problem,” Bass stated. “It was gonna be yard, I knew it was gonna be hard, the recovery. It was hard to get out of bed for a couple of weeks. But once I got through that, you know, show myself and my body that I can kinda do anything.” As for when Bass was finally able to confidently kick as expected, he said that “it probably took a few months, when I started kicking. But, you know, we started with baby steps, you know like 20-yarders, 10-yarders; kinda worked from there. And then it wasn’t really until like OTAs — like midway through OTAs — where I started really feeling kinda like myself again.” Now back in the fold and ready to kick in 2026, Bass brings with him a new number after relinquishing his “2” jersey to wide receiver DJ Moore. When asked why he chose “16,” Bass exclaimed “college number, I’m really excited; a lot of good memories with it.” Tyler Bass says it was hard to even get out of bed for weeks while recovering from a pelvic injury that cost him all of last season. His road back started with just 10 yard field goals. Now the #Bills kicker says he's ready to go… with a new number. pic.twitter.com/ssCzKlfYn3 — Jon Scott (@JonScottTV) July 30, 2026

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting reports: CB Davison Igbinosun
summary: The Buffalo Bills came into the 2026 offseason with plenty of needs. That’s not necessarily surprising given the fickle nature of the NFL, but for a team that has qualified for the playoffs in each of the last seven seasons, the list of needs seemed to be larger than one would expect. After head coach […]
full_text: MADISON, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Davison Igbinosun #1 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the game against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium on October 18, 2025 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills came into the 2026 offseason with plenty of needs. That’s not necessarily surprising given the fickle nature of the NFL, but for a team that has qualified for the playoffs in each of the last seven seasons, the list of needs seemed to be larger than one would expect. After head coach Sean McDermott was fired, that list of needs grew to include defensive players who could fit a new defensive system, as well. One of the positions where the team seemed fairly solid on the surface was cornerback; however, a look beyond that top layer of the depth chart showed a troublesome lack of depth. That lack of depth reared its head at the worst possible time for Buffalo last season, and as a result, the Bills and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane made sure to bolster the defensive secondary this spring. In today’s installment of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss one of the additions to the depth chart at corner — a rookie with great size and tremendous potential. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Davison Igbinosun Number: 21 Position: CB Height/Weight: 6’2”, 193 pounds Age: 22 (23 on 4/11/2027) Experience/Draft: R; selected by Buffalo in the second round (No. 62 overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft College: Ohio State Acquired: Second-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): Igbinosun enters the first year of his rookie contract, a four-year pact worth $7,949,010 overall. For the 2026 season, Igbinosun’s cap hit is $1,445,274 if he makes the 53-man roster. If he’s released, Buffalo will carry a dead-cap charge of $5,738,907 for the season. 2025 Recap: Igbinosun was once again a key contributor to a top-flight Buckeyes defense. He started all 14 games, notching 53 tackles, half a tackle for loss, eight pass breakups, and two interceptions. For his efforts, he was named First-Team All-Big Ten Conference for the first time ; he was honorable mention in both the 2023 and 2024 seasons. Igbinosun’s play on the field had already made him a solid NFL prospect, but his performance at the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine and Ohio State’s Pro Day solidified that notion. At the combine, he ran a 4.45-second 40-yard dash, and he leapt 34” in the vertical jump and 10’ in the broad jump. At Ohio State’s Pro Day, he leapt 35” in the vertical jump and 10’4” in the broad jump; he also ran the 20-yard shuttle in 4.32 seconds and completed the three-cone drill in 7.07 seconds. He did not complete the bench press at either workout. Positional outlook: Igbinosun is one of five players listed at cornerback on the current roster. Dee Alford, Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston, and Toriano Pride Jr. are the others. Te’Cory Couch, Kani Walker, Jordan Dunbar, and Jordan Hancock are all listed at defensive back, but they each either play corner or bounce between playing corner and safety. 2026 Offseason: Igbinosun is healthy and he participated in all offseason workouts. 2026 Season outlook: Buffalo has repeatedly said that Igbinosun was drafted not due to a lack of satisfaction with last year’s top draft choice, Maxwell Hairston, but instead due to an overall need for more depth at the position. Looking at the selection through that lens, well, it would be nice to have someone to turn to other than Dane Jackson in the fourth quarter of a playoff game. However, it’s hard not to wonder whether Igbinosun has a legitimate chance at earning starter’s reps given that we’re looking at a new defensive system coached by a new person in defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. Does this mean that I expect Igbinosun to come in and usurp Hairston right away? No, it doesn’t, and I’ll go one step further in saying that Hairston is a clear-cut starter on this defense. In limited action last season, he was fantastic. His injuries were both of the flukey variety, as a buckled knee during training camp caused him to miss time before his season ended prematurely thanks to someone rolling up on his ankle at the end of a running play in the regular-season finale. In between, Hairston put together some good reps in both the run game and the passing game, and he showed me enough that he deserves to come into this season as a starter. Could Igbinosun push for playing time? Perhaps in the future or as an injury replacement, but he’ll have to fix one thing first: penalties. In college, he was flagged an absurd 30 times , which reminds me of another former high draft choice at corner in Kaiir Elam. I’m not saying Igbinosun and Elam are destined for similar fates, nor am I saying that they’re similar athletes. What is similar, though, is their tendency to grab when plays go south, a tendency that could lead to devastating consequences in the NFL. Igbinosun is a lock for the roster, and his likely best role in 2026 is as a sub-package player or an injury replacement as he learns the ropes. If he can remove that “grabby” tendency from his game, he has a chance to be an outstanding pro corner. As the old adage goes, “You can never have enough corners.” Over the last few years, Buffalo has learned the hard way just how true that is.

summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: 2003 September 07 | Sunday: Stephen Davis (48) Running Back Carolina Panthers rushes the football against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Ericsson Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Allio/Icon Sportswire) (Photo by David Allio/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #44. Stephen Davis Running back is probably the most well represented position on this list except for maybe linebacker. Today’s running back of note is Stephen Davis, the first ever Carolina Panthers running back to start in a Super Bowl. Davis, a native of Spartanburg, South Carolina, entered the NFL as a fourth round pick by Washington. He played as a fullback and backup running back for the first three years of his career before getting a chance at the lead back role in 1999. He took the position and ran with it, literally. He rushed for over 1,400 yards and scored a league high 17 touchdowns. He followed that with two more stellar seasons before injury troubles messed up his 2002 season. Following that 2002 season, Davis signed with the Panthers to be the team’s starting running back ahead of DeShaun Foster, who was coming off a season ending injury prior to his rookie season. He was able to rediscover the magic that he found in Washington, rushing for 1,444 yards and eight touchdowns as the Panthers made an improbable run to the Super Bowl. He ran for 315 yards during the playoff run, though just 49 came in the Super Bowl as the Panthers went to the air in a game that got wildly out of control. Unfortunately, Davis would end up being a one hit wonder of sorts for the Panthers. Injuries robbed him of all but two games in his second season in Carolina, and he struggled to bounce back for his third. He started ceding work to Foster as he limped to just 3.1 yards per carry in his third and final season in Carolina. Davis spent one last season with the Rams before hanging up the cleats. When that time came, he signed a one day contract to retire as a Panther. Davis only had one standout season in Carolina, but it feels like more than that given the timing. He was a central figure in the Cardiac Cats’ run to the Super Bowl, and that run perfectly coincided with his arrival. While it’s a shame that we didn’t get to see more of Davis at his best, we at least got that one season. And that’s enough to earn him spot number 44 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 45 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA - JANUARY 18: Head coach John Fox of the Carolina Panthers celebrates with Panthers' defensive end Julius Peppers #90 as he cheers his team on in the forth quarter during the NFC Championship game against the Philadelphia Eagles on January 18, 2004 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Panthers won the game 14-3, advancing them to the Super Bowl. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #45. John Fox John Fox’s first ever coaching position was as a 23-year-old graduate assistant at San Diego State University in 1978. He then spent several years as a defensive backs coach at the collegiate level before becoming the Defensive Coordinator for the Pitt Panthers for three seasons. Staying in Pittsburgh, Fox transitioned from college to the NFL, joining the Steelers staff as defensive backs coach in 1989. After three years with the Steelers and two with the Chargers, Foxy got his first big break as an NFL Defensive Coordinator with the Raiders. He spent a couple seasons between LA and Oakland, then spent one season as a consultant for the Rams. He spent the next five seasons as the Defensive Coordinator for the New York Giants. The Panthers had just finished their worst season in franchise history (by a wide margin) in 2001. The team went 1-15 and had abysmal performances on both sides of the ball (29th in points for, 28th in points against). The season started off with a bang as future Hall of Honor member Steve Smith began his rookie campaign with a kickoff return touchdown, helping lift the team to a win over the Minnesota Vikings. From there, however, the wheels fell off. Offensive minded coach George Seifert was fired, essentially freeing up both the head coach position and general manager position. Marty Hurney, No. 82 on our list, was hired as GM, and Giants DC John Fox was hired as head coach. The defensive turnaround was instant. While the offense still sputtered, the defense jumped up to 5th in the league in points against. The team finished 7-9 on the back of that stout defense. Some free agent acquisitions and young player development on offense helped the team really flourish during the 2003 season. With the offense still struggling throughout the first half of the their Week 1 matchup against the Jaguars, Fox made the gutsy decision to pull starter Rodney Peete in favor of some guy named Jake Delhomme. That no-name backup quarterback led a comeback victory, and the Panthers rattled off an impressive 11-5 season that culminated in the franchise’s first trip to the Super Bowl. The offense was still very much an average unit (literally 15th in points for), so it was Fox’s defense that really drove the team’s success. John Fox’s tenure in Carolina ultimately lasted nine seasons, though none ever reached the success of his second season. The 2005 and 2008 seasons were both promising, but neither led to a Super Bowl birth. The 2-14 season in 2010 was the nail in the coffin for Fox, ending his career in Carolina. He ended up with a 73-71 record, boasting multiple defenses that landed in the top ten of the league in both points allowed and yards allowed. In fact, the 2002 and 2005 defenses finished top five in both categories. Fox went on to be the head coach for the Denver Broncos before ending his career as the Bears head coach in 2017 (though he has had some consultant/assistant gigs since then). While the end of Foxy’s tenure was stale and underwhelming, he undoubtedly had a massive impact on the franchise. He was brought in to fix the defense and did so with incredible success, earning him this spot on our countdown.

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Austin Booker #94 and Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears tackle Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers during the first half of an NFL wild card football game at Solider Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. Free article on The Atheletic. title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: Darnell Wright’s potential contract extension
summary: A lot of Bears fans are curious about Darnell Wright and other Chicago Bears players in terms of their future with the team and what type of contract extension they could receive. We are going to do a series over the next week or so: Cash, Stash, or Slash. It’s going to look at a […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - JANUARY 5: Offensive tackle Darnell Wright #58 of the Chicago Bears blocks during an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers, at Lambeau Field on January 5, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images A lot of Bears fans are curious about Darnell Wright and other Chicago Bears players in terms of their future with the team and what type of contract extension they could receive. We are going to do a series over the next week or so: Cash, Stash, or Slash. It’s going to look at a handful of Chicago Bears and whether they should receive an extension (Cash), whether the Bears should “wait and see” (Stash), or whether the Bears should go in a new direction (Slash). Also, an important note: this isn’t if the Bears should make a decision on these players right now (although some may think that’s the case), but it’s if these players should receive an extension in the next 13 months, before the start of the 2027 NFL season. It makes sense to start with Darnell Wright, who was discussed by Ryan Poles at his opening press conference at training camp. Poles mentioned Wright was a guy that the Bears wanted to keep around and be a part of this team for many years. Let’s start with the verdict on this one as it’s obvious and then go into the details. Darnell Wright: Cash Of course, Darnell Wright should receive an extension, and he should receive one in the next 40 days. The question with Wright isn’t a question of if; it’s a question of how much, so let’s take a look at that and try to figure out what type of offer Wright should receive. When Poles talked about Wright’s extension to the media, he talked about how it takes two to negotiate, which makes you think that right now, Wright’s camp and the Bears are fairly far off on numbers, and they aren’t actively talking about finding common ground. I hear a lot of Bears fans talk about how this is a negotiation and if both sides aren’t disappointed after a negotiation, then it wasn’t done well. This isn’t Wall Street; this is the NFL. That’s not how negotiations work. Players want salaries that show the team respects them and that they get the respect they’ve earned across the league. Yes, players will sign team-friendly deals, and I am certainly not saying the Bears should overpay all their players, but they should absolutely give them a fair-market offer. Low-balling players is how you get a reputation around the league, and that’s not how you convince future free agents to sign here. Now, I am not saying that Poles has low-balled Wright; I have no inside information as to how those negotiations have gone, or if they have gone at all. It also should be noted that Poles has done a good job getting pretty team-friendly deals with a lot of the players he has signed, so let’s look at what’s fair for Wright. Wright has been on the team for three seasons and has shown steady improvement in each of his seasons. He is still being penalized too frequently, but beyond that, he has shown dynamic skills in both the run and pass games. He’s a pure mountain of strength but has quick enough feet to keep most edges at bay in the pass rush as well. Wright’s skills earned him 2nd-team All-Pro this past season at the right tackle position. No shame in being second in the league when Penei Sewell earned first-team honors, arguably the best offensive lineman at any position in the entire NFL. Sewell is moving to left tackle this season, which, theoretically, makes Wright the best RT in the NFL. If he has another season like he did last year, he will certainly make that claim five months from now. So where should the Bears be considering Wright’s deal? Let’s look at recent RT deals, and we should look no further than Sewell. Sewell received his contract extension from the Lions before the 2024 season. It was a 4-year deal worth $112 million with an average value of $ 28 million per season. At the time of the extension, Sewell was a more decorated player with two Pro Bowls and one first-team All-Pro. The cap has risen 18% in the last two seasons, so if Sewell’s contract was signed today with the same percentage of cap designated to him, his AAV would be $33 million per season. I think if we look at the other highest-paid RTs, other than Sewell, we find those contracts settling in around $24 or $25 million a year. Wright is clearly better than those other right tackles (other than Lane Johnson, but he’s 36 years old and winding down his career in the next year or two. I’m sure Wright’s team wants him to be paid at the top of the market. If we use the Sewell deal to convert his contract to $33 million in 2026 dollars, I think Wright making about $30 million is quite fair, putting him at 4 years and $120 million. If the Bears can negotiate a more team-friendly deal with the argument that Sewell is at $28 million and, despite the rising cap, we can’t pay you more than Sewell, you still, to be fair to Wright, need to make sure he clears the other RTs in the league. In this case, you would be looking at $26 to $27 million per season. The fair offer for Wright is a 4-year deal with the total contract being valued somewhere between $104 and $120 million. Sewell got $43 million fully guaranteed and about $85 million in total guarantees. I think that’s also the framework for Wright’s deal. Wright is looking at a contract with $40 to $50 million fully guaranteed and somewhere between $80 and $90 million in total guarantees. The Bears are going to be giving out two major 9-figure contracts in the next 12 months that are going to be upwards of $350 to $400 million. That’s some big spending for George McCaskey; hopefully he doesn’t blink. I’d be stunned if Wright can’t get an extension with the Bears before the season begins, and I think when it happens, you’ll see the numbers fall in the ranges listed above.

title: Chicago Bears 2026 Training Camp Position Breakdown: Tight end
summary: Are you sick of hearing about 13 personnel yet? Shortly after the Chicago Bears drafted Sam Roush in the third round (69 overall), analysts started discussing how he’d be deployed with Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland. Playing three tight ends is a trend that more teams started doing last year, but you really need a […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 28: Colston Loveland #84 of the Chicago Bears gets set during the second half of an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Are you sick of hearing about 13 personnel yet? Shortly after the Chicago Bears drafted Sam Roush in the third round (69 overall), analysts started discussing how he’d be deployed with Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland. Playing three tight ends is a trend that more teams started doing last year, but you really need a unicorn at the position to take advantage of possible mismatches that are created, so not every team is equipped to run 13 effectively. The Bears are. Roster Locks Loveland’s blocking was the most underrated part of his game coming out of Michigan, but it’s the first thing I noticed in the regular season. In his first four games, he had only 5 receptions for 54 yards, so much of his film was as a blocker, and while his technique had some inconsistent moments, his effort was always there. As he proved he could block in Ben Johnson’s offense, the rock started to come his way more and more. Running 13 personnel with Loveland will allow the Bears to be right, no matter how the defense counters. As a receiver, the 6’6″, 241-pounder is too big for most defensive backs to match up with, and he’s too good a route runner for most linebackers to cover. In a recent article by Dwain McFarland of Matthew Berry’s Fantasy Life, Loveland is ranked in their tier 2 of tight ends, only behind Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders and Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals. “He brings a rare combo of target-earning and vertical usage, the same traits that have driven ceiling seasons from Rob Gronkowski, Jimmy Graham, and Mark Andrews,” McFarland writes about Loveland’s 2026 projection. To highlight the “vertical usage,” Loveland’s aDOT (average depth of target when targeted) was tied for 4th-best among all tight ends last season at 9.0, but in his two playoff games, it increased to 12.5. But there’s more to his fantasy projection than aDOT. McFarland continued, “Ben Johnson leaned into TE-friendly personnel last season, using 12 personnel on 33% of plays (5th) and 13 personnel at 9% (5th)—both strong signals for TE route volume and production. Johnson also creates high-efficiency looks for his pass catchers. Chicago ranked 6th in play action (33%) and 6th in motion at the snap (59%), two areas that consistently boost TE efficiency.” But staying on the aDOT theme, guess who was just two tight ends away from Loveland in that category? Yep, Chicago’s other tight end, Cole Kmet. He wasn’t just sneaking out into the flat in 2025, because his aDOT was 8.8. He may never approach the career highs of 73 receptions and 719 yards he had in 2023, but he’s still a top 32 player at the position. Roush will need to acclimate to the pro game, but Lance Zierlein of NFL.com called him a “plug-and-play” Y (in-line) tight end. He’s going to play more than last year’s TE3, so expect Chicago’s 13 usage to be more than just 9% of the time. A Good Bet To Make It The Bears only carried three tight ends last year, but I think UDFA Hayden Large has a good chance to make it. He’s a tenacious blocker, he lined up at fullback for Iowa, and he had plenty of special teams experience with the Hawkeyes as well. If the Bears plan to play more 13, it makes sense to have a fourth on the 53-man roster. Roster Bubble/Practice Squad The Bears had three tight ends on their practice squad most of last season, and Nikola Kalinic, Stephen Carlson, and Qadir Ismail all return to try and make it again. Kalanic and Carlson were both elevated for two games each last season, but Ismail ended the year on injured reserve for the Bears. Of the three, Ismail, a former wide receiver, is the only one who has the athleticism to line up as a move tight end. What are your expectations for Loveland? Do you think the Bears carry a fourth tight end this season? Sound off in the comment section! Join the conversation! title: Battle of the Hawgs – Preview for the Chicago Bears’ Training Camp Battle at Center
summary: As we’ve finally made it to Training Camp for the Chicago Bears, and there shall be a slew of competitions at multiple positions across the roster. Most recently, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed there will be such a contest for the starting job at Center. The two contestants are veteran Garrett Bradbury and rookie Logan […]
full_text: LAKE FOREST, ILLINOIS - JULY 29: Logan Jones #54 of the Chicago Bears looks on during Chicago Bears Training Camp at Halas Hall on July 29, 2026 in Lake Forest, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we’ve finally made it to Training Camp for the Chicago Bears, and there shall be a slew of competitions at multiple positions across the roster. Most recently, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed there will be such a contest for the starting job at Center. The two contestants are veteran Garrett Bradbury and rookie Logan Jones. Regardless of who ultimately wins the job this season, all signs point to Logan Jones becoming *the* guy at Center for 2027 and beyond. That being said, the youngster from Iowa will have his chance to unseat the veteran in Bradbury, who was acquired this offseason via trade from the New England Patriots. I firmly believe this is the most underrated competition to watch at Halas Hall this year. In the Blue Corner at 6ft 3in and 305 pounds – #67 Garrett Bradbury Age: 31 Exp: 8 seasons Previous team(s): NC State Wolfpack; Minnesota Vikings; New England Patriots The former 18th overall pick of the 2019 NFL Draft has started in all 105 career games he dressed for between the Vikings and the Patriots. Just coming off a Super Bowl run with the Patriots he was also in a similar situation when they selected current starter Jared Wilson with the 95th overall pick and played him at guard during his rookie season. While there was no competition during training camp in Foxborough, he cemented himself as a key cog for an efficient group which spearheaded one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Nothing spectacular, just solid. And solid is all the Bears need at Center for the time being. Naturally, the Bears didn’t plan for this transition to happen so soon in the first place. Pro Bowler Drew Dalman was just 27 years old and coming off his best season of his career before abruptly retiring in the spring. This caused Ben Johnson and Ryan Poles to scramble for both an immediate and long-term solution to their center position on relatively short notice. Ultimately, they pivoted towards a trade that landed Garrett Bradbury. He now reunites with a former NC State teammate in All-Pro Guard and reigning Protector of the Year Joe Thuney as well. What I will point out is that offensive line coach Dan Roushar has only seen one rookie in his career take the mantle as his team’s starting center – Erik McCoy in 2019. Then again, Garrett Bradbury himself started in every game as a rookie too. The center position is by far the most difficult to learn as you have to master both calling protections and your techniques between snapping the ball and identifying the first threat from inside. A team pursuing their own run at the Super Bowl, like the Bears, may not have the appetite for a learning curve at center. Not all rookies are the same. In the Orange Corner at 6ft 3in and 299 pounds – #54 Logan Jones Age: 24 Exp: None (rookie) Previous Team(s): Iowa Hawkeyes Here we have the young challenger to the Bears’ job at Center. While he doesn’t have any experience as a pro just yet, there is a ton of buzz surrounding this latest selection from the OL factory known as Iowa Hawkeye brand football. And it’s not just because the jersey number (54) has returned to the Bears’ lineup. The Bears picked him as the first center to hear their name called during the 2026 NFL Draft at selection number 57 overall. A spot that has seen great history for the Bears from previous draft classes, including one Devin Hester. The Heinz 57 sponsored product brings with him an excellent set of physical tools anchored by sound technique and a keen awareness for how protections are set. He was named the recipient of the 2025 Rimington Trophy as the nation’s top ranked center in NCAA football as well. A player most frequently brought up as a pro comparison for Logan Jones – Drew Dalman. Their physicality and athleticism from the center position are reminiscent to each other, where you can see both players pulling naturally when called upon in protection or road paving. The Bears had Logan Jones as their top choice at Center from the start of the process and pounced on him when he was still there in the second round. There have not been a ton of rookies to start and finish a full season at center for the Bears in recent history. The last such occurrence was in 2016 when Cody Whitehair was kicked inside shortly after the surprise signing of All-Pro Guard Josh Sitton. Even Olin Kruetz himself started just one game during his rookie season. Yet I’d argue the Bears haven’t drafted a pure center who’s nearly as good as Logan Jones is in quite some time. From the moment his name was called there always was a chance for him to compete for a starting job this year instead of waiting until Garrett Bradbury’s eventual departure. When the pads come on starting next Monday, his opportunities will open up. I’d expect this competition to last all the way until the second preseason game. Match-up between both players Size: Tie Even though Garrett Bradbury is listed as a few pounds heavier, their wingspans are almost identical, with Garrett Bradbury being measured at 1.94m (6ft 4-1/2in) and Logan Jones at 1.93m (6ft 4in). I would almost be willing to bet that Logan Jones will be at or around 305 pounds solid by the end of this season as well. Exp: Bradbury This is almost self-explanatory, as we have an 8-year veteran with 105 career starts going against a rookie. That experience will come in handy as the Bears look to get into an offensive groove as quickly as possible. Schematical fit: Jones Logan Jones is almost as perfect of a fit for what both Ben Johnson and Dan Roushar want at center that you can possibly imagine. While Bradbury is no slouch himself with a 4.92 forty compared to Jones’ 4.90 forty, Jones wins hands-down in the 3-cone time with a stunning 7.35, in comparison to a respectable 7.41 by Bradbury. What’s more is Jones’ athleticism pops on film as he can run any protection asked of him, while Bradbury has occasionally struggled when tasked to pull or slide in protection. Jones is extremely powerful at the point of attack as well. Short term fit: Bradbury What I’m looking at here is seeing who can be counted on right this second to line up and play center for the Bears if a game were happening at the time this article was published. Garrett Bradbury has all the experience, technical expertise, and knowledge of protections to identify the first threat before the ball is snapped. His previous chemistry with Joe Thuney is a plus as well. It is a very tall task for any rookie to line up at center during week one. Long term fit: Jones Much like the experience question above, this is blatantly obvious. Never mind the 7-year age difference between each player, their contracts also are drastically different. Garrett Bradbury signed a revised deal following his arrival to Chicago which amounts to 1-year and $4.7M. Out of the total value $3.7M is fully guaranteed with an additional $1M moved to what’s called Not Likely to be Earned (NLTBE) incentives. Logan Jones is on the standard 4-year rookie contract with a pre-slotted $8.47M and a $2.12M annual average. My pick: Logan Jones Yes, I did literally just say I’d expect Garrett Bradbury to get the nod if a game happened while I’m sitting at my desk typing this article. However, if Logan Jones performs well enough during training camp, then I cannot see Ben Johnson turning down a chance for the future to begin right away at center. I’m not simply saying he needs to be adequate – he needs to be outstanding for him to unseat Garrett Bradbury. I.E. dominate from the very moment the pads come on. Otherwise, the job will go to Garrett Bradbury, and Logan Jones will wait his turn. Whether that is in 2027 or this season is up to a multitude of factors. Who do you think opens week one with the starters at center?

title: Bengals training camp Day 2 news and discussion
summary: Competition breeds success. The Cincinnati Bengals are hoping to see plenty of that this training camp after the defense has undergone a significant upgrade to help one of the league’s best offenses not need to play near perfectly every week. That competition will also bring out some serious tension. After all, guys are fighting for […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JANUARY 04: Jalen Davis #35 of the Cincinnati Bengals celebrates a tackle during the second quarter of the game against the Cleveland Browns at Paycor Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Competition breeds success. The Cincinnati Bengals are hoping to see plenty of that this training camp after the defense has undergone a significant upgrade to help one of the league’s best offenses not need to play near perfectly every week. That competition will also bring out some serious tension. After all, guys are fighting for spots on the depth chart or on the roster entirely. There is a lifetime opportunity on the line for some players. In contrast, the Joe Burrows and Ja’Marr Chases of the team don’t need to worry about their spot on the roster. The reality is a good chunk of these players will not be around in Week 1, and for some of them, they will never touch an NFL practice field for the rest of their lives. Maybe Jalen Davis went a little overboard jumping onto Mike Gesicki’s back, but it is that kind of mindset and intensity this defense needs to foster if it wants to turn things around this upcoming season. Bengals News Training Camp Report | Scoping out Bengals’ Intense First Practice: ‘A Lot Of Alphas Out There’ “We didn’t have any false starts today. That’s number one, I think. Getting back into it, usually those come with the twos who haven’t heard the cadence very much, (or) gone against live defenses, and we didn’t have any today, so that’s positive. We’ve got to continue that. There shouldn’t be any, but we also had a couple motion errors, one by me, and a couple others by receivers. So we’ve got to clean that up. But overall, a productive day.” Dexter Lawrence is already showing why he was so coveted as a New York Giant. He has turned into one of the guys so naturally. His presence and how he talks about teammates shows he is a natural born leader. Five Observations from Day 1 of Bengals Training Camp “Somebody has to challenge the King of the Jungle as they say,” Lawrence said. “Somebody has to keep him on edge in order for him to get better and grow. That competitive spirit won’t stop. And with a guy like that, I know he’s going to bring it. It’s going to be fun.” A fun exchange from Dexter Lawrence and Joe Burrow is hopefully going to set the tone for both of these superstar players as Lawrence heads into his first season with Cincinnati. Joe Burrow, DJ Turner and Jalen Davis Break Silence on Bengals Practice Fight Everybody clarified once practice ended that the situation was only the result of competition, with no hostility present in the locker room afterwards. Turner compared the scuffle to brothers fighting. Turner would also say that Joe Burrow throwing in his direction was fun, and continued by saying practice should be harder for everyone. Turner had the most level-headed response to the fight. It was like brothers fighting. Realistically, Turner and Davis have been practicing with Chase and Gesicki for years now. Tempers are going to flare, but respect is the biggest thing at the end of the day. Bengals’ first-round D-lineman carted off with injury at training camp The status of one of the key figures on the Cincinnati Bengals’ reconfigured defensive line is in question after a training camp injury on Wednesday, July 29. Defensive end Shemar Stewart was carted off from practice after suffering an apparent leg injury. This could be a real blow to the defensive line’s depth. Stewart may not have made a Year 2 leap into being some monster pass rusher, but he certainly could have been a valuable rotational lineman at the very least. If he is out an extended period, the team may want to look at who is available. After tempers flared on Day 1, what are you hoping to see? More intensity from both sides or a bit of a cool-off? Let us know what you’re thinking in the comments!

summary: This offseason, the Cincinnati Bengals front office had one major job: Revamp the defensive side of the ball. full_text: This offseason, the Cincinnati Bengals front office had one major job: Revamp the defensive side of the ball. They seemed to have done just that on paper, landing players like Dexter Lawrence, Bryan Cook, and Super Bowl-winning defensive end Boye Mafe. Coming to the Queen City from Seattle, Mafe has seen a team transform quickly as the Seahawks won another title last season. Now suiting up for the Bengals, he sees some similarities between his time in the PNW and his time in Cincy so far. He recently joined The Insiders on the NFL Network last week and had this to say about Al Golden’s defense: “When I was in Seattle, when we first had Mike (McDonald) there, there was always a learning curve. Guys are learning a new defense. There’s gonna be a learning curve,” Mafe said. “Coming into spring, I’m seeing that guys are comfortable with the defense. I’m seeing that guys are understanding everything. They’re seeing the vision. They’re seeing how he (Golden) wants to run the defense, and what he wants it to look like. “It’s starting to become his vision of what the defense should look like.” "It's starting to become his vision" 👓 @Bengals Boye Mafe on DC Al Golden pic.twitter.com/bD5COWcHeh — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) July 24, 2026 Bengals fans should love hearing that as the team searches for a defensive pulse this year to keep up with their potent offense. If all of these new additions can click, it could mean another deep playoff run for Zac Taylor’s squad. However, we will have to wait and see if those pieces are actually fitting together before we all start booking our flights and hotels in Los Angeles.

title: Cleveland Browns continue to sit low in the preseason rankings
summary: The Cleveland Browns made it through Day 2 of training camp on Thursday under the watchful eye of visiting Colorado head coach Deion Sanders. That led to far too many breathless questions from the media to head coach Todd Monken about what Sanders the elder thought about various things related to the Browns. Fortunately, that […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 29: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns watches a drill during Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 29, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns made it through Day 2 of training camp on Thursday under the watchful eye of visiting Colorado head coach Deion Sanders. That led to far too many breathless questions from the media to head coach Todd Monken about what Sanders the elder thought about various things related to the Browns. Fortunately, that did not distract from the important work at hand for Monken, which includes: Figuring out who the starting quarterback will be from the equally poor choices of Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders. ( Best get comfy, Browns fans, because Monken is in no hurry .) Determining which pieces of the rebuilt offensive line fit best, with plenty of combinations on the field in the early part of camp. Keeping an eye on new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg, who is adding some much-needed freshness to the defensive scheme, according to safety Grant Delpit. This is all to be expected with a new head coach, a team filled with several first- and second-year players at key positions, and coming off a two-year run that produced just eight wins . The offensive line will work itself out, and while there may be a few growing pains in the opening weeks of the season, Rutenberg’s defense should be fine. (Or at least no worse than the one that allowed Carson Wentz to drive 80 yards for a game-winning touchdown pass last season.) It is still the Browns, of course, so everything begins and ends with the ongoing issue at quarterback, which explains in large part why Cleveland checks in at No. 27 in Josh Kendall’s latest rankings at The Athletic : In exchange for a $230 million guaranteed contract, the Browns have gotten 19 games, and nine wins out of Watson. He’s back for the final year of his deal after missing 10 games in 2024 and all of 2025 due to a twice-torn Achilles. He and Shedeur Sanders will compete for the starting job under new coach Todd Monken. Oh, and Myles Garrett is gone, after being traded to the Rams. Yes, Garrett is now with the Rams, but it is not as if Verse is the second coming of Nate Orchard, so the dropoff at the position may not be quite so impactful. Unfortunately, there is not much to be done this year about the quarterback play, other than hope that Monken can figure out a way to get something approaching average play out of the Watson/Sanders combo. The good news is that ranking is just one writer’s opinion, and being so low means there is nowhere to go but up!

title: Browns Shedeur Sanders needs ‘this throw in his bag’ to succeed due to lack of ‘size’, ‘arm talent’
summary: To the surprise of almost no one, the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition has not been the star of the show in Day 1 or Day 2 of training camp. Week 1 of Browns training camp still has two more practices, and the decision on whether Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders will be the team’s starter […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns watches a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images To the surprise of almost no one, the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition has not been the star of the show in Day 1 or Day 2 of training camp. Week 1 of Browns training camp still has two more practices, and the decision on whether Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders will be the team’s starter is not required until Week 1 of the season, as both HC Todd Monken and GM Andrew Berry have noted during the first two days in Berea. Berry also noted that the only variable that matters in deciding the competition is production , not Sanders’ age and developmental arc, Watson’s contract and history, or any other thing. According to Ben Solak of ESPN, Sanders’ lack of “elite size to shrug off contact” and lack of “special arm talent,” along with being a “below-average mover for the position,” means he needs to be able to make sure he has perfected one specific throw : If Sanders is to succeed at the NFL level, he needs this throw in his bag: the quick-release vertical ball against one-on-one coverage. It will be hard for him to create explosive plays otherwise. The type of throw that Solak is describing Sanders needs is similar to the deep throws Russell Wilson often threw down the sidelines, which were often described as “moon balls.” Those throws do not require a big arm, per se, but great timing and placement are key attributes that can lead to big plays. Solak did note that Sanders is comfortable in the scramble drill and is often willing to “give his receivers a shot,” which could help him make plays out of structure. Adding a quick-release vertical talent to the good traits Sanders showed last year could unlock the young quarterback’s future. What do you think of Solak’s comments on Sanders’ size, arm talent and movement skills? Do you think the kind of throw he describes could take Sanders to another level in the NFL? summary: Between Day 1 of Cleveland Browns training camp and Week 1 of the regular season ends up being just under two months of time. There is a lot of space for things to change on the Browns roster, including the QB competition. As we’ve seen with other teams, injuries are a big part of what […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Deshaun Watson #4 and Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Between Day 1 of Cleveland Browns training camp and Week 1 of the regular season ends up being just under two months of time. There is a lot of space for things to change on the Browns roster, including the QB competition . As we’ve seen with other teams , injuries are a big part of what changes things around the NFL . Cleveland also has a roster full of young players , so the swings in performance can be great. The competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders got off to an interesting start on Day 1 of training camp . On Day 2, Browns GM Andrew Berry spoke to the media and was asked about the starting quarterback job and the variables, including the age of the two combatants, that would impact the decision. Berry made it very clear that the only thing he and Todd Monken care about in the battle is “production,” as he minimized age as a meaningful reason to make the big decision: Browns GM Andrew Berry on theory they should go with younger QB in Shedeur Sanders if competition with Deshaun Watson is close. pic.twitter.com/6NSfTGd2Lg — Scott Petrak ct (@ScottPetrak) July 30, 2026 Based on Berry’s statement, Watson’s huge contract will not impact their decision. Sanders’ lack of experience and upside will not impact their decision. Watson heading to free agency at the end of the year will not impact their decision. Previous performance will not impact their decision. If Berry is to be trusted at his word, which is similar to what Monken has said, the starting quarterback will be the one they believe will be the most productive on the field in Week 1 of the 2026 season. Do you believe Berry? If so, do you think that is the only variable that should matter in the decision, or should the Browns think about age, contracts, etc when deciding between the two? summary: The Cleveland Browns have started training camp 2026. This year, there are plenty of new bodies in the coaching booth and on the roster. full_text: WR Denzel Boston #12 (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have started training camp 2026 . This year, there are plenty of new bodies in the coaching booth and on the roster. A total of 90 guys are in camp, with the final cutdown date being August 30, with waiver claims the following day. The NFL is down to three preseason games after going to a 17-game season. After the league takes on an 18-game schedule (and it will), most likely the exhibition games will be pared down to just two contests. RELATED: REALISTIC/UNREALISTIC EXPECTATIONS Preseason games are important. It works for the new guys who played under different systems the year before. And then there are the drafted rookies and the undrafted rookies that need the playing time to prove that they belong on the final roster. The Browns have zero issue with keeping undrafted rookies who stand out. Last year alone, Cleveland employed 12 guys who fit this description. As this year’s training camp rolls along and the preseason games are checked off the schedule, it is this year’s draft class who will be watched and scrutinized the most. Some will start. Others will secure backup spots, while others will go up and down the depth chart as the calendar drops off completed games. Plus, preseason games give the coaching staff of which players to cut. Although it is rare, sometimes drafted rookies are cut after their first camp. In 2024, seventh-round pick DT Jowon Briggs was waived on the final cutdown, then signed to the practice squad. Just because a guy was taken early in the draft doesn’t mean he will become the standout rookie in his first season. He could ultimately be labeled the franchise’s best draft pick. For this upcoming season, when it’s all said and done, which player will be this year’s best rookie? Here at Dawgs by Nature , we assembled some very knowledgeable folks with Browns affiliations. They cover the Browns and know their team. Which Browns’ rookie will have the best year in 2026? The 2026 Cleveland Browns draft class includes: Spencer Fano: OT, Utah – Round 1, Pick #9 KC Concepcion: WR, Texas A&M – Round 1, Pick #24 Denzel Boston: WR, Washington – Round 2, Pick #39 Emmanuel McNeil-Warren: S, Toledo – Round 2, Pick #58 Austin Barber: OT, Florida – Round 3, Pick #86 Parker Brailsford: C, Alabama – Round 5, Pick #146 Justin Jefferson: LB, Alabama – Round 5, Pick #149 Joe Royer: TE, Cincinnati – Round 5, Pick #170 Taylen Green: QB, Arkansas – Round 6, Pick #182 Carsen Ryan: TE, BYU – Round 7, Pick #248 Rod Bluhm The Browns Blitz Podcast LINK: THE BROWNS BLITZ PODCAST WR Denzel Boston The second wide receiver selected by the Browns in April, Denzel Boston, is a tough choice in a rookie class loaded with potential high-level contributors. Boston is my choice to have the best rookie season on the team. Word on the street is Denzel Boston is the best offensive player at OTA’s period. — JIA (@Jeremyinakron17) May 24, 2026 The Browns have been hungry for a big-bodied receiver since the days of Josh Gordon. Boston has an outstanding skill set that goes far beyond his role as a consistent red-zone target. His speed and great hands were evident in spring camps, matching his play at the University of Washington. Boston will be much more than a situational receiver winning 50/50 balls. Boston will likely challenge for second in Browns’ targets. Boston has the potential to lead the team in receiving yards and touchdown catches but will have a lot of competition. I expect him to put up impressive numbers in his rookie season. Look for 50 catches, 750 yards, and as many as 10 TDs. Anything close would be an outstanding season for a rookie receiver in Cleveland. Kristy Acuti Administrator: Browns Fans Only Facebook page Co-Host: Ulterior Motives Sports Podcast Network LINK: BFO LINK: ULTERIOR MOTIVES SPORTS PODCAST OT Spencer Fano Spencer Fano will be the breakout Browns rookie this season, and here is why I think he will be. First, he was drafted #9 overall. He’s the younger brother of Logan, who the Browns picked up undrafted, so they’ll have the sibling thing pushing him. Fano realizes that our offense has always needed work, and he’s shown in camp so far that he’s up for that challenge. Monken is singing his praises and has put him into the starting lineup for practices lately, and said he knows the challenge ahead of him. But he’s ready, and since OT Joe Thomas, I haven’t seen someone so dedicated to the offensive line. He’s ready to bring the energy and be as much of a leader in his rookie Year l, that he can be, and he’s ready to follow the standard that Joe set as the LT. He’s used to the right side, but excited to take on this challenge and prove to Monken he made the right choice. He’s got some great guys to protect, and he knows what’s on the line. “ Kenny Mac” MacDonald President: Ottawa Browns Backers Co-Host: The Dawgs Podcast LINK: OTTAWA BROWNS BACKERS FACEBOOK PAGE LINK: THE DAWGS PODCAST S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren When the Browns selected safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren out of Toledo with the 58th overall pick, most of the conversation centered around where he would fit on the depth chart. With Grant Delpit securing a contract extension and Ronnie Hickman returning on his tender, many assumed the rookie would have to wait his turn. It’s a different game now. Under new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg, this is less about winning a traditional starting job and more about earning snaps in a defense built around versatility. Across the NFL, defenses are relying more than ever on three-safety personnel packages to disguise coverages, rotate responsibilities after the snap, and better defend today’s NFL offenses. McNeil-Warren doesn’t have to replace Delpit or Hickman to make an immediate impact—he simply has to prove he belongs on the field with them. What makes McNeil-Warren my choice isn’t just his athletic ability; it’s how naturally his game aligns with Rutenberg’s defensive philosophy. Since arriving in Cleveland, Rutenberg has emphasized one message above all else: attack the football. His mantra has been, “When the ball is in the air, breathe it in.” McNeil-Warren already plays with that mentality. He attacks passes with confidence, trusts his instincts, and finishes plays. Just as importantly, he creates takeaways in multiple ways. He can “breathe it in” by coming down with an interception, but he also has the physicality and awareness to punch the football free after the catch. Those are game-changing plays, and coordinators always find room on the field for defenders who consistently create extra possessions. The Browns have also embraced the organization’s new defensive identity: Heart. Mind. Fist. McNeil-Warren embodies all three. The heart shows up in his relentless effort and willingness to play a physical brand of football. The mind is evident in his route recognition, communication, and ability to diagnose plays before they fully develop. The fist is what separates him from many young defensive backs. He doesn’t settle for making tackles—he attacks the football. Whether he’s ripping the ball free from a runner or high-pointing an interception, his first instinct is to create turnovers rather than simply end the play. Stylistically, McNeil-Warren reminds me of the type of player Xavier Watts became entering the NFL. This isn’t a comparison of résumés—Watts left Notre Dame as one of the nation’s most decorated defensive players—but rather a comparison of playing style. Both players built their reputations on instincts instead of elite testing numbers. They diagnose plays quickly, anticipate routes, and seem to have a natural feel for where the football is going. They’re ballhawks first and foremost, and in today’s NFL, that trait is invaluable. McNeil-Warren has the same turnover-producing DNA that made Watts such an intriguing prospect, and that type of instinctive playmaker fits exactly what…

title: Biggest difference between the 2025 and 2026 Browns
summary: After finishing the season 5-12, the 2025 Cleveland Browns struggled to find an identity. With three different quarterbacks starting over the course of the season and inconsistent offensive play throughout, the team often appeared to lack a clear direction. The team had reached a point where meaningful changes were necessary to shake things up. Going […]
full_text: After finishing the season 5-12, the 2025 Cleveland Browns struggled to find an identity. With three different quarterbacks starting over the course of the season and inconsistent offensive play throughout, the team often appeared to lack a clear direction. The team had reached a point where meaningful changes were necessary to shake things up. Going into the 2026 season, one of the biggest changes the team made was bringing in new head coach Todd Monken . Regardless of who returns to the field, the team will have a different look under its new leadership. While there is still uncertainty at quarterback, Shedeur Sanders is returning with a year of experience under his belt, and Deshaun Watson is returning from injury. Cleveland GM Andrew Berry also invested heavily in the offensive line all offseason, while long standing veterans Joel Bitonio , Wyatt Teller, and David Njoku are no longer on the team. The young players like Carson Schwesinger and Harold Fannin Jr. , who had really impressive rookie seasons, have a great opportunity to build on what they did in 2025. Additionally, the Browns’ 2026 draft class impressed many and brings another level of potential to what this team can be. Both seasons come with plenty of uncertainty, but the 2026 roster has a clearer vision and more upside, while the 2025 team seemed stuck repeating an approach that had already proven ineffective. Let me know what you think in the comments – What is the biggest difference between the 2026 and 2025 Browns?

summary: Dallas Cowboys Training Camp Day 2 Notes: Javonte Williams is being asked to do something he didn’t do enough of last year and more – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys offense has shined through two training camp practices. full_text: Dallas Cowboys Training Camp Day 2 Notes: Javonte Williams is being asked to do something he didn’t do enough of last year and more – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys offense has shined through two training camp practices. Javonte Williams as a pass catcher changes things There has been a clear focus by the Cowboys in these first couple of practices to develop the screen game, and that could be huge for the offense. Granted, screens can get predictable if you go about them the wrong way. Cowboys fans, media, and content creators know that all too well from years past. However, it has been a long time since running backs posed a legitimate threat in Dallas’ passing game, and that might change in 2026. The Cowboys are trying to get Williams more involved as a receiver. One play stood out from Thursday’s practice: Dak Prescott found Williams on a screen, and safety Caleb Downs came crashing down as a blitzer. The full view wasn’t available, but it looked like Downs was caught off guard by the play. Here’s the thing about Williams as a pass catcher: if he can contribute in the receiving game, the value you’re getting out of him goes up a notch. Last season, as good as Williams was running the ball, he was a non-factor through the air. Out of 51 running backs with minimum targets, Williams ranked dead last in EPA per target and dead last in yards per route run. His success rate came in 48th out of 51. He was essentially a checkdown catcher who gave you a completion but no damage after the catch. Practice Points: Thursday’s quick observations – DallasCowboys.com What stood out in Thursday’s practice? OXNARD, Calif. – Back at it for Thursday’s Day 2 of training camp, the Cowboys put together another spirited practice — even without pads coming on. The offense continued to make plenty of plays, much like it did on Wednesday, but the defense responded and helped even things out. This team entered camp relatively healthy, which makes every rep that much more important as players try to get on the field as much as possible. Here are some quick observations from the Cowboys’ staff writers. 4-2-88: The middle of the field has been friendly grounds for Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb to connect over the years, and the same was true on Thursday’s practice. Lamb was open on several occasions, and Prescott found him each time, allowing Lamb to turn the corner and finish plays that would’ve gone for chunk gains. Prescott was also able to get Jonathan Mingo involved in the middle of the field for a big gain, as Mingo fights for a spot on the 53-man roster. – (Tommy Yarrish) Adding Spice : After saying he’s feeling better than he did following his first foot surgery, Cowboys CB DaRon Bland had a strong practice highlighted by jumping a quick short route and breaking up a pass intended for Brevyn Spann-Ford. From there, you didn’t notice Bland too much, which is never a bad thing for defensive backs because it means they’re not getting picked on. Bland said Wednesday that his reps would be limited as he gets back into playing shape, but made the most of the work he saw on Thursday. – (Tommy Yarrish) Cowboys’ Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals – Todd Archer, ESPN.com Dak Prescott has his eyes set on the Super Bowl in 2026. Is he right for doing so? Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott isn’t afraid to let everybody know he carries big goals into 2026. Prescott wore a vintage T-shirt from the Cowboys’ last Super Bowl appearance — Super Bowl XXX in 1995 — when the team arrived in Oxnard, California, for training camp Monday. And while working out with skill players in Park City, Utah, before camp, Prescott came up with the anacronym GOTI, which stands for Greatest Offense There Is. “We want stuff in life a lot of times, but then when people start talking about it, you kind of hesitate. ‘Should I say that if they’re going to hold me to it?'” Prescott said. “Well, absolutely. Playing in this organization, being in it 10 years, going into year 11, I’m not going to shy away from it. When you don’t have it, it sucks when you don’t get to play for it. When you’re watching other teams play in the playoffs, there’s nothing worse than that. And so, yeah, I said I’d be the quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys when I was 6 years old and said I’d be in the NFL, and I got here. “A lot of things in my life, I said I’d do and I did it. And so why shy away from that now? Why shy away from asking people to hold me to the same standard that I believe that I can accomplish and this team can accomplish?” Jaishawn Barham & 6 Surprise Dallas Cowboys Turning Heads Early at Training Camp – Josh Sanchez, SI.com A look at a few surprises early in training camp. Jaishawn Barham, Linebacker Not enough great things can be said about third-rouond pick Jaishawn Barham. The former Michigan Wolverines star is a no-nonsense player whose physicality is jumping off of the screen, even without the team in pads. He has also shown an incredible attention to detail. If Barham is not going through drills himself, he is getting up close and personal, paying attention to every word the coaches say. Fans, media members, and even Brian Schottenheimer can’t help but turn their heads when Barham is taking reps. CB DaRon Bland, Shavon Revel ‘feeling good’ at start of training camp – Brian Martin, Blogging the Boys All eyes are on the cornerback room in the first week of training camp. The Dallas Cowboys spent the entire offseason attempting to upgrade the roster from top to bottom, and by most accounts they’ve succeeded. There are a few positions that may still need to be addressed at some point, but maybe cornerback will not be one. Dating back to December when DaRon Bland was placed on injured reserve, there’s been some concerns about his long-term future in Dallas. This is due to the injuries he sustained to his left foot that has required offseason surgery in consecutive years. No one quite knew how he would bounce back from surgery No. 2, but early reports definitely sound encouraging. Seeing that No. 26 is the Cowboys most seasoned and proven CB on the entire roster, and someone who is expected to start, him already “feeling really good” right now and running with the first-team defense is amazing news. Now, he just needs to find a way to remain healthy and return to his 2023 form. After two rather disappointing seasons, it’s easy to forget how well Bland played back in 2023. He was an All-Pro and set the NFL record for pick-sixes in a season with five, plus led the league in total interceptions with nine. That production ultimately led to the four-year, $92 million contract he signed in 2025. Daily discussion question: Who is standing out to you so far from camp?

title: CB DaRon Bland, Shavon Revel ‘feeling good’ at start of training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys spent the entire offseason attempting to upgrade the roster from top to bottom, and by most accounts they’ve succeeded. There are a few positions that may still need to be addressed at some point, but maybe cornerback will not be one. Dating back to December when DaRon Bland was placed on injured […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys spent the entire offseason attempting to upgrade the roster from top to bottom, and by most accounts they’ve succeeded. There are a few positions that may still need to be addressed at some point, but maybe cornerback will not be one. Dating back to December when DaRon Bland was placed on injured reserve, there’s been some concerns about his long-term future in Dallas. This is due to the injuries he sustained to his left foot that has required offseason surgery in consecutive years. No one quite knew how he would bounce back from surgery No. 2, but early reports definitely sound encouraging. DaRon Bland was a full participant in the first training camp practice and here’s what he had to say about his recent foot issue: “I feel really good — way better than I was the 1st time I had the surgery. … I'm confident right now. This whole rehab, I had no hiccups like last… — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) July 30, 2026 Seeing that No. 26 is the Cowboys most seasoned and proven CB on the entire roster, and someone who is expected to start, him already “feeling really good” right now and running with the first-team defense is amazing news. Now, he just needs to find a way to remain healthy and return to his 2023 form. After two rather disappointing seasons, it’s easy to forget how well Bland played back in 2023. He was an All-Pro and set the NFL record for pick-sixes in a season with five, plus led the league in total interceptions with nine. That production ultimately led to the four-year, $92 million contract he signed in 2025. Bland is currently the seventh highest-paid CB in the entire league and needs to start living up to his contract. The Cowboys are relying on him to start this year and play well. If not, they will be forced to turn to some younger and unproven players such as Shavon Revel to fill the void. Revel is coming off a rather ho-hum rookie season, one in which he never really looked fully healthy after sustaining a season-ending knee injury in his final collegiate season. He played all of last season with a knee brace, but has been moving/playing much more loosely and confidently without it in OTAs and now in training camp. Much like with DaRon Bland, there was some concerns about Revel’s health and how his knee would respond once things got much more physical and training camp. If early signs are any indicator, he too is “feeling good” right now. Shavon Revel told me his knee feels night-and-day better than last year. evidence: he banged it during a play (ouch) today and it went right back to feeling perfectly fine just a few minutes later. he’s all smiles and ready for Year 2. #Cowboys — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) July 29, 2026 Although Revel isn’t a projected starter right now, he could be competing with free agent addition Cobie Durant for the job. He was considered a first-round talent who slid to the Cowboys in the third round in last year’s draft. And, at 6’2”, 198-pounds, he would add some much-needed size to the Cowboys secondary. With both DaRon Bland and Shavon Revel well ahead of where they were a year ago, the Cowboys CB position is much less of a concern that it was before learning more about their health status. Hopefully they can continue to remain healthy from now throughout the rest of the 2026 NFL season. Christian Parker and his new-look defense is certainly hoping so.

While the first few practices of camp usually don’t produce many fireworks, players getting back on the field, even in a limited capacity, always drives discussion. Today, the Cowboys’ star receiving duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were the leaders of that conversation. At this point, it’s an easy argument to make that the Cowboys have the best pair of receivers in the NFL. This afternoon, Dallas’ talented wideouts showed why they both are so special, making plays all practice long. Pickens started the show, kicking off the afternoon with an impressive grab by the sideline. Dak to George Pickens pic.twitter.com/ODIdZG7JzF — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) July 30, 2026 As practice wore on, both Pickens and Lamb continued to make their presence felt. George Pickens pic.twitter.com/4chSq5a9uo — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026 A lot of CeeDee Lamb today too pic.twitter.com/mKWQ5TriGE — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026 Last season we saw defenses struggle time and time again trying to stop the slant to George Pickens. CeeDee Lamb has had a nice day pic.twitter.com/nvzVfbt44N — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) July 30, 2026 While he did put together a more-than-solid 2025 campaign, Lamb’s breakaway speed is something we didn’t see a whole lot of last season. Lamb’s 320 YAC and his 4.3 YAC/REC were both the second-lowest of his six-year NFL career. Getting Lamb back to being that dominant after-the-catch player that he has been throughout his time as a Cowboy will likely be a main focus for Dallas’ offense this upcoming year. While it may be hard to imagine Dallas talented receiving duo playing any better than they did last year, working together for the second year may bring out an even better version of each player this upcoming season. If Pickens can find consistency throughout the entirety of the regular season and Lamb can replicate his 2023 All-Pro-caliber campaign, it’s hard to see any defense in the league capable of stopping Dallas’ offense. Smith played for the Cowboys from 1990-02. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 45 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome to Day 45 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the toughest individual performances in Cowboys history. Dallas and New York both entered with identical records, with the NFC East, a first-round bye, and home-field advantage all sitting on the line. The game was close and went into overtime, but the score only tells a fraction of the story. This was the Emmitt Smith separated-shoulder game in 1994. Sunday, January 2, 1994 — 1:00 p.m. ET / 12:00 p.m. CT Giants Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 16, New York Giants 13 (OT) Dallas controlled the first half with the ball in Smith’s hands. Eddie Murray opened the scoring with a 32-yard field goal, then Troy Aikman found Smith for a five-yard touchdown in the second quarter. Another Murray field goal from 38 yards made it 13-0 at halftime. The Cowboys had the lead, the division within reach, and Smith was already carrying the offense. Then came the injury that turned a big game into a franchise legend. Smith separated his shoulder on a 46-yard run before halftime, but he refused to come out. Jimmy Johnson wanted to use Lincoln Coleman more, but Smith pushed back and made it clear he did not want to be a decoy. He wanted the ball. That is what made the performance feel different from a normal tough-guy story. Smith was not just surviving pain, he was still deciding the game. The Giants made their move after halftime. Jarrod Bunch scored from one yard out in the third quarter, David Treadwell added a 29-yard field goal, and suddenly Dallas’ 13-0 lead was down to 13-10. Early in the fourth quarter, Treadwell hit again from 32 yards to tie the game. The Cowboys had stopped scoring, the Giants had the home crowd behind them, and Smith was playing with one arm. That is where the game became one of the defining moments of the 1990s Cowboys. The Giants won the overtime toss and took the ball, but Dallas forced a punt. Starting at their own 25, the Cowboys put together an 11-play drive built almost entirely around Smith. He ran it. He caught it. He absorbed contact. He kept getting up. The drive ended with Murray’s 41-yard field goal, and Dallas walked out with the NFC East title, the bye, and home-field advantage. Smith’s final numbers were ridiculous given the circumstances. He had 32 carries for 168 rushing yards, 10 catches for 61 receiving yards, and Dallas’ only touchdown. That gave him 229 total yards on a day when the Giants knew exactly where the ball was going. Aikman was efficient, completing 24 of 30 passes for 180 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions, but this game belonged to number 22. This game belongs on the countdown because it is one of the clearest examples of what made Emmitt Smith great. He was not the biggest back, not the fastest back, and not the flashiest back, but in the biggest moment of the regular season, with the Cowboys’ Super Bowl path hanging in the balance, he carried the team with a separated shoulder. Dallas would use the bye, beat Green Bay, beat San Francisco, and then defeat Buffalo in Super Bowl XXVIII. This win in the Meadowlands helped make that road possible and Smith showed the NFL what made him the greatest running back in league history. #Cowboys vs #Giants 1994 Week 18 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 16, New York Giants 13 (OT) #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/gSRLZZtvqy — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 29, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Smith clinched his third straight NFL rushing title with this performance. He stayed in the game after the shoulder injury, rushed for 168 yards, helped Dallas win in overtime, and wrapped up the rushing crown.
