title: Cowboys 2026 roster rundown: S Markquese Bell
summary: Markquese Bell has called Dallas his NFL home for the last four seasons, but a fifth won’t come easily. With the Cowboys’ new defensive look and significant investment at safety, Bell could be swept away in a wave of change. This 2026 training camp could have serious ramifications for his career. Background Years in NFL: 4Acquired […]
full_text: Markquese Bell has called Dallas his NFL home for the last four seasons, but a fifth won’t come easily. With the Cowboys’ new defensive look and significant investment at safety, Bell could be swept away in a wave of change. This 2026 training camp could have serious ramifications for his career. Background Years in NFL: 4 Acquired by: UDFA (2022) Despite being an FCS All-American in his senior year at Florida A&M, Bell went undrafted in 2022. While possessing great size and length for an NFL safety, that big frame comes with a lack of quickness that causes issues in pass coverage. Still, he signed with Dallas after the draft and had a strong camp. He earned a spot on the 53-man roster, though he was inactive most of the season. In the five games Bell did play, it was almost entirely on special teams. In 2023, with Dallas shorthanded at linebacker, Bell moved into a surprisingly big role on Dan Quinn’s defense as a hybrid LB. Quinn had been using Jayron Kearse in this way, mainly in nickel looks, and Bell took it a step further with even more LB usage in other formations. He finished second on the team in tackles behind Damone Clark, playing all 17 games and starting eight. With the move to Mike Zimmer as defensive coordinator in 2024, Dallas went away from some of its “small ball” practices and Bell went back to safety. He fell down the depth chart, only getting 34 defensive snaps in nine games, but remained active on special teams. A shoulder injury in Week 11 ended his season prematurely. Despite the down year, Bell got a three-year contract extension in 2025 at about $3 million per season. It was a mutually beneficial agreement, reducing Bell’s cap hit from what a restricted free agent tender would cost but giving him some job security in exchange. Bell’s role also increased last year as one of the core backups at safety, which included three starts. Ahead of this crucial fifth season and with a new defensive coaching staff to impress, Bell got off to a bad start with an arrest last April for marijuana possession. It is still unknown if he will face any suspension from the league or team to start the regular season. As we just learned with Charles Snowden, sometimes the league’s discipline doesn’t come quickly Contract Status Years Left: 2 2026 Cap Hit: $2.83 million If Bell is released, it will come with zero cap relief and push about $833k dead money onto next year’s cap. That isn’t enough to keep him around if Dallas prefers another player, but it could be a tiebreaker in Bell’s favor at final cuts. 2026 Projections Role: Backup S Roster Chance: 30% Bell has one of the more enigmatic situations this summer. His experience and versatility are valuable, but we’ve seen how shifts in defensive coordinators have helped and hurt his status and playing time. Bell’s limitations in coverage and Parker’s expected use of two-high safety formations don’t seem like a great pairing, but what if Parker likes Bell’s past work in the hybrid LB role? And if nothing else, Bell’s been a core special teams player for a while, which matters most at the bottom of the roster. At this point, it feels like Bell’s outside looking in and hoping for an injury. Between all the new defensive backs and linebackers, it feels like “out with the old” is a theme this summer. As long as the handpicked rookies and free agents stay healthy and show competence, Bell feels like a holdover whose best days came and went with Dan Quinn. Don’t be surprised if Bell isn’t a Commander by September. Still, Bell’s survived this long by continuing to show up in Oxnard and earn his spot. That same opportunity lays before him now. The legal issue shouldn’t make a difference: Bell isn’t going to have a large enough role to make a brief suspension painful for the team. As long as he outplays the down-roster competition, and there’s a clear role for him in the new scheme, Bell could get at least one more year with the Cowboys. title: Jerry Jones excites Cowboys camp with potential trade talk
summary: The Dallas Cowboys arrived at training camp in Oxnard, California, with a newfound sense of optimism. The offseason featured almost no drama, and quite honestly, it’s been rather cricket-y. This has left many people wondering, when is the drama coming? Well, leave it to Jerry Jones to create some noise as soon as he stepped […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys arrived at training camp in Oxnard, California, with a newfound sense of optimism. The offseason featured almost no drama, and quite honestly, it’s been rather cricket-y. This has left many people wondering, when is the drama coming? Well, leave it to Jerry Jones to create some noise as soon as he stepped in front of the microphone. Rather than spending the better part of Tuesday’s press conference justifying their lack of front office moves, Jones opted to throw some unprovoked fuel on the fire, stating that he is willing to make a big move to make this year’s team better, even if it requires trading away future draft capital. For years, the Cowboys’ front office has built its identity on calculated decisions. Draft capital is like gold to them. Lately, they’ve been dabbling a little, giving up some high picks for George Pickens last summer, and then Quinnen Williams at the trade deadline. That was easier to part with considering some of those draft picks came courtesy of the Micah Parsons trade, but is it possible that Jones has more dealing to do? “I’d give up the future to substitute where we are today, as to a player, to give you an idea about what I’d invest, something substantive, to get the right kind of deal and improve us for Opening Day, I would, “ Jones said, surprisingly deviating from the typical “we like our guys” approach we’ve seen routinely over the years. The Cowboys owner then proceeded to talk about saving a little for today, a little for tomorrow, and then about milk toast, in an otherwise typical incoherent Jones, except we could sense what he was getting at. Jones was blunt, stating that he feels good enough about this team to be comfortable in pulling the trigger to make a big trade to help them go from good to great. He knows the clock is ticking and he doesn’t have a lot of time to lolligag if he wants to capitalize on a dwindling window where Dak Prescott is leading the offense. Time is of the essence. Jones is always saying things. He is quite the talker, but he created real excitement by leaking that he had just recently been on the phone with some unnamed owner discussing a big trade to strengthen the defense. He backpedaled slightly to avoid implicating himself in any potential tampering violations, but it was too late. Jones now has the fanbase believing they are just a piece here or there away from something big happening in Dallas, and maybe, just maybe, Jerry is going to finally push those chips in the middle. With the idea that the Cowboys could be up to something, the question then moves to – who are they eyeballing? Edge rusher Maxx Crosby is atop the rumors , especially after Jones clarified that he has never walked away from pursuing him. Additionally, this new development also happens to align with the recent rumors of Vita Vea wanting out of Tampa Bay, although the team has already reloaded considerably at the defensive tackle position after trades for Williams and Kenny Clark. The remnants of Jones’ comments are spreading like wildfire, and it has sparked huge enthusiasm within the fanbase. A willingness to go big now and make a blockbuster deal creates even more excitement in an already exciting start to training camp. New coaches and new players have amplified the intrigue, so why stop? Just keep teasing away with more goodness. The team has already mortgaged some future cap for right-now productivity, so who’s to say they’re not willing to ship off a little more of their future?

title: Why the Cowboys’ pass rush couldn’t save their pass defense
summary: In a recent post on the Cowboys’ pass rush, we saw that the 2025 Cowboys ranked sixth in pressure rate despite ranking just 22nd in sacks. Of course, pressuring the passer only works if your secondary is any good. And the 2025 Cowboys secondary was the exact opposite of whatever “good” is, ranking just 31st […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Dallas Cowboys cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. (34) reacts to breaking up a pass during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Minnesota Vikings on December 14, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In a recent post on the Cowboys’ pass rush, we saw that the 2025 Cowboys ranked sixth in pressure rate despite ranking just 22nd in sacks . Of course, pressuring the passer only works if your secondary is any good. And the 2025 Cowboys secondary was the exact opposite of whatever “good” is, ranking just 31st in the league with a 109.6 defensive passer rating. If you’re in the “if only they’d had more sacks” school of thought, consider that in 2024, when the Cowboys were third in total sacks and still had Micah Parsons, they also ranked at the bottom of the league (28th) in defensive passer rating. The lesson is hard to ignore: generating pressure is only half the equation. What happens after the ball leaves the quarterback’s hand matters just as much – and for the Cowboys in 2025, it mattered a lot more. And that’s what we’re going to focus on today. We’ll first look at the overall pass defense performance and then deep-dive into the different position groups. We’ll be using two key metrics along the way: Burn rate : number of catches a defensive player allows versus the number of balls thrown at the receiver he is covering. For example, a burn rate of 80% would mean that opponents have completed eight of ten passes thrown at the receiver the defensive player was covering. Defensive Passer Rating : uses the same data and formula as the better known passer rating for the quarterback ( i.e. completion percentage, yard per attempt, touchdowns and interceptions), but applies them to a defender, where they become completion percentage allowed (aka ‘burn rate’) , yards per attempt allowed , touchdowns allowed and interceptions made . Have you ever wondered where opposing quarterbacks are throwing the ball against the Cowboys, and how successful they are? No? Well I did, so I reverse engineered the game-by-game stats at ProFootballFocus.com to come up with the nifty little graphic below which breaks down the 2025 passer rating and burn rate of the Cowboys’ 2025 opponents by pass direction and -distance. A couple of things stand out immediately. The Cowboys generated pressure, but opposing quarterbacks rarely had to hold the football long enough for it to matter. There was almost always somebody open underneath. You’ll notice that the burn rate in the six quadrants below the yellow line (i.e. less than 10 yards down the field) is quite high – 86% on 282 for 327 passing – which might be an indicator for why the pressure the Cowboys are generating is not leading to a better pass defense: if the QB can just dump off the ball to a receiver with a seven to 10-yard cushion, or simply target anybody covered by a linebacker, the opposing QB doesn’t even need a hot read anymore, because there’s always going to be people running free underneath. Also, 46% of passing yards allowed by the Cowboys defense are generated by passes completed between the numbers – and that’s despite playing Jalen Hurts and his fear of the middle, not once but twice. Perhaps the middle of the field is where the communication issues hurt the Cowboys the most as blown coverages by linebackers, corners, and safeties allowed opponents to roam freely across the middle. And finally, the Cowboys secondary allowed a defensive passer rating (DPR) of 110 or more in five of the six quadrants beyond the yellow line (i.e. ten yards or more downfield), making this defense the perfect complement for a Rex Grossman-like play style. Stats by Position Some analytical housekeeping: in official NFL team box scores, every official pass attempt by the opposing offense must be accounted for as a target. PFF, which we’ll be using for the individual stats later on, excludes specific types of throws from their defensive player tallies. Unassigned Targets (Throwaways and Spikes) : When an opposing quarterback throws the ball away or spikes it, the NFL counts it as an official pass attempt. PFF does not assign a target to any individual defensive player on a throwaway or spike because no defender was actually covering a receiver. Clear Overthrows : If a quarterback overthrows a receiver by 15 yards or throws into a completely vacant zone due to a broken route, the NFL log still charts a target to the intended receiver. PFF often omits these if no defender was in a position to realistically make a play on the ball. The difference is notable: the traditional box score shows the Cowboys defense with 556 targets and a 109.6 defensive passer rating, while PFF shows only 504 assigned targets, which in turn drives DPR to 121.5, with all else remaining equal. Most of us are quite used to the traditional passer rating, and may feel the PFF-based DPR (without unassigned targets and overthrows) are quite high. The following table shows how to evaluate the individual DPR numbers. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Positional Ranking Description Linebacker DPR Corner DPR Safety DPR 100-80 Blue-Chip Players <90 <77 <80 79-60 NFL starter quality at position 91-100 78-88 81-97 59-40 Average to slightly below average player 101-108 89-96 98-109 39-20 Underperformer 109-115 97-110 110-118 19-0 Red Flag >115 >110 >118 Source: PFF, min. 20 targets Most targeted Linebackers The Cowboys knew they were thin at linebacker going into the 2025 season, so they brought in Kenneth Murray and Jack Sanborn in free agency, and later even traded for Logan Wilson in early November. Here’s how the entire linebacker room fared in pass defense. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Player Targets CMP Yards Burn rate DPR Kenneth Murray 48 35 345 73% 99.7 Logan Wilson 44 33 327 75% 118.3 Shemar James 37 35 332 95% 131.1 DeMarvion Overshown 18 17 156 94% 121.3 Marist Liufau 15 14 167 93% 135.3 Jack Sanborn 12 11 117 92% 107.3 Linebacker Average 174 145 1,444 83% 118.5 If you rank 31st overall in DPR, none of your position groups will impress anybody. The Cowboys linebackers rank 29th overall. The league average DPR for linebackers is 107.3, and the two best linebacker rooms in Seattle (78.3) and Philly (84.6) run circles around the Cowboys linebackers. And the table above does not inspire a lot of confidence for 2026. Murray, Wilson, and Sanborn are gone, for good reason, but they might better than anything the Cowboys had and have. A burn rate in the 90s is a playcalling invitation for opposing quarterbacks, “ just target whoever is covered by a linebacker and you should be fine. ” Dee Winters was added to the room and brings a “yellow” 104.2 DPR to Dallas, and what third-round pick Jaishawn Barham brings to the room remains to be seen. There is some hope that DeMarvion Overshown, now fully healthy, could also be an upgrade. He was slightly better in 2024 with a 101.6 DPR, but his burn rate was also quite high at 91%. Many fans have been clamoring for an additional signing at linebacker, and they are right, but it has to be a guy who can cover. Otherwise OC Christian Parker’s scheme will have to fix the linebacker performance by itself, and that’s a big ask. But perhaps it is the right ask. If the Cowboys are going to play with Caleb Downs as a nickelback patrolling the middle of the field, that might take pressure off the linebackers and fix some…

title: Caleb Downs finds the football regardless of position at first Cowboys camp practice
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have completed their first practice of 2026 training camp in Oxnard, California, and crossing this big offseason milestone feels so good. A “boring” offseason storyline wise has put an even more intense focus on the football activities of the team. On day one, this featured a lot of expected, familiar names on […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 26: Caleb Downs of the Ohio State Buckeyes poses on the NFL Network set during the NFL Scouting Combine at the Indiana Convention Center on February 26, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have completed their first practice of 2026 training camp in Oxnard, California, and crossing this big offseason milestone feels so good. A “boring” offseason storyline wise has put an even more intense focus on the football activities of the team. On day one, this featured a lot of expected, familiar names on offense doing their thing, and a whole host of new ones in Christian Parker’s defense doing the same – including first-round pick Caleb Downs. The narrative on the Cowboys defense until they prove otherwise is that they were abysmal in 2025, and no single player acquisition or coaching change can fix this. While that may be true, the Cowboys did find a brilliant way to land the best defensive back in this year’s draft, likely it’s most versatile overall defender, and an elite communicator that’s highly coachable to pair with a defensive back expert in Parker. Step aside 31 other fanbases, Cowboys fans should finally feel justified to let the hype train leave the station when it comes to year one for Downs. The Cowboys wasted no time utilizing Downs in a variety of ways at his first practice. Rookie minicamp and OTAs set the expectation that Downs would be a primary nickel defender, which Downs did play up against the first team offense, with P.J. Locke (who got banged up in practice as well), Malik Hooker, and Jalen Thompson getting the deep safety reps. Caleb Downs looks to be in the nickel here with PJ Locke as trailing safety. both are facing the first team. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/8DdvgYW0fG — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) July 29, 2026 Downs also lined up off the edge, in the box, and deep in the secondary according to reports, and came from a deep position to recover a forced fumble by Rashan Gary on running back Phil Mafah for his first splash play of camp. Rashan Gary punch out and Caleb Downs recovery pic.twitter.com/Dwdo9n56km — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 29, 2026 When Downs was in the nickel, the Cowboys’ starting cornerbacks from the jump at practice were Cobie Durant and DaRon Bland. For a defense that gave up an onslaught of big plays over the top last season, this is as good of a place to start on the back end as one could hope for. The next positive things to look for in the secondary would be more work from Shavon Revel and Caelen Carson, and rookie Devin Moore as potential further options at cornerback, but most of all above all this is the development of Downs in the perfect environment to really hit the ground running as a rookie. Caleb Downs, a very popular player among Cowboys fans pic.twitter.com/GntoQT0891 — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) July 29, 2026 The Cowboys’ second practice on Thursday will begin at the same time as their first, and will be their last until the pads come on for the first time on Monday, August 3rd. With the most experienced safety on this roster, Malik Hooker, already finding a way to make a physical play with a “deck” of Phil Mafah without pads on, the rest of the Cowboys safety group will be extra motivated to make a play in this practice as well, and will have the motivation from Parker to do so given the energy he brings to the practice field. This should be another big day to watch for Caleb Downs to do new things that make us go “wow”. Later on, Malik Hooker decked Phil Mafah. full_text: Observations from the first Dallas Cowboys training camp practice in Oxnard – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The first day of training camp is in the books. Jaydon Blue Takes Advantage Of Phil Mafah Fumble The backup running back role is up for grabs going into training camp, and Wednesday served as the first opportunity for the players behind Javonte Williams on the depth chart to make an impression. After Williams started with the first-team, Mafah was the first one to rotate in. He saw a few handoffs before a Rashan Gary punchout saw him drop the ball only for rookie Caleb Downs to recover. Just like your coach in middle school would do if a player turned the ball over in practice, Mafah was subbed out. Jaydon Blue rotated in and immediately ran for a 45-yard touchdown that probably would have stood if the pads were on. It was a big play to set the tone for what is to come this training camp at the position. Deeper in the room, Israel Abanikanda and Dominic Richardson both popped big runs with the third-team unit. George Pickens Generates Crowd Excitement The crowd on-hand at the River Ridge Playing Fields in Oxnard wasn’t packed by any means in the middle of a weekday, but there were a good amount of youth groups and Cowboys fans on-hand. The ones who did make the trip to see the Cowboys were treated with some excitement in the form of George Pickens during the team period. In one of the first plays of full 11-on-11 work, Dak Prescott found Pickens on the right side for a quick completion. Had it been in full pads, he most likely would’ve immediately been wrapped up by DaRon Bland, but he squeaked out and ran all the way down the field before falling on his back across the end zone. The crowd loved it, and they cheered on Pickens while he ran back into the huddle. After the practice, he spent a good amount of time signing autographs with fans as well. For a player that has had a public eye on his contract situation this offseason, Pickens has been front-and-center with his mentality and approach in Oxnard so far. It took one practice for the Dallas Cowboys to make telling Caleb Downs reveal at training camp – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Caleb Downs was all over the field on the first day of camp. It took one Dallas Cowboys practice to reveal something surprising about first-round rookie Caleb Downs. The Cowboys held their first open practice of training camp in Oxnard, California, and the early defensive alignment was very revealing. That starts with the first-round rookie’s usage. Cowboys use Downs everywhere in first practice For months, the Cowboys had Caleb Downs penciled in as the starting nickel cornerback. That may still be the case come September. But based on what reporters saw on the field during Day 1 of camp, Dallas appears willing to deploy Downs all over the defense, not just in the slot. According to Joseph Hoyt from the Dallas Morning News, Downs did start the practice session at nickel. However, Hoyt offered a revealing observation that caught my attention: “In the last three plays I have seen, Cowboys rookie Caleb Downs line up near the edge in the box and play deep middle third,” Hoyt wrote on social media . “They wanted a versatile defensive back and they plan to use downs accordingly.” Safety P. J. Locke exits Cowboys’ first training camp practice with non-contact knee injury – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News It appears to not be serious. OXNARD, Calif. — Cowboys safety P.J. Locke was helped off the field during Wednesday’s training camp practice with a knee injury, a person familiar with the situation told The Dallas Morning News. Locke limped off the field with roughly half an hour left in the team’s first training camp practice. He was back pedaling during a play and appeared to injure his left knee when he planted on it. It was a non-contact injury. Locke walked alongside Jim Maurer, the team’s head trainer, off the field. He didn’t return. Tyler Guyton on competition, 2026 challenges: ‘I want to be a better player’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The former first-round pick is ready to take the next step. OXNARD, Calif. — Tyler Guyton is no stranger to competition. The Austin native has been battling for position ever since he picked up a football as a child, and upwards through his time at TCU and, ultimately, the University of Oklahoma. He’d weather all of those storms to become a first-round pick for the Dallas Cowboys in 2024, and now comes yet another round of competition to test his mettle — from two entirely different directions. “I mean, it’s the same as every day: coming to work and getting better, to try and get one percent better every day,” Guyton said following the first practice of 2026 training camp. Outwardly, he’s working to stave off offensive lineman Nate Thomas, but his biggest opponent is himself and his health. If he wins against the latter, Guyton will likely win against the former. Ability isn’t the question — availability is. Guyton has shown he can make strides when he’s on the field, but he’s suffered injury in both of his first two seasons that has cost him significant time and, as such, a significant opportunity at gaining experience. He’s made changes to both his diet and training regimen to improve durability, also noting that he’s “put on “grown man strength” for this coming season while balancing it with being technically sound against literally the most freakishly athletic pass rushers on the planet. From there, well, here’s how Guyton sees it through his point-of-view: “I [want to get] more technically sound, more confident in the playbook and the scheme and, overall, just a better player,” he said. “It’s a process, of course, and we have to take it day by day, one foot in front of the other. But, at the end of the day, I’m trying to get to a certain point where I feel good about going to the season.” Daily discussion question: What was your biggest takeaway from the first practice of camp?

title: Denver Broncos roster review: Offensive lineman Matt Peart
summary: The offensive line is a premier strength of the Denver Broncos. They tout a quality starting lineup and good depth behind them with promising young players. Under the guidance of Head Coach Sean Payton and Assistant Head Coach Zach Strief, the Broncos’ offensive trenches have once again become a formidable force for the franchise. One […]
full_text: Nov 10, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Denver Broncos offensive tackle Matt Peart (79) at the line of scrimmage against the Kansas City Chiefs during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | Denny Medley-Imagn Images The offensive line is a premier strength of the Denver Broncos. They tout a quality starting lineup and good depth behind them with promising young players. Under the guidance of Head Coach Sean Payton and Assistant Head Coach Zach Strief, the Broncos’ offensive trenches have once again become a formidable force for the franchise. One player vying to make the final 53-man roster this year is Matt Peart. The Broncos signed Peart to a two-year deal worth $7 million during the 2024 free agency period. In his first season with the Broncos, Peart was a valuable swing man in the offensive trenches. He appeared in every game and started two of them. Last season, he made the final roster and appeared in six games with one start before a knee injury ended his season in mid-October. Entering the final year of his deal, Peart appears to be on the outside looking in with respect to making the Broncos’ final roster. Let’s discuss the odds of him earning one of the backup spots on the team. Player Profile Age: 29 | Experience: Seventh Year | College: Uconn | Height: 6’7” | Weight: 318 pounds 2025 Statistics : Appeared in six games with one start replacing Ben Powers at left guard. Missed remainder of season after suffering a knee injury early in October. Matt Peart’s 2026 outlook with the Broncos Last season, the Broncos kept nine offensive linemen on their active roster. Peart was one of four backups alongside Alex Palczeswki, Frank Crum and Alex Forsyth. I expect the Broncos to carry the same number at the position this season. However, I’m not too sure Peart will be one of them. Denver drafted Boise State offensive lineman Kage Casey in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Given such, that is one less reserve spot available or up for grabs compared to ’25. Barring some sort of unforeseen circumstance, Casey seems like an absolute lock to make the final 53-man roster. Additionally, the Broncos rewarded Palczewski with a two-year contract this offseason. They clearly believe in his potential and believe his continued development will be crucial for the state of Denver’s offensive line moving forward. Last but not least, I presume the Broncos’ brass would like to see Crum continue to grow. He appeared in just one game during the ‘24 season but was active for 11 last season and showed some promise in his limited snap share on offense. Final Thoughts Peart is one of the veteran players who made last year’s final roster that I expect to be cut in this year’s roster trimming process. Truth be told, I’m not worried about his skill or talent level. He has over 1,000 career offensive snaps as a pinch starter—a lot more than most any backup Denver is poised to bring back. However, coming off injury and facing stiff competition from several other young players the team is trying to develop will make it a tough challenge for him. Peart will have to stay healthy, compete at a high-level during training camp, and perform well during the preseason to make the squad.

summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! People always try to find comparisons and make connections. That is especially true in the wide world of sports. And it’s even truer when you have Sean Payton. As one of the best head coaches in the NFL and for one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history, Payton brings a […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos warms up before kickoff against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoff game at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! People always try to find comparisons and make connections. That is especially true in the wide world of sports. And it’s even truer when you have Sean Payton. As one of the best head coaches in the NFL and for one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history, Payton brings a unique perspective. Payton will present Drew Brees for his induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame next week. Of course, Payton was asked about his years coaching Brees with the New Orleans Saints on Thursday. It makes sense given the success the two had and the relationship they built over their time together. One day at a time. 😤 pic.twitter.com/Wu7BnICusZ — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 30, 2026 Regarding the Denver Broncos, Payton was asked about Brees and Bo Nix. Hence, the comparison and connection referenced earlier. Payton said about Brees and Nix: “I think that No. 1, they were high-volume college players. He (Brees) played a lot of snaps at Purdue. I would say the immediate, just analytical statistical number would be the accuracy numbers. From an NFL perspective, he’ll go down as the most accurate passer in the history of the league, and, collegiately, he was at Purdue. I think historically speaking, Bo was the most accurate college passer when you look at a lot of numbers, so that would be the first. “(It’s) a tough comparison for anybody in their (third) year, but that would just be the beginning. Their personalities are different, of course, but their accuracy and their positioning of the ball is certainly noticed.” Nix has a long way to go before he’s in the discussion with Brees. However, Nix is on the right path after his first two seasons in the league. Coming off an ankle injury after one of the best wins in franchise history is an interesting element to the coming season. We’ll see what the future holds, but it’s going to be fun to see Nix’s continued development and growth this season and going forward.

(Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the eve of training camp officially opening, the Denver Broncos have made a minor roster move. According to reports, the team has signed defensive back Sam Webb and has waived cornerback Blake Cotton with an injury designation . Webb had a tryout with the team earlier today and impressed the coaches enough to sign him to their 90-man roster. Cotton suffered a hamstring injury during Wednesday’s first ramp-up practice and sat out today’s practice before being waived with an injury settlement later in the day. #Broncos are signing DB Sam Webb per source. NFL veteran won his tryout from today. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) July 30, 2026 Sam Webb is a 28-year-old cornerback who is listed at 6-0, 194 pounds and has bounced around the league a bit. He originally went undrafted in 2022 and signed with the Las Vegas Raiders. From there, he spent time with the Carolina Panthers, back with the Raiders, and spent last season with the Titans and Browns. Now, he joins the Denver Broncos and adds some backend corner depth to their 90-man roster. Throughout his career, Webb has appeared in 36 games, including 5 starts, and has totaled 45 tackles, 1 pass deflection, and 1 fumble return for a touchdown. The Broncos cornerback room is loaded and pretty much set with Pat Surtain II, Riley Moss, Ja’Quan McMillian, Jahdae Barron, and Kris Abrams-Draine, but there’s an opportunity to compete for a spot on the practice squad. Webb will be competing with Jaden Robinson, Taylor Reese, Brent Austin, and Sean Fresch Jr. for those spots on the practice squad. Realistically, Webb is likely more or less a camp body and someone to play in the second half of preseason games. With that said, he is joining the team early enough into camp where he will have a chance to impress the coaches. He has spent time in this league and is experienced, so it’s possible he could push for a spot on the practice squad, but we shall see how it plays out. Training camp officially kicks off tomorrow for the Broncos after two days of acclimation/ramp up practices. Fans will be in attendance, we’ll have live updates, and more information about how the team looked during that day’s practice. Stay tuned to Mile High Report for updates on all things Broncos Camp.

title: Sean Payton is pleased with the shape Bo Nix is in to start training camp
summary: All eyes have been on Bo Nix since the shocking announcement of his season-ending ankle injury just minutes after a thrilling comeback overtime win against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Round. Since that day, the news around Nix and his rehab has been mostly on schedule and positive and now that training camp […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 16: Bo Nix (10) of the Denver Broncos works out during minicamp at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, June 16, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images All eyes have been on Bo Nix since the shocking announcement of his season-ending ankle injury just minutes after a thrilling comeback overtime win against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Round. Since that day, the news around Nix and his rehab has been mostly on schedule and positive and now that training camp has begun, head coach Sean Payton has confirmed he is all the way back and good to go. When asked where Nix could take a step in his third season, Payton mentioned how great of a season he was already coming off of and the real improvement will come from improving the offense around him. “The next step is kind of cliché,” Payton said. “He just finished winning 14 games and having a really good season. Do I think he’s going to continue to improve? Yes. I’m pleased with the shape he’s in. The timeline relative to everything we’ve discussed injury-wise is falling into place. It’s good to have him back out there in the team periods. I think there are certain areas for us offensively that can help with the quarterback, a consistent run game throughout the year. There are some things that we can do to help him, so we’re off and getting started.” “I think there are certain areas for us offensively that can help with the quarterback, a consistent run game throughout the year. There are some things that we can do to help him, so we’re off and getting started.” Sean Payton I touched on this in my last post about what Jaylen Waddle will bring to the offense. The offense essentially brought everyone back and the only changes at starter-level positions is in play-calling from Davis Webb and the trade for Waddle. Ironically, both could end up playing a pivotal role in helping the offense find sustained consistency in games — something it lacked in large stretches of games last season. Nix nearly passed for 4,000 yards last season and, I believe, if all goes well in 2026, he won’t need to come close to that number for this team to make a huge leap in efficiency and scoring. If they can find both, this team is going to be a serious Super Bowl contender.

title: Sean Payton says certain prototypes ‘can walk on water’ and Jaylen Waddle is one of them
summary: With the Denver Broncos primed to start training camp on Friday, we had a few early acclimation practices this week where the media got to talk with members of the team with Head Coach Sean Payton being one of them. There were a couple of things he mentioned that really stood out to me. The […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos speaks to members of the media during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images With the Denver Broncos primed to start training camp on Friday, we had a few early acclimation practices this week where the media got to talk with members of the team with Head Coach Sean Payton being one of them. There were a couple of things he mentioned that really stood out to me. The biggest being how he heaped praise upon new Broncos’ wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this week. I don’t think I’ve ever heard a coach refer to a player’s ability as ‘walking on water’ until yesterday. “There are certain prototypes at every position, and then there is that one where if they can walk on water… He’s one of those players relative to how he runs, how he stops and his competitive instincts.” Sean Payton “There are certain prototypes at every position, and then there is that one where if they can walk on water… He’s one of those players relative to how he runs, how he stops and his competitive instincts,” Payton said on Wednesday. “There is a clear vision for him. I think the knowledge we had with all the other pieces relative to a trade like that was important.” While Waddle is clearly not Jesus out there, what Payton clearly trying to imply is that Waddle is so dang good at what he does that he doesn’t really have to coach him. All Payton and his staff need to do is create opportunities for Waddle to break the big plays. Last season, this offense lacked consistency through the whole 60 minutes of a game. Whether it was the run game flailing about or the passing game misfiring for large stretches of the game, Waddle figures to help provide stability and consistency to help both find outlets. Defenses will be forced to account for Waddle, which should open things up for other wide receivers and also running lanes that would otherwise have stacked boxes. No player will benefit more from this addition than Bo Nix. He had to single-handedly put this team on his back in comeback after comeback last year. Hopefully we only have to see him do that a couple of times in the bigger games.

(Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Malcolm Roach is yet another of Sean Payton’s guys. He came over in 2023 like several others to shore up a team in need of better run defense. He’s been an excellent rotational interior defensive lineman for the Broncos who consistently provides quality situational snaps. Player Profile Malcolm Roach | Defensive Tackle | Denver Broncos Height: 6′ 3″ Weight: 290 pounds Age: 24 years old Experience: 7th season College: Texas 2025 stats: 41 tackles, 2 TFL, 5 QB hits, 4 sacks Contract 2026 outlook with the Broncos We’ll likely see Roach taking on more snaps this season with the loss of John Franklin-Myers. Roach is known for his run defense ability, but he’s shown the ability to generate a solid pass rush in one-on-one situations. This is often going to be the case with a line stacked with pass rushers like Nik Bonito and Zach Allen. Roach isn’t going anywhere for at least two years, based on what his contract looks like. I don’t know if he’s able to really turn up the number of snaps he’s on the field for, but if he can, I could see him earning another raise next offseason. Final Word I’m pretty bearish on Malcolm Roach having a breakout year. He’s going to be given every opportunity to show that he’s ready to take on a bigger role with the defense. I’m really curious to see what kind of rotation Vance Joseph cooks up with these interior guys. Roach has shown he’s an impact player, and it is time to see if he can do that with a heavier snap count.

title: Sean Payton believes this year’s Broncos squad can win the Super Bowl
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Super Bowl is the ultimate goal for every team in the National Football League. For some teams it’s a realistic objective. However, there are franchises where it’s simply just a talking point fantasy. Last season, the Denver Broncos fell short of that lofty ambition. This season, redemptions are in their […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 29: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos speaks after practice at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Super Bowl is the ultimate goal for every team in the National Football League. For some teams it’s a realistic objective. However, there are franchises where it’s simply just a talking point fantasy. Last season, the Denver Broncos fell short of that lofty ambition. This season, redemptions are in their sights, and the expectations are truly a mile high. A few days ago, shutdown corner Patrick Surtain II emphasized they have the coaching staff and players to hoist the Lombardi Trophy. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton took the podium to field questions from all sorts of topics. When asked about whether or not this year’s Broncos squad can win it all, Payton didn’t hesitate. He had a checklist of four criteria that gives him confidence as they prepare for the upcoming season. “Yeah, this is one of them. I think you have to play good defense to be one of those teams. You have to get good quarterback play. You have to be good on the offensive and defensive lines. You have to be well coached. I think we’re all of the above,” stated Payton. The Broncos were one of the best defensive teams in NFL in 2025. For the second year in a row, they league in sacks. Additionally, they allowed the third fewest points and were widely regarded as the best on third downs. Every starter outside John Fraklin-Myers is set to return this year. That continuity should help them help be one of the top units in 2026. With respect to quarterback play, we saw Bo Nix take great strides in his second season. Had he not gotten injured in Denver’s thrilling victory over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Championship game, the outcome of their season could have been much different. This year, Nix has a shot to cement himself as one of the game’s best quarterbacks. The Broncos added several playmakers into the fold via trade and the NFL Draft, which should bolster Nix’s play and the offense’s overall productivity this coming season. When it comes to the offensive and defensive fronts, those are Denver’s foundational building blocks. According to Payton, those groups help set the tone in games and have been a huge reason for their success. Several years ago, that couldn’t be said. Nevertheless, heir diligence and resource allocation in those areas the past few seasons have paid off—especially on the offensive line. “I think that room permeates the building in general, and I think that was an important goal of ours that first year. I think the depth and experience in that room, we have the veteran players that have been together,” remarked Payton. “Then with the influx of each year, some real good young players. I think it’s hard to find in free agency, and I think we’ve done a good job even in the later rounds or in college free agency.” Last but not least, the Broncos have assembled a phenomenal coaching staff. Quality players matter but having the right coaches to develop and set them up for success is equally as important. The Broncos have come a long way in a short period of time. A lot of that is because of Payton and his staff who have changed the team’s culture and infused the franchise with a winning mindset. Belief is a powerful too. Can the Broncos forge that mentality to reach the ultimate goal in ‘26? I can’t wait to find out. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: 4 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ ‘Inside the Den’ for 2026 NFL Draft
summary: Thursday evening brought on a surprise drop of “Inside the Den,” the Detroit Lions Emmy-award winning documentary series. The latest installment was a look back at the 2026 NFL Draft, and it provided for a lot of insight into the things that happened—and nearly happened—for the Lions. Here are a few of the biggest takeaways […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - APRIL 24: Former Detroit Lions Calvin Johnson waves during Round Two of the 2026 NFL Draft at Acrisure Stadium on April 24, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thursday evening brought on a surprise drop of “Inside the Den,” the Detroit Lions Emmy-award winning documentary series. The latest installment was a look back at the 2026 NFL Draft , and it provided for a lot of insight into the things that happened—and nearly happened—for the Lions. Here are a few of the biggest takeaways from this newest episode. The Lions feelings on Blake Miller changed their approach to Day 1 Every team’s media department has what very well could be their most difficult job of the year when it comes to producing a behind-the-scenes look of draft day. They comb through hours upon hours of footage, making sure not to unveil sensitive intel— like flashing a draft board directly to the media to make your point —while also looking to cut and edit things in a way that makes it appear as everything happened just the way your team had wanted it to happen. Franchise propaganda provides for a lot of hope, but even so, there’s a lot of footage here that shows the Lions were actually pretty high on their eventual first-round pick, Clemson’s Blake Miller. Brad Holmes and Dan Campbell were shown having a discussion about how—and when—the run on tackles would happen, with Holmes wondering if one would potentially go before the sixth overall pick. “Well, the good news is we got hot on Miller,” Campbell said just a few minutes into the time for Las Vegas to make their pick at No. 1. “You know, that [liking Miller] helped big time.” The Lions appeared to be content with a few names coming off the board at offensive tackle, but by pick No. 12, Detroit started to get active on the phone to ensure they’d come away with Miller. Holmes’ first call was to Eric DeCosta, the general manager for the Baltimore Ravens, who held the No. 14 pick. Baltimore’s asking price was No. 17, 118, 128, and a third-round pick in 2027. The Los Angeles Rams, sitting at No. 13, wanted No. 17, 50, and 118 for No. 13 and 93. Even the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had their price for Detroit to move up to No. 15: No. 17, 118, and 128 for No. 15 and 195. But once the Rams went with Ty Simpson, and the Buccaneers took Rueben Bain, Detroit felt confident that Miller would be there at No. 17. Who Detroit preferred to Miller remains to be revealed, but what’s clear is Miller was the player among the tackles they seemed willing to move up and make sure they left with on Day 1. “We do all the rankings, and when we started to dive into those tackle rankings, it really just kind of came very very clear that we’d love have this guy as a Lion,” Holmes said about Miller. “I can’t believe it worked out that way,” Campbell told to Holmes in the Lions draft room. “I mean, that was crazy. I thought all those tackles were gonna be gone. Got our guy and didn’t have to give up anything to do it.” “Not a damn thing,” Holmes added. No fourth round picks would come in between Holmes and Derrick Moore Much like Detroit’s first day of the draft, the Lions identified a player they wanted to come away with, but weren’t sure if he’d be available at their selection (No. 50). “You always reset and you have that stack, cluster of players that you would really like to have,” Holmes described about the process for Day 2 of the draft, “but Derrick [Moore] was at the top of that stack.” Prior to Day 2 of the NFL Draft, we see both Holmes and Campbell share their interest with Sheila Ford Hamp about Michigan’s Derrick Moore, identifying him as an intriguing player for tomorrow. But then when the day arrives, we hear Campbell spell out his interest more plainly. “We’d love to get the rusher from Michigan. He’s kind of our top target right now. There’s a lot of guys in there that are really good players we like, but that’s kinda because he can play d-end, able to rush, but you know, bring something we can use.” Initially, Holmes felt Moore would stick around until the Lions pick at No. 50, but once Kansas City took R Mason Thomas with the pick at No. 40, Holmes grew concerned with the number of teams after the Chiefs and before the Lions’ pick that had a need at defensive end. So much so that the video footage of Holmes and Campbell learning about the Thomas pick caused Holmes to shift in his chair and grab his phone—and Campbell to bite at his fingernail. “Derrick Moore was our No. 1 guy, we have multiple fours,” Holmes recalled of his thought process in moving up for Moore. “That’s why I felt like let’s not lose out on our top guy. That’s why we went ahead and just made the move up just to make sure that we secured them.” Detroit had their sights set on an undersized defensive tackle heading into Day 3 As the second day of the NFL Draft winded down, a few of the Lions staff gathered to discuss players still available for Detroit’s final selections on Day 3. Holmes throws out a hypothetical: “Would you take [Keith] Abney over [Kendrick] Law?” The Lions director of scouting, Dwayne Joseph prefers Law while Brian Hudspeth, the Lions director of college scouting, would be in favor of Abney. Senior advisory Don Corzine throws out his favorite player: Jimmy Rolder. While these three players would all end up getting selected by the Detroit Lions, Holmes asks everyone in the room to give him their “Halton, Rolder, Abney, and Law rankings.” As in Gracen Halton, the defensive tackle from Oklahoma. The San Francisco 49ers would end up taking Halton with the No. 107 pick, 11 spots ahead of Jimmy Rolder going at No. 118. If Detroit’s guy wasn’t at 118, Holmes was ready to move back “If our guy’s not there, then I’ll let you know,” Holmes told a member of the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers were willing to part with No. 123 and a pick in the sixth round according to the footage from “Inside the Den,” and Holmes reiterates to his staff that if the Lions’ top guy isn’t available at 118, he’s willing to move back because there were “five guys” that Detroit considered to be their top targets at this point in the draft. The Chargers would instead make that same trade offered to Detroit with Houston, sending No. 123 and No. 204 to the Texans for No. 117 to select Travis Burke, an offensive tackle from Memphis. That left the Lions with the prospect they’d been hoping to grab in Jimmy Rolder.

title: Detroit Lions teammates hopeful Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in ends soon
summary: On Thursday morning, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell spoke to the media and downplayed his concern about Jahmyr Gibbs’ absence from training camp practices, as he awaits a new contract. After practice, his teammates threw their entire support behind the Pro Bowl running back. “Jah’s doing what he can do,” fellow running back Sione Vaki […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 14: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions celebrates his touchdown with Jahmyr Gibbs #0 during a 41-34 loss to the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday morning, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell spoke to the media and downplayed his concern about Jahmyr Gibbs’ absence from training camp practices, as he awaits a new contract. After practice, his teammates threw their entire support behind the Pro Bowl running back. “Jah’s doing what he can do,” fellow running back Sione Vaki said. “He definitely wants to be out there. That’s something he wanted to emphasize. This isn’t something he do. It’s just a business. He definitely wants to be with his teammates, man. He’s that kind of guy. So, anytime we get to see him, we’re just loving him up, telling him, ‘Do what you’ve got to do.’” Gibbs is currently under contract through 2027 after Detroit exercised his fifth-year option this offseason. But he became eligible for an extension this year, and after putting together three straight Pro Bowl seasons, it’s clear he’s ready for his first big-time payday. [From Gibbs’ instagram page] same, Waymo. pic.twitter.com/jGHXpj0b36 — Morgan Cannon (@MCannon313) July 30, 2026 Amon-Ra St. Brown has a particularly valuable perspective on the situation. Not only is he very close to Gibbs, but two years ago, St. Brown was dealing with his own contractual negotiations that resulted in a four-year, $120 million extension. He’s hopeful Gibbs will join practice soon. “Jahmyr’s my dawg. I miss him out here. I think he’ll be out here hopefully sooner rather than later,” St. Brown said. “I talk to him quite a bit. Obviously, I can’t share with you guys everything, but I love Jahmyr. I miss him out here. Like I said, he’ll be out here sooner rather than later, hopefully.” But while St. Brown’s deal got done very early in the process—he signed his extension days before the 2024 NFL Draft—Gibbs’ negotiations have bled into training camp. Campbell admitted on Thursday he expected a deal to get done by now. “I thought we’d have been done by now, but I also know how this goes,” Campbell said. “I’ve been in this league a long time, player and a coach. So know how it goes. I’m not sweating it.” Detroit isn’t wasting their time with Gibbs’ absence. It’s been the perfect opportunity for free agent add Isiah Pacheco to get valuable reps in a new offense, and Vaki to get his first significant starter reps since joining the team in 2024. “We’re still out there practicing, doing our thing,” St. Brown said. “Guys stepping up: Isiah, Vaki, (Jacob) Saylors. So, getting other guys opportunities too to show what they can do. So it all works out for a reason.” Most importantly for Detroit, Gibbs’ absence doesn’t appear to be creating any sort of animosity in the locker room. He’s still at the facility, going through all the same meetings and other responsibilities. And as many players know, these negotiations are just part of life as an NFL player. “Obviously, we’re missing one of our best players on offense, which sucks, but he’s still in the building,” St. Brown said. “He’s still at all the meetings and everything. So, I think that the players understand what’s going on. Everyone kinda gets it as part of this business.”

title: Detroit Lions 2026 training camp observations, Day 2: 10 standouts from Thursday
summary: The Detroit Lions were back on the practice field on Thursday as they went through their second day of 2026 training camp. As the team continues through the acclimation process, they were able to add a bit more time to their practice schedule, and they continue to implement a lot of their base schemes. For […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill (54) walks off the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions were back on the practice field on Thursday as they went through their second day of 2026 training camp. As the team continues through the acclimation process, they were able to add a bit more time to their practice schedule, and they continue to implement a lot of their base schemes. For the most part, attendance was the same; no one was removed from an injury report, and no one was noticeably injured at practice. However, Giovanni Manu (who was placed on NFI on Wednesday night) and Payton Turner (dealing with a back injury) were both absent from practice on Thursday. Blake Miller locking up RT role, welcomed to the NFL For the second straight practice, Blake Miller started every first-team rep at right tackle, pointing to the fact that he is locking up the RT battle, if he hasn’t outright won the job already. Larry Borom has been exclusively with the second team—save operating as a sixth offensive lineman in big sets—and appears to be preparing for a swing OT3 role. While Miller has been solid through the first two days of camp, every rookie has a “welcome to the NFL” moment, and Blake Miller may have gotten his on Thursday. During 11-on-11s, Aidan Hutchinson lined up opposite Miller, giving us a glimpse of a battle we’ve been looking forward to for some time. Miller was square in his setup, and at the snap executed a well-timed drop, taking two fast steps backward into a pass pro set. Hutchinson took one strong step upfield, then unleashed his patented inside move and left the rookie leaning awkwardly in the wrong direction and grasping at air. I’m not sure Miller got a finger on Hutchinson as the All-Pro got into the backfield with ease. For the most part, Miller has been solid, but this play offered a solid reminder that he’s still a rookie and needs to gain experience like this to grow. Defensive line shows up during team drills Beyond Hutchinson looking strong, the rest of the starting defensive line had a great day overall. Defensive tackles Alim McNeill showed up in my notebook several times, earning positive marks for shooting gaps and/or getting pressure (Juice Scruggs struggled against McNeill), while Tyleik Williams also created pressure and showed the range to get out into space. Levi Onwuzurike was limited in practice on Wednesday, but on Thursday he was rotating with the first team at the three-technique and even took a handful of reps at the big end. While he was working a bit farther down the depth chart, it’s worth recognizing that Mekhi Wingo was also able to generate noticeable pressure, which is a good sign, considering we’re starting to see more reps for rookies Skyler Gill-Howard and Tyre West. DJ Wonnum also had a solid day, registering a sack and another pressure, while also jumping into a passing lane to disrupt a quick screen pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Tyler Lacy continues to get first-team reps at big end, but it was Ahmed Hassanein who showed up in my notebook for gaining pressures. Installing the base of the offensive playbook The defense certainly deserves a lot of credit for disrupting the offense on Thursday; it’s worth pointing out that the offense looked heavily focused on installing certain parts of the playbook. They restarted multiple plays after missed assignments or players lining up incorrectly, and coaches had to call players out on a few occasions. When running plays, several resulted in repeated outcomes—multiple screen passes, quick outs, etc.—but the offense arrived at them in different ways. They appeared focused on installing a variety of plays that would get them specific outcomes and wanted to execute them perfectly. Mixed in with the base installs, we saw the introduction of a few more playbook staples we expected from offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, including finding unique ways to get mismatches. My favorite, and most effective, of the day was using motion to get Jameson Williams matched up against Malcolm Rodriguez. Williams quickly chewed up the zone coverage and peeled off into the gap between the corner and the safety along the sideline for a solid result. Petzing looks like he’ll have a few fun wrinkles in his playbook that we haven’t seen from this offensive scheme in a few seasons. Cedric Wilson makes the catch of the day Greg Dortch looks to have solidified himself as WR4 and is mixing in with the starters, but the battle amongst the depth reserves looks wide open. On Thursday, Cedric Wilson made his case for the WR5 job. During 7-on-7s, Wilson set up on the outside and ran a quick out, which drew in defender Khalill Dorsey. Wilson then turned his route up the field in a variation of a wheel route, and while Dorsey did a nice job of sticking with him, Teddy Bridgewater took advantage of Wilson’s frame and placed a perfect ball on his outside shoulder. What initially looked like an overthrow ended up being a spectacular catch, as Wilson elevated and snagged the ball out of the air with one hand, landed in bounds, and scampered up the sidelines. 5 more standouts from Thursday Avonte Maddox had a terrific day, showing great breaks on passes and run plays, and also made a highlight-reel pass breakup, coming from range and elevating over St. Brown to prevent a big play. Derrick Barnes showed great instincts on Thursday, shooting gaps to generate pressures, as well as fake blitzing and dropping into coverage, with one of those drops resulting in the first interception of camp. Rookie Jimmy Rolder continues to rep at second-team MIKE and already looks surprisingly comfortable. He’s showing solid play recognition and even got credited with a would-be sack on a blitz. Jackson Meeks may have officially switched to tight end, but he still showed he can move like a wide receiver on routes. During 7-on-7s, he set up in the slot, drifted outside, hit a classic wheel route that left Erick Hunter in his wake, and was wide open running down the sideline. Unfortunately, Luke Altmyer missed the would-be touchdown and threw to the opposite side of the field. Sione Vaki continues to supplement RB1 duties with Isiah Pacheco and is looking to be as ready as possible for when his number is called. On one play, Vaki was given a choice route, made the wrong read, and was locked up by Malcolm Rodriguez. After practice, when every player had left the field, Vaki continued to work on his routes, dipping and cutting off blocking bags. “I’m just trying to gain the trust of the No. 1 guys and show that whenever they need me, whenever my number is called, that I’ll be prepared for the moment.”
author: Erik Schlitt

title: Lions safety Kerby Joseph optimistic about injury with help from his faith
summary: The saga of Kerby Joseph’s knee injury continues. A day after coach Dan Campbell said he wasn’t expecting the Detroit Lions safety for Week 1 of the regular season, Joseph talked to the media for the first time since midway through his injury-plagued 2025 season. Joseph finally gave some insight into how the knee injury […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The saga of Kerby Joseph’s knee injury continues. A day after coach Dan Campbell said he wasn’t expecting the Detroit Lions safety for Week 1 of the regular season , Joseph talked to the media for the first time since midway through his injury-plagued 2025 season. Joseph finally gave some insight into how the knee injury crept up on him last season, starting in training camp. “I woke up, it was swollen. I didn’t think nothing much. I was just like, ‘I can still run, do all of that. I’m finna go out there and practice.’” Joseph said. “We had scrimmage, but I’m running, I’m like, ‘Man, I ain’t that fast today.’ I thought—you know, I ate good that day. I’m thinking it’s a little breakfast or something going on. It’s not, my knee is just—I couldn’t, you know. I got the MRI, I got the news.” Joseph would battle the knee injury for the first six weeks of the season until things came to a head in Detroit’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs. In that game, Joseph had to go to the sidelines several times due to knee pain. He would miss the next few games. And after a failed attempt to return later in the season, Detroit shut him down for good. Since then, there there has been rampant speculation on Joseph’s NFL future, and the Lions haven’t made things much clearer. Campbell continues to say they don’t know how Joseph’s knee will respond nor when he’ll be ready for action. On Wednesday, Joseph was seen doing a pretty intense workout at training camp, and he followed it up on Thursday with a bout of confidence that things will turn out okay. “I’m super optimistic. I never gave up,” Joseph said. “I’m going to always work hard. All I do is work! If you see me outside, I’m working.” What’s clear from Joseph’s time with the media is that he’s keeping spirits high by relying on his faith. Earlier this offseason, he was baptised and it changed his perspective . “My baptism, it was like an opening,” Joseph said. “It opened a lot of things. God opened my eyes, informed me of a lot of things. I’m just so thankful for it, because if I never got baptized, I would never be able to see the things I needed to see.” He also referred to the last 10 months of battling this injury as his “walk with God,” noting that He is the only person who can truly help him navigate this time. As for when he expects to finally return to the field? “Whenever God wants me out there, I’m going to be out there. God don’t want me out there, I ain’t going to be out there.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions training camp Day 2 injury report: Bad news for Giovanni Manu
summary: After the Detroit Lions’ first training camp practice, the team made a rare roster move. Despite passing his physical and practicing on Wednesday, Giovanni Manu was placed on the Non-Football Injury list. That raised questions as to whether he got hurt after practice in a non-football setting or if something else was going on. On […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - OCTOBER 05: Detroit Lions offensive lineman Giovanni Manu (59) walks off the field after the game against the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals on October 5, 2025, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After the Detroit Lions’ first training camp practice, the team made a rare roster move. Despite passing his physical and practicing on Wednesday, Giovanni Manu was placed on the Non-Football Injury list. That raised questions as to whether he got hurt after practice in a non-football setting or if something else was going on. On Thursday, coach Dan Campbell gave some clarity, and it wasn’t good news for the third-year offensive tackle. According to Campbell, Manu had an offseason injury that wasn’t reported to the team, and he started to feel it again after practice. “We obviously put him on NFI. And he had an injury, a previous injury over the summer that was not disclosed,” Campbell said. “And so (he) came off the practice field, didn’t feel good, got it checked, sure enough, that’s what it was.” Campbell estimated Manu will be out around three months, which means he’s almost certainly going to start the season on the PUP list and miss at least the first four games of the season. “So, he will be out for a period of time. I don’t know how long that’s going to be; call it 12 weeks, 14 weeks. I don’t know, we’ll figure it out all down the road, but he is NFI,” Campbell said. Let’s get into the rest of the Lions’ injury report from Day 2 of Detroit Lions training camp. Not practicing: RB Jahmyr Gibbs ( not-injury related ) TE Tyler Conklin (PUP, calf) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) G Christian Mahogany (NFI) EDGE Payton Turner (back) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Gibbs continues his sit-in for the second day in a row, but Campbell emphasized that the team is not overly concerned right now. “At some point, it’ll all get done. It’s going to get done. I’m not even sweating it,” Campbell said. In Gibbs’ place, Isiah Pacheco and Sione Vaki continued to split time with the first-team offense. Tyler Conklin was estimated by Campbell to sit for two to three weeks, so we’ll likely see him around mid-August, assuming there is no setback. After working a significant amount on the training hill on Wednesday, it looked like it was a day off from field work for Mahogany. But Campbell suggested he could be back relatively soon. Juice Scruggs continued to work as the first-team left guard in Mahogany’s absence. Defensive end Payton Turner sat from practice with a back injury. But Campbell suggested it was not serious. “He’s got a little bit of a stiff back, so just got that, but we don’t think that’ll be anything serious,” Campbell said. Joseph also was not doing any field work after an intense workout on Wednesday. The Lions safety spoke to the media after practice, but didn’t offer much insight into his timeline for a return, and remained optimistic about his chances. “I’m super optimistic. I never gave up,” Joseph said. “I’m always going to work hard. All I do is work! If you see me outside, I’m working.” Branch continues to be outside with the team at practice going through mental reps, but he doesn’t appear ready for true on-field work with a trainer yet. Not practicing, but working on the side S Christian Izien (NFI, flu) Izien continues to look the closest to being able to return. For the second straight day, he was working with a trainer in a helmet and pads, as he works through the flu.

title: Detroit Lions rookie Madden 27 ratings revealed
summary: All 32 NFL teams have reported for training camp. What does that mean? Madden season is here! Seriously though, the football season is coming up soon, and a good way to get back into the football mindset can be by playing some Madden NFL. Madden NFL 27 comes out on August 13, and early access […]
full_text: All 32 NFL teams have reported for training camp. What does that mean? Madden season is here! Seriously though, the football season is coming up soon, and a good way to get back into the football mindset can be by playing some Madden NFL. Madden NFL 27 comes out on August 13, and early access starts on August 6, which gives fans just under 10 days until they can play the latest version of the video game series. Before the game is released, ratings get revealed for things like the 99 Club (which players are given the highest overall of 99), rookie ratings, and more. This gives fans an idea of who the best players and teams are before they load up the game. On Tuesday, Madden revealed all of the rookies’ overalls, giving Detroit Lions fans an idea of how good the incoming class could be according to the Madden development team. The ratings didn’t just include all the drafted rookies; undrafted quarterback Luke Altmyer made the list as well, since not every undrafted free agent is lucky enough to be in the video game series. Below is the full list of the Lions rookie ratings: EDGE Derrick Moore – 77 RT Blake Miller – 75 WILL Jimmy Rolder – 70 WR Kendrick Law – 70 EDGE – Tyre West – 70 CB Keith Abney II – 68 QB Luke Altmyer – 65 DT Skyler Gil-Howard – 65 When reviewing the ratings, I’m surprised Moore is higher than Miller, as usually first-round picks are some of the highest rookies for each team. That doesn’t mean that Miller was considered a bad pick by the Lions, but that Moore could’ve been taken higher in the Madden team’s eyes and is the best rookie of the class. Miller is the projected starting right tackle for the Lions, while Moore is seen as a backup for Week 1. That doesn’t mean by the end of the season, though, he can’t be starting opposite superstar EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. It was also interesting to see that a seventh-round pick in Tyre West got a 70 overall, as again usually the lower picks get the lower overalls for each draft class. The development team must also see something in Altmyer to include him as an undrafted free agent with the rest of the drafted picks. To compare to the past few years, here are some of the current players on the roster and their initial rookie ratings compared to what they were at the end of last season. Moore appears to be one of the top-rated rookies in Madden’s eyes for the franchise in the past five years, but he still couldn’t top wide receiver Jameson Williams. title: Detroit Lions ‘not sweating’ Jahmyr Gibbs’ contract hold-in
summary: As Jahmyr Gibbs enters Day 2 of his hold-in in the hopes of a new contract, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell isn’t too worried about it. When peppered with questions about Gibbs’ status with the team, Campbell downplayed any drama between him and the star running back. “You guys know how I feel about—how we […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - DECEMBER 25: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions warms up before the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Jahmyr Gibbs enters Day 2 of his hold-in in the hopes of a new contract, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell isn’t too worried about it. When peppered with questions about Gibbs’ status with the team, Campbell downplayed any drama between him and the star running back. “You guys know how I feel about—how we feel about—Gibbs and what the team feels about him. I’ll leave it at that,” Campbell said. “My job is to coach who’s out there right now. I love the kid, but I’ve got a team to coach right now. And, listen, whatever all this—at some point, it’ll all get done. It’s going to get done. I’m not even sweating it.” Gibbs is still under contract for two years—the 2026 season and his already-exercised fifth-year option for 2027. But this is typically when players drafted under this regime begin discussions with management on an extension. Gibbs’ draftmate, Falcons running back Bijan Robinson, is executing a similar sit-in over in Atlanta right now. Campbell showed compassion for Gibbs and his pursuit of a new contract, but he also admitted he thought the deal would be done by now. He joked that calling him the “bell-cow” back in the spring may have set back negotiations. “I shouldn’t have said bell cow, I guess, right? ‘Hey, well, coach said bell cow.’ Honestly, I didn’t even think twice about it. I didn’t think it would be—I really didn’t. I didn’t,” Campbell said. “I thought we’d have been done by now, but I also know how this goes. I’ve been in this league a long time, player and a coach. So know how it goes. I’m not sweating it.” As for when they’ll see Gibbs back on the field, Campbell didn’t have a timeline. He also said he didn’t have clarity on whether Gibbs would continue his hold-in even if the team doesn’t come to an agreement. But, still, there appears to be very little concern about that. In the meantime, Campbell talked about the silver lining in the running back room. Gibbs’ absences allow the opportunity to get free agent signing Isiah Pacheco some much-needed reps to learn the offensive system. It allows Sione Vaki to get the running back snaps he’s desperately needed since making the transition from safety. And it also bumps up depth players like Jacob Saylors, Jabari Small, and Kye Robichaux. “It’s a great opportunity,” Campbell said. “And, look, it’s one of the reasons we got Pacheco. This is extra reps for ‘Pop’ with us just within our system. So that’s awesome. Vaki gets these reps, Saylors, Small, Robichaux. But, yes, to answer your question, it’s great. It’s a great opportunity for him; it gives him more reps.”
