title: Blake Miller is on a mission to help fix the Lions offensive line
summary: The Detroit Lions made a huge investment in the offensive line this offseason. They signed Cade Mays to be their new center and drafted Blake Miller in the first round to become their future right tackle. Mays is essentially the unchallenged starter at center, but Miller has veteran Larry Borom to compete with at right […]
full_text: The Detroit Lions made a huge investment in the offensive line this offseason. They signed Cade Mays to be their new center and drafted Blake Miller in the first round to become their future right tackle. Mays is essentially the unchallenged starter at center, but Miller has veteran Larry Borom to compete with at right tackle. However, during the first day of training camp on Wednesday, Miller had already assumed the starting role, playing what appeared to be every first-team rep at right tackle, while Borom was reduced to reserve and jumbo formation roles. That’s a significant shift from the spring, where Miller and Borom split reps daily. And it could be a sign that Miller has already done enough to warrant the majority of the starting reps for training camp. “Definitely feel more comfortable. Things are coming a bit quicker,” Miller told media after the first day of practice. “That’s not to say that there’s still not more things to learn. I want to be able to just go out there; I want to be able to make the point in my head. Things just should be automatic. We’re still working to that point, but the guys that you have in that room, the veterans, and then coaches as well making themselves available, I have no doubt that I’ll be in a good spot.” Detroit’s investment in the offensive line was for a good reason. After a couple of years of dominant football, the unit took a significant step back last year. Jared Goff suffered a career-high 38 sacks (eighth most in NFL) and Detroit’s rushing success rate plummeted from 44.9% in 2024 (seventh) to 40.7% (21st). Asking Miller to step in and immediately provide high-level play is a lot for a rookie, but the former Clemson Tiger comes to the NFL with far more experience than most. He started a whopping 54 games over four seasons. And beyond that experience, he’s also bringing an all-in mentality. When asked if he feels like there’s pressure on him to help the offensive line reclaim its standards, he showed a clear devotion to doing whatever it takes. “As any player, it’s a duty to your team, it’s a duty to God, a duty to your family—whoever it might be—you have a duty to be the best player that you can be for your teammates, for your family, for everybody, for the city of Detroit,” Miller said. “I have a duty to be the best player I can be.” It’s far too early to say that Miller’s play on the field indicates he’ll be ready for Week 1. The pads have yet to come on, and Miller is still picking up the playbook. But with upcoming daily bouts against the likes of Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, and fellow rookie Derrick Moore, he’s certain to get a taste of the big challenges that await in the NFL.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Discussion: Should Lions fans be mad about Jahmyr Gibbs’ sit-in?
summary: Turns out the offseason rumors were right. The Detroit Lions opened training camp on Wednesday morning, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs wasn’t there on the practice field. He has officially reported to camp, as evidenced by a photo from the Lions’ media team, but at this point it’s pretty clear Gibbs doesn’t intend to actually […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JUNE 17: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions works out at mandatory minicamp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on June 17, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Turns out the offseason rumors were right. The Detroit Lions opened training camp on Wednesday morning, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs wasn’t there on the practice field. He has officially reported to camp, as evidenced by a photo from the Lions’ media team, but at this point it’s pretty clear Gibbs doesn’t intend to actually practice until there is some sort of new contract deal in place. While this isn’t the first time the Lions have found themselves in some contractual drama (remember Alex Anzalone last year?), this is the first time there has been a snag in extending a core player beyond their rookie contract while Brad Holmes has been in town. Typically, those deals have gotten done well ahead of time with literally no drama. Now, the Lions do still have a long runway with Gibbs. After exercising his fifth-year option earlier this offseason, the Lions have their star running back under contract through the 2027 season. But this is the time in which the Lions have typically given new deals to their best players still on rookie contract, so it’s somewhat reasonable for Gibbs to be making this negotiating tactic. So today’s Question of the Day is: Are you mad about Jahmyr Gibbs’ sit-in? If so, who’s to blame? My answer: At this point, I don’t think there’s any valid reason to be mad. Gibbs has missed a single practice, and it appears there’s been at least some progress in contract talks , as evidenced by Adam Schefter’s relatively optimistic reporting on the situation. If this thing lingers several weeks into training camp, that’s the time to be annoyed. Don’t get me wrong. It would be nice to have Gibbs out there for the entirety of training camp. I’d love to see him out there getting used to Drew Petzing’s new scheme, preparing his body for a more full workload, and I’d rather him not set this sort of precedent for other players in similar situations. However, I can also recognize that Gibbs doesn’t want to risk any sort of injury before getting paid. An NFL career is so fragile, and it can turn your fortune around completely in an instant. We saw how quickly the career outlook of Kerby Joseph changed last season, and there’s already been a handful of NFL players who have suffered season-ending injuries before the first week of training camp has ended. With running backs’ careers being especially short and fragile, I don’t fault Gibbs for trying to cash in when he can. It’s not an ideal situation, and I certainly understand those who are frustrated to see this happen after what has already been a pretty frustrating offseason. But until Gibbs actually misses significant time, I’m not too worried about it.

title: Packers to sign a former starting long snapper Cal Adomitis
summary: Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber is reporting that the Green Bay Packers will be signing long snapper Cal Adomitis and also confirmed a report that the team has signed receiver Kaden Prather on Thursday. As we mentioned in our story covering the Packers’ workouts today , the team brought in three long snappers following head coach Matt LaFleur’s comments that the team was planning on working out players at the position later on Thursday. On Wednesday, Gutekunst stated that Green Bay doesn’t believe that the injury to long snapper Matt Orzech (calf) is going to be a long-term problem, but that the team would search for a short-term stopgap while Orzech heals. title: Packers sign UFL champion receiver Kaden Prather
summary: The Green Bay Packers worked out 10 players on Thursday, including four wide receivers. Apparently, one of them took, as the Packers signed Kaden Prather, formerly of the Louisville Kings, to a contract, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Prather was a seventh-round pick of the Buffalo Bills last season before he suffered a hamstring injury […]
full_text: COLUMBUS, OHIO - MAY 31: Kaden Prather #10 of the Louisville Kings seen in action during the UFL game against the Columbus Aviators at Historic Crew Stadium on May 31, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Mowry/UFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers worked out 10 players on Thursday, including four wide receivers. Apparently, one of them took, as the Packers signed Kaden Prather, formerly of the Louisville Kings, to a contract, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport . Prather was a seventh-round pick of the Buffalo Bills last season before he suffered a hamstring injury that led to him being waived with an injury settlement in late August. With the UFL-winning Kings, Prather finished fifth on the team in receiving yards, posting nine receptions for 148 yards over nine games. Since Prather’s release from Buffalo, he had workouts with the Seattle Seahawks (October), Atlanta Falcons (December) and Miami Dolphins (December), but his tryout with the Packers was the first one that has been reported since he finished the UFL season. Kaden Prather was drafted in round 7 pick 240 in the 2025 draft class. He scored a 7.68 #RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 888 out of 3816 WR from 1987 to 2025. https://t.co/7SZiUxFwEH pic.twitter.com/kHMRTfInH8 — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 26, 2025 Currently, Green Bay’s only injury at the receiver position is to Brenden Rice, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. The Packers’ roster is full, meaning that Prather’s addition needs to come with a corresponding roster move. That move has yet to be announced. Back in 2025, The Athletic’s Dane Brugler ranked Prather as the 40th overall receiver in the class and labeled him with a free agent grade. Here was Brugler’s blurb on Prather: A two-year starter at Maryland, Prather was an outside receiver in offensive coordinator Josh Gattis’ pro-style spread scheme. He generated some buzz in NFL scouting circles over the summer, based on his 2023 tapes, although that seemed to cool — there wasn’t much of a jump in his 2024 performance. Working outside the numbers, Prather is a tall target who adjusts well to the football and does a nice job working back to help his quarterback. However, he is a non-explosive receiver with straight-line tendencies, lacking suddenness in his breaks and consistency downfield (two catches of 30 yards or more in 2024; none longer than 35 yards). Overall, Prather has a rangy frame with solid hands and speed, which certainly gives him a chance to stick in the NFL, but the lack of a true distinguishing trait will require him to find a favorable situation. In college, Prather registered 162 receptions for 1,966 yards and 12 touchdowns with West Virginia and Maryland. He started in 35 of the 48 games that he played, including 31 of 36 after his true freshman season. He only missed one game in his college career with an injury.

title: Packers Training Camp Recap: Keisean Nixon returns
summary: We’re learning a little more about the 2026 Green Bay Packers every day. Yesterday, we got a huge dump of information from the team’s first training camp practice. Today, more information was discovered about the Packers’ injury situation and their current depth chart. If you weren’t at training camp on Thursday, here’s what you missed. […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Keisean Nixon #25 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re learning a little more about the 2026 Green Bay Packers every day. Yesterday, we got a huge dump of information from the team’s first training camp practice. Today, more information was discovered about the Packers’ injury situation and their current depth chart. If you weren’t at training camp on Thursday, here’s what you missed. Injuries Keisean Nixon is indeed back. pic.twitter.com/6PBZxZlhwu — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) July 30, 2026 The Packers’ injury situation mostly stayed the same between Wednesday and Thursday. Green Bay’s reserve list is currently made up of: RB Chris Brooks (hamstring, NFI) TE Tucker Kraft (knee, PUP) TE Luke Musgrave (neck, PUP) OL Brant Banks (hamstring, PUP) DL Javon Hargrave (knee, PUP) DL Jordon Riley (ankle, PUP) EDGE Micah Parsons (knee, PUP) CB Kamal Hadden (ankle, PUP) LS Matt Orzech (calf, PUP) Beyond those players, the non-participants on Thursday were receiver Brendan Rice (hamstring) left guard Aaron Banks (load management day as he comes off a knee injury) and offensive lineman Jager Burton (hamstring). Burton was injured during Wednesday’s practice but stated that it wasn’t a serious injury. Cornerback Keisean Nixon returned to practice today after experiencing what head coach Matt LaFleur called “tightness” on Wednesday. Nixon was seen doing drills with a band around his thighs on Thursday. LaFleur also stated that the team hopes that Musgrave’s neck issue will “subside over time,” which doesn’t instill great confidence that the tight end’s injury luck will turn around soon. Keep an eye on that situation, as the Packers are short on roster-worthy tight end bodies already. Offense Starters in team: Love Jacobs Whyle (FB) Dafney (TE) Golden – Watson Morgan – Monk – Rhyan – Belton – Kinnard Sorrell – Brinson – McClellan – Brooks – LVN Zaire – Coop Nixon – Valentine Williams – X (Bullard came in at nickel) Cisse & St-Juste rotated in with the 1’s. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) July 30, 2026 With Banks and Burton out of practice and Zach Tom still not participating in team drills, the offensive line remained the same with the 1s on Thursday. Jacob Monk appears to be the next man up at guard, while Darian Kinnard has been holding down the fort at right tackle. The Packers’ premier two-tight end look right now involves Josh Whyle, who was called up from the practice squad in-season last year after he was let go from the Tennessee Titans, and Drake Dabney, who was called up for just the last two games of last regular season. It’s a less-than-ideal situation for Green Bay right now. Considering that the Packers don’t have full pads on yet, I wouldn’t make too much about individual player performances at this stage on offense, considering how much further ahead the defense is at this point in the season. Generally, the offensive side of the ball takes a longer time to gel. Defense #Packers rookie Brandon Cisse working individual drills. pic.twitter.com/wiGtbezdJO — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) July 30, 2026 As I see it, there are really two big position battles on the defensive side of the ball this camp, at least on the starter level. The first is on the defensive line, where the question is who the third starter will be next to Devonte Wyatt and Javon Hargrave. The second is at cornerback, where the question is who will start opposite Keisean Nixon. On the line, no questions are being answered so far, as Wyatt remains out of team drills as he comes off his ankle injury and Hargrave remains on the PUP list. Because of the injuries, we’ve seen back-to-back days of a starting line of Warren Brinson, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan, the three players most likely in the running for that third starting spot. At cornerback, though, Carrington Valentine was the “starter” with Nixon in several team periods on Thursday, a hint of how the Packers’ pecking order at the position looks in late July. For what it’s worth, even with Nixon out yesterday, Benjamin St-Juste has been primarily a second-team cornerback for the last two days. On Wednesday, rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse was getting looks over him with the 1s. During practice, linebacker Edgerrin Cooper dropped out of action but did not reportedly receive attention from the medical staff. In different periods, both Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper came in as Cooper’s sub. A name generating some buzz early on in camp is “safety” Johnathan Baldwin, who has a chance to make the 53-man roster this year as the fifth safety and backup slot. For whatever reason, Baldwin is getting looks in the slot ahead of Kitan Oladapo, who was the third option (behind Javon Bullard and the now-released Nate Hobbs) in 2025. Baldwin, who played the slot primarily at UNLV, recorded an interception in today’s practice. Special Teams The Packers don’t even have a healthy long snapper in practice right now, and they certainly aren’t going live in kicking periods, but rookie kicker Trey Smack went three-for-three today from the 25-yard line. Hey, we’ll take it.

summary: Christian Watson has spent much of the past two seasons answering questions about injuries and production. Fair. But I’d argue it’s also fair to shift the 2026 conversation about Watson away from counting stats and toward understanding what he brings to Green Bay’s offense. As Packers Wire recently posted, Watson has embraced the idea that […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Christian Watson #9 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball after a catch against the Chicago Bears during the second quarter in the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christian Watson has spent much of the past two seasons answering questions about injuries and production. Fair. But I’d argue it’s also fair to shift the 2026 conversation about Watson away from counting stats and toward understanding what he brings to Green Bay’s offense. As Packers Wire recently posted , Watson has embraced the idea that his role extends beyond filling up the stat sheet. His size-speed combo forces defenses to account for him on every snap, creating opportunities for everyone else in Matt LaFleur’s offense. That’s especially important because the Packers finally appear to know exactly who the core of their receiving corps is. After a few seasons of quite a crowded kitchen, we’re down to a comfy three-chef lineup. Watson, Jayden Reed and first-round pick Matthew Golden each bring distinct skill sets, giving LaFleur complementary weapons rather than a bunch of players competing for the spotlight. Watson stretches the field, Reed thrives underneath and after the catch, and Golden adds another playmaking ability at all levels. When defenses dedicate extra attention to Watson, those teammates stand to benefit. Reed should find more room to operate in the middle of the field, Golden could see favorable one-on-one matchups, and the running game may even face lighter boxes (though that is TBD). Those contributions won’t appear next to Watson’s name in the box score, but they can have a significant impact on the offense as a whole. I do expect Watson to deliver on yards and touchdowns this year, but that shouldn’t be the only measuring stick. If he stays healthy, the Packers may get exactly what they’ve been betting on all along: a player whose biggest influence comes from making life easier for everyone around him. title: Texans’ fans need to rally behind C.J. Stroud
summary: Every fanbase has a personality. An underlying tone that spans across seasons and generations, whether good or bad. Eagles fans are rowdy and demanding. Cowboys fans are arrogant and delusional. Browns fans self-pity. Raiders fans are proud and intense. Texans fans? Well, Texans fans are pessimistic. We’re always waiting for the other shoe to drop […]
full_text: Every fanbase has a personality. An underlying tone that spans across seasons and generations, whether good or bad. Eagles fans are rowdy and demanding. Cowboys fans are arrogant and delusional. Browns fans self-pity. Raiders fans are proud and intense. Texans fans? Well, Texans fans are pessimistic. We’re always waiting for the other shoe to drop and for the team to fall apart. This sentiment remains true even while Houston is coming off its first ever back-to-back-to-back Divisional Round appearances. The team’s potential has arguably never been higher, yet the sentiment around the team is impending doom. There’s too much “I’ll believe it when I see it” mentality for a club that’s competing at the highest level in the sport. Most of the fans would swap their team’s plight for Houston’s position any day. We’ve got a QB on a rookie contract, a defense that’s at the height of its dominance, and a young core powering the entire team. How does this mindset take hold? Well, over the years the lows have been… low. Multi-year rebuilds, incompetent front offices, and QB carousels have sown discontent among the fanbase. But now, the city has a legitimate reason to believe in the team, yet shows no sign of excitement, anticipation, or optimism. We as a fanbase should celebrate how far we’ve come in such little time. Or, should we give Jack Easterby a call to see if he wants to run it back. Much of this surrounds C.J. Stroud’s regression and woeful playoff performance. Has he declined since his rookie season? Yes. Has the situation around him not been perfect? Absolutely. Did he completely, utterly collapse during the playoffs? Certainly. All that is true and can’t be argued. What’s also undeniable is he has been at the helm throughout this unprecedented run. The offense isn’t perfect, but it is light-years better than what it was four seasons ago. For the number of years we’ve spent toiling and spinning our wheels waiting for a QB, we should absolutely get behind and support Stroud. The alternatives are 1) we tear down everything to roll the dice on a rebuild around a rookie QB, 2) overpay for an over-the-hill veteran whose own team passed on him, or 3) pay an exorbitant cost of draft and salary to acquire a top-end QB. All of those options pale in comparison to Stroud actually succeeding and being paid appropriately in two seasons. Fans, we are in the best-case scenario as is and, we need to embrace it. From a roster standpoint, he has everything he needs to succeed now. Houston has 20 of 22 starters under contract for two seasons. That’s an unbelievable accomplishment by Nick Caserio. For the first time in a decade, we should have roster continuity. Fans can go buy a jersey and know the player will be here next season. The roster is deep, possesses elite talent, and isn’t going anywhere. Reason to hope? Yes, but the fanbase has a reason to believe. I truly believe teams take on the personality of their fans. The fanbase can provide a player a longer leash given their sentiment and exclamation about him. Back in 2022, the Philadelphia Phillies signed Trea Turner to a blockbuster deal worth $300M over 11 years. Turner stumbled out of the blocks the next season and was met with immense criticism and booing. However, in the video below, you’ll see one fan’s social media post shift the fans’ mindset to cheer on Turner instead of booing him. Texans fans need to give C.J. Stroud the Trea Turner experience. The fanbase should rally behind their quarterback, not pile on more pressure than he is already under. The kid is 24 years old, he’s going to struggle at times, lose his composure, and feel the weight of criticism. He’s obviously a player who is deep in his own head and clearly pressing. Stroud is not the first QB to struggle under the bright lights and won’t be the last. This is not the time for fans to be calling for his demotion. We should instead be propping up Stroud and reveling in this short period where we have an above-average QB on an extremely friendly contract. What’s the point of being a fan if we can’t root for our players and embrace winning? Am I advocating for accepting mediocrity? Absolutely not. We have to hold hard-working talent to a high standard. But that standard does not have to come with negative criticism every time they underperform, even on the biggest stage. German philosopher Johann Goethe once said, “Treat people as if they were what they ought to be, and you help them become what they are capable of becoming.” I truly believe if this fanbase can pivot its worry and criticism into belief and support of the young star, it will turn his career around. We all win if Stroud succeeds.

title: Report: Colts work out former All-Rookie Team veteran  wideout
summary: According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Indianapolis Colts worked out veteran free agent wideout Chase Claypool, who hasn’t appeared in an NFL game since 2023: The 28-year-old former 2020 2nd round pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers also spent time with the Chicago Bears, Miami Dolphins, and Buffalo Bills organization during his initial 4-year NFL […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 29: Chase Claypool #83 of the Miami Dolphins reacts after a play during the second half of the game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on October 29, 2023 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Indianapolis Colts worked out veteran free agent wideout Chase Claypool, who hasn’t appeared in an NFL game since 2023: The #Colts worked out veteran WR Chase Claypool today. — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) July 30, 2026 The 28-year-old former 2020 2nd round pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers also spent time with the Chicago Bears, Miami Dolphins, and Buffalo Bills organization during his initial 4-year NFL career. His best season came as a rookie for the Steelers back in 2020, when he recorded 62 receptions for 873 receiving yards (14.1 ypr. avg.) and 9 touchdown receptions during 16 games (6 starts)—earning PWFA All-Rookie Team honors that same season. Claypool would follow that strong debut pro campaign up with a ‘sophomore season’ in which he recorded 59 receptions for 860 total receiving yards (14.6 ypr. avg.) and 2 touchdown receptions during 15 games (13 starts). Unfortunately for Claypool, his production would significantly dip after his first two seasons with the Steelers, before eventually and rather infamously being traded to the Chicago Bears for a 2023 2nd round pick, where he would never live up to that higher draft pick that was surrendered. Claypool couldn’t regain his prior footing in the Windy City and had a subsequent underwhelming sole season with the Miami Dolphins in 2023, before joining the Buffalo Bills in 2024, but never appearing in an NFL game again because of a significant toe injury. At 6,4”, 238 pounds, Claypool during his early career playing peak, was a big, physical possession wideout, who had the ability to separate vertically. In that regard, he was somewhat similar to recently departed veteran Colts wideout Michael Pittman Jr. in sheer stature and big bodied playing style. He was also a RAS darling coming out Notre Dame in 2020 with a 9.98 RAS grade out of a maximum of 10.0 , but whether he still has that peak athletic ability remains to be seen—especially having been out of football for two seasons and some quiet receiving seasons to end his initial career. It’s worth noting that he previously worked out for the Green Bay Packers in May of this year. It’s not as thought the Colts couldn’t use a potential wide receiver upgrade along the outside, especially with Alec Pierce still out of training camp commission for the next week or so. The projected starter on the outside opposite of Pierce, when he’s fully healthy of course, is currently Ashton Dulin and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. That being said, it seems like a longshot that Claypool can regain his prior early career form with Pittsburgh. This may be just an instance of the Colts doing an agent a solid or kicking the tires purely for due diligence purposes too see how much gas Claypool realistically has left.

title: Colts defense scores twice on Day 2
summary: WESTFIELD, Ind. — Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones sold the play-action before rolling right, looking to find tight end Tyler Warren in rhythm, but with defensive end Laiatu Latu chasing him down quickly, Jones released the pass just behind Warren, which allowed linebacker Austin Ajiake to undercut the throw and race the other way untouched […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts edge rushers Laiatu Latu and Jaylahn Tuimoloau speak between plays during training camp practice at Grand Park in Westfield, Ind. — July 25, 2025 | Thomas Butler-Guerrero WESTFIELD, Ind. — Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones sold the play-action before rolling right, looking to find tight end Tyler Warren in rhythm, but with defensive end Laiatu Latu chasing him down quickly, Jones released the pass just behind Warren, which allowed linebacker Austin Ajiake to undercut the throw and race the other way untouched for a pick-six. The interception was Jones’ first visible mistake of training camp, but it shows there are no limits on what he’s doing in another rather efficient practice. Jones continued to operate the electrifying run-pass-option style offense that — prior to his season-ending Achilles injury — went into last year’s Week 14 matchup in Jacksonville leading the NFL averaging 6.3 yards per play and 29.8 points per game. Jones started off hot with a few quick throws underneath before opening it up during 7-on-7 drills. He finished with a clean session while hitting Josh Downs on an out route, followed by a pass over the middle to Ashton Dulin. He also found veteran receiver Laquon Treadwell twice on dig routes and developed a strong connection with Warren, who fetched a handful of targets throughout Thursday’s team periods. Jones completed 7-of-9 passes and though he showed he can still orchestrate the offense, the defense made it just as difficult than it had a day earlier. Ajiake wasn’t the only defender to capitalize on a turnover opportunity. During the 7-on-7 session, quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. sailed a pass intended for rookie receiver Deion Burks. After Burks had to leap to just tip it in the air, it was cornerback Cameron Mitchell who caught it and returned the interception approximately 30 yards for the first defensive score of camp. Richardson responded in the final team session with perhaps his best throw of the morning. Off play action, he fired a strike over 20 yards downfield to receiver Anthony Gould, who likely would have absorbed a massive hit from rookie safety A.J. Haulcy had the pads been on. Second-year cornerback Justin Walley continued his impressive start to camp, showcasing his closing speed with a diving deflection on a deep sideline throw from Jones intended for Downs. Walley missed his entire rookie season after suffering a torn ACL during a joint practice in Baltimore last August, but the former third-round draft pick has looked comfortable while manning the vacant nickel spot during the first few practices. The secondary as a whole continues to prove why the Colts traded future draft picks to assemble one of the deepest position groups on the roster. Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo admitted after practice the organization has invested “a lot of capital” into the secondary, and the early competition has reflected that investment. Hunter Wohler once again worked with the first-team defense at strong safety, while AJ Haulcy, Johnathan Owens and Juanyeh Thomas continued rotating at the position during team drills. During the final team periods, Anarumo mixed his defensive fronts by deploying a five-man look featuring Latu, Colby Wooden, Adetomiwa Adebawore, Grover Stewart and Jaylahn Tuimoloau, who notably received his first extended work with the starters after veteran addition Arden Key opened camp in that role. Any physical evaluation of the trenches will have to wait until the pads come on next week, but through two practices, Anarumo’s creativity and exotic formations have players scrapping and clawing to earn their spot across the stampede up front. The Colts host a third straight morning practice at Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus on Friday at 10 a.m., then close the first week of training camp with a Saturday afternoon practice at 4 p.m.

full_text: We have seen players get PUP designation, which is generally one of the first legit pieces of information shared from the team. They let you know in advance why a player is not on the field. In our case, we had to be happy about a short list that did not include Buckner. Most were not surprised to read Pierce’s name on the list, but seeing our first pick in the draft added, did catch most off guard. Then you had to wait to find out what body part was the reason for the designation. The good news is that it appears to be a minor calf issue. It is not optimal, but unless is lingers for more than a couple of weeks, I’d say we have to be pretty pleased with the first report. From there, we get actually practices! No pads or anything, but it did offer the chance to see who got the initial 1st team reps. On offense, someone had to take Pittman’s reps and Dulin, somewhat expectantly got first dibs. Treadwell was also part of the 1’s, as a Pierce replacement was needed. The backfield and the O-line were all of the starters from last year. Whether Farmer can create a role for himself, may be the only question that will be resolved in training camp. AR did get 2nd team snaps over Leonard. On defense, even with Buckner not designated as unable, he didn’t take snaps. Wooden slid in there for now. I think we will see a lot of Limited Participation (LP) weekly designations during the season for Buck. Boettcher played Allen’s role, which highlights just how fragile the LB room might be. Pratt is still out there and shouldn’t be expensive, so pick up the phone! The CBs were as expected, as Walley moved into the slot with the 1st team. Wohlers got the first shot over Haulcey. Nothing against Wohlers and he was a darling of camp last year, but I’d be a little disappointed if Haulcey did not win role opposite Bynum. AP’s sidelined status, should provide a lot of opportunities to see if roles will go to our rostered players, or if an upgrade is required. I would guess that all of the WRs get a shot with Jones, as you may not be able to tell as much by what they do with AR and Leonard. As for AR, the outward line is that he is a valuable member of the team and that we still expect him to succeed in the league. How many fans really expect to see him succeed with us? If a starting QB goes down for another team, I have to believe that a 4th is offered and accepted. Speaking of QBs, I am probably burying the lead as DJ took first team snaps and showed no ill effects. If you are as optimistic as I am about the coming season, Jones replicating last year’s performance is paramount. I didn’t see a stat line, official or otherwise, but his movement was reported as a non-issue. It also sounds like Leonard was not sharp. Maybe he was bummed about being 3rd string? Camp won’t stop the speculation season, but does provide some tangible visuals and data to fuel the thoughts. Have you seen anything that might change your thoughts on the starters or the roster in general?

title: Chris Ballard just got out in front of the Colts with his latest contract talk
summary: It is hot outside in Indiana. As we complete July and head into the dog days of summer, everyone is feeling the heat. No matter how hot you get, no one is feeling it as much as Chris Ballard. At his press conference, he understands the pressure is on and only increasing. He just found […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts General Manager Chris Ballard leaves the Mike Chappell Media Room after he spoke to the press in a pre-draft press conference Monday, April 21, 2025 at the Colts headquarters, the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center. | Kelly Wilkinson/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images It is hot outside in Indiana. As we complete July and head into the dog days of summer, everyone is feeling the heat. No matter how hot you get, no one is feeling it as much as Chris Ballard. At his press conference, he understands the pressure is on and only increasing. He just found a release valve that is going to ease things a bit and gained the upper hand on the Indianapolis Colts in the process. Would you sign a two or three-year contract for millions of dollars? That’s the question. For you and me, the answer is yes, assuming everything is above board. Ballard said he wasn’t looking for an extension and would decline one regardless. In the last year of his deal, he feels he has too much to prove to sign one now, and it wouldn’t be good for the organization without results this year to back it up. He has been around a long time and believes no one puts more pressure on him than himself. See what he did there? He just set the stage. Some of you may be yelling how dumb it is to turn down an extension. Take the money! That’s assuming there is an extension to be signed. This type of rhetoric leads one to believe there is no current offer from the Colts, no deal at all. He has been willing to sign an extension before. Wasn’t he in the last year of that deal too? Maybe that had a fresh playoff win behind it, but the level of success hasn’t necessarily taken a tremendous dip. He knows without a shadow of a doubt this is it. I highly doubt ownership has plans to extend him before the season. If things go well to start the year, they might, but not before. If things fall apart and Ballard is shown the door, he can leave with some sense of understanding, or at least perceived understanding, that he was part of that decision. It’s like when someone at your company leaves and the corporate memo spins it, but you know they were canned due to performance. Maybe Chris Ballard is being noble. Maybe he feels he really doesn’t deserve it. I am not in his brain. I have, however, seen a lot of sports professionals cash checks they really shouldn’t get. He wouldn’t be the first or last to do so. Turning any potential offer from the Colts down would be foolish. The only thing more foolish is expecting us to believe there was an offer on the table to begin with.

title: Projecting Jonathan Taylor’s next contract
summary: Jonathan Taylor is actively having negotiations with the Colts on a 3rd contract with the team, one that would pay him handsomely once his current deal expires after this upcoming season. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jonathan Taylor is actively having negotiations with the Colts on a 3rd contract with the team, one that would pay him handsomely once his current deal expires after this upcoming season. After previous reports suggested that Jonathan Taylor would be a hold in during Training Camp, he reported fully on the first day of camp with a very positive update regarding his negotiations. Colts RB Jonathan Taylor says of his contract situation, “there’s been some good conversations” and “I have faith” in the team coming through with a new deal. — Stephen Holder (@HolderStephen) July 29, 2026 Jonathan Taylor on his contract, says there have been conversations: “I have faith things are moving in the right direction” — Joel A. Erickson (@JoelAErickson) July 29, 2026 All signs point to the Colts and Taylor’s camp having productive conversations and could reach an agreement prior to the 2026 season. Taylor himself has repeatedly expressed his desire to be a Colt for life, and the Colts themselves seem eager to keep their All Time Rushing TD leader and reigning 2025 TD leader (and likely soon-to-be All Time Rushing Yards Leader with another 1628 yards on the ground). "I would love to be a Colt for life." #Colts running back Jonathan Taylor is entering the final year of his contract, and wants to continue wearing the Horseshoe: pic.twitter.com/BA05a94flg — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) July 29, 2026 Ballard on still appreciating the greatness of Jonathan Taylor. pic.twitter.com/HhZISBlUT1 — Matt Taylor (@MayTayColts) July 28, 2026 So what could the deal look like? Currently Jonathan Taylor is on a 3 year, $42 million deal. He ranks 8th in Total Contract Value, 7th in Average Annual Value ($14 million per year), and 9th in Total Guarantees. For 2026 Jonathan Taylor has the highest Cap Hit in the NFL among RBs at $15.56 million, but by 2027 that number will be eclipsed by Christian McCaffrey, Kenneth Walker III, Josh Jacobs, Derrick Henry, and Alvin Kamara and by 2028 Saquon Barkley and Devon Achane do so as well. RB leaders in EPA per rush (2025, min. 175 attempts) 1. D'Andre Swift: +0.069 2. De'Von Achane: +0.059 3. Jonathan Taylor: +0.055 4. Javonte Williams: +0.048 5. TreVeyon Henderson: +0.047 6. Derrick Henry: +0.030 pic.twitter.com/G7uIhJ9YQB — Fantasy Points Data (@FantasyPtsData) July 27, 2026 Expect Taylor to receive an extension in the ballpark of Saquon Barkley and Christian McCaffrey’s deals annually. They are the two highest earners at the RB position and each got 2 year extensions averaging $20.6 million and $19 million per year respectively. He likely will get an average either in between this total, or just exceeding Saquon record setting figure per year. Their Total Guarantees were in $36 million and $24 million as well. The NFL's leading rushers by EPA in 2025: 1. Jonathan Taylor (18.8) 2. Blake Corum (15.9) 3. D'Andre Swift (15.4) 4. De'Von Achane (14.0) 5. Javonte Williams (12.2) 6. Rachaad White (10.4) 7. Kareem Hunt (9.7) 8. Derrick Henry (9.2) 9. TreVeyon Henderson (8.4) 10. Chris… pic.twitter.com/00U3nHQikf — Pro Football Network (@PFN365) July 25, 2026 Both Saquon Barkley and Christian McCaffrey signed these extensions at age 28 which is at around the same part of their career as 27 year old Jonathan Taylor right now. Albeit their deals were ahead of time to pay them in their age 30-31 year seasons whereas Taylor’s 1st year of his extension would begin at his age 28 season. NFL coaches/execs/scouts rank their Top 10 RBs: 1) Bijan Robinson 2) Jahmyr Gibbs 3) Saquon Barkley 4) Christian McCaffrey 5) Jonathan Taylor 6) Derrick Henry 7) James Cook 8) De’Von Achane 9) Kenneth Walker 10) Breece Hall ( @JFowlerESPN ) pic.twitter.com/caCfYzvARQ — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) July 6, 2026 Because of Taylor’s age at signing in the midst of a contract year, there is a chance his new deal would be more than 2 years. Devon Achane (age 25 when extended in 2026), James Cook (age 26 when extended in 2025) and Travis Etienne (age 27 when signed in 2026) all signed 4 year deals. Albeit Cook and Etienne signed theirs at $11.5-$12 million respectively. Achane got $16 million per year, but he got the lowest % of his contract guaranteed of any RB making over $12 million by a large margin at 27.2% ($24 million total guaranteed out of $64 million) and was the youngest RB of the trio, making his contract a more unique circumstance. With all that in mind, here’s what Jonathan Taylor’s contract is likely going to be in the range of based off of current RB contracts* (no based off of insider information). 2-3 Years $37.4-$43.3 Million/$56.1-$65 Million (Median: $40.35/$60.55 Million) $18.7-$21.7 Million Average Annual Value (Median: $20.2 Million) $17.5-$25 Million/$30-$ 45 Million Total Guaranteed (Median: $21.25/$37.5 Million) With the CBA increasing by $22 Million or $45.8 Million since Saquon Barkley and Christian McCaffrey’s extensions in 2024-2025, Jonathan Taylor has the opportunity to reset the RB market and be the highest paid RB in NFL history by exceeding Achane’s extension total, Saquon’s Average Annual Value and Guarantees. Being only 27 means a 3 year contract could pay him handsomely for the rest of his 20s as his deal would expire just before he turns 30. Jonathan Taylor, 2025 by the numbers: • 6.9 YPC running off tackle • 1,028 yards vs 6-man boxes • Positive EPA at every gap Load the box, doesn't matter. pic.twitter.com/JHsEybZnHQ — Outside Zone • Football Data (@OutsideZoneIO) July 27, 2026 But it isn’t a guarantee Taylor exceeds Saquon and McCaffrey’s contract due to his lessened receiving value compared to them, so he could instead on the lower end of his contract range he could be in between the two or just below McCaffrey’s deal as the 2nd/3rd highest paid back in the NFL. If the Colts end up giving Taylor a shorter deal, it is more likely going to be closer to Saquon/market topping deal. If its a longer deal, expect the per year cost to be lower and in the ball park of Christian McCaffrey’s deal or lower, as well as the contract to be front loaded to minimize the long term risk associated with a RB in his late 20s potentially regressing as most have at that age range. A 3 year deal could look like: 2027: $27 Million (highest paid RB just over Christian McCaffrey’s $26.4 Million under contract at this point*, currently 15 RBs with cap hits over $10 Million in 2027), $25 Million guaranteed. 2028: $17 Million (4th highest paid RB behind Kenneth Walker III, Saquon, and Achane under contract at this point*, currently 13 RBs with cap hits over $10 Million in 2028), $10 Million guaranteed. 2029: $10 Million (6th highest paid RB under contract at this point*, currently only 5 RBs with cap hits over $10 Million in 2029), $2.5 Million guaranteed. title: 10 Observations from Day 2 of Jaguars Training Camp
summary: After a Day 1 of Jacksonville Jaguars training camp that belonged almost entirely to the defense, Thursday brought a far more competitive practice to the Miller Electric Center. Depending on who you ask, the debate over which side of the ball came out ahead may be somewhat unsettled. Where Wednesday was a defensive showcase, Thursday […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - MAY 26: Wide Receivers Brian Thomas Jr. #7 and Parker Washington #11 of the Jacksonville Jaguars go through workout drills during OTA Offseason Workouts at Miller Electric Center on May 26, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a Day 1 of Jacksonville Jaguars training camp that belonged almost entirely to the defense, Thursday brought a far more competitive practice to the Miller Electric Center. Depending on who you ask, the debate over which side of the ball came out ahead may be somewhat unsettled. Where Wednesday was a defensive showcase, Thursday was a dogfight from start to finish. Both units dominated in different periods, and the honest answer on who won the day depends entirely on which stretch of practice you were watching. Here is a breakdown of the ten most notable takeaways from Day 2 of Jacksonville Jaguars Training Camp. Cole Van Lanen Looks Good on the Side Multiple members of the media in attendance were in agreement: starting left tackle Cole Van Lanen, who was placed on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list to open camp as he continues recovering from his Week 18 knee injury against Tennessee, is looking sharp working out to the side of the field. The team is reportedly managing his return deliberately, with the plan being to bring him along gradually toward an eventual return during camp, a timeline consistent with what head coach Liam Coen indicated during the offseason program. But his clearly spry mobility makes his return seem like more of a when, not if, conversation. Jack Kiser To Return to Camp The Jaguars announced Thursday that linebacker Jack Kiser will be back sometime in camp after undergoing an MRI on his right knee overnight. The injury was confirmed as on the minor side, and Kiser’s return is not expected to be a prolonged absence. Lawrence and Washington Heating Up The Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington connection is heating up, and Thursday gave the crowd two of the more impressive throws of early camp. A deep ball, sideline throw that Lawrence dropped perfectly into Washington’s hands with cornerback Montaric Brown in coverage was a clean display of the timing and trust the two have built up over the offseason. More importantly, Washington climbed the latter to bring the throw in, in a contested catch scenario. The moment that stood out most, though, was a deep sideline route where Lawrence beat the coverage to the spot with an exceptionally-timed throw, and Washington got both feet down inbounds in tight quarters. Otw to an endzone near you 😮‍💨 Free camp tickets: https://t.co/fhVdfYSB9O pic.twitter.com/z37tRb0JkJ — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) July 30, 2026 It was the kind of play that makes the extension conversation surrounding Washington feel like a formality. If there was an offensive player of the day award for each training camp day, Thursday’s would go to Washington. Josh Cameron Makes His Case The most impressive catch of the day, arguably, belonged to sixth-round rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron, who hauled in a diving deep ball from backup quarterback Nick Mullens that drew a strong reaction from everyone watching. . @Josh_Cameron34 is cooking at camp 🍳 @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/wF0cbWzhqN — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) July 30, 2026 Cameron followed that up with two additional catches during team periods and logged multiple competitive reps throughout the session. His most talked-about moment came on a deep out-breaking route against Travis Hunter, where the crowd and media in attendance were split on the ruling. Cameron made the catch along the sideline, but Hunter forced him out of bounds and the play was ruled incomplete. It was a good rep for both players: Cameron showing the contested-catch ability that made him a training camp name to watch, and Hunter demonstrating the competitive instincts at cornerback that the organization has been counting on. Travis Hunter Makes Plays on Both Sides Speaking of Hunter, beyond the Cameron coverage rep, he made his presence felt on offense as well, pulling in a 15-yard out-breaking route later in the session. The dual-contribution day is exactly what Liam Coen has described as the plan for Hunter in 2026, and Thursday was an early example of it playing out in practice. Brian Thomas Jr. Finishes Strong Thursday began as a quiet morning for Brian Thomas Jr. And then it wasn’t. After his slower start, Thomas erupted in the final two periods with three receptions of 20 or more yards, including one catch and run that would have likely been a touchdown in a live game. In many ways, it felt like one of those games where a player has no catches at the end of halftime, and you turn around at the end of the third quarter and they have a hundred yards and a touchdown on three catches. It’s those types of explosive plays that Jacksonville fans hope becomes a theme for his 2026 campaign. Defense Getting Hands On The Ball The secondary had a strong day, as a unit, even beyond the Hunter coverage rep. Cornerbacks Jourdan Lewis and Jarrian Jones each recorded two pass breakups. Meanwhile, linebacker Branson Combs turned in perhaps the most underrated rep of the day, running stride for stride with Parker Washington on a contested catch where initial appearances suggested a near-interception. The ball arrived with simultaneous possession, and Combs’ ability to hang with one of the team’s most productive receivers in a contested situation was a notable takeaway from a player looking to carve out a larger role. Linebacker Ventrell Miller closed out the day’s defensive highlights by picking off a Nick Mullens in a middle period. . @ventrell_miller with the user lurk 🎮 @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/c7gWb4DfZM — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) July 30, 2026 Rayuan Lane Draws Attention The three-way safety competition for the role behind Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray continues to develop storylines. Rayuan Lane had an interception on a Trevor Lawrence pass in the final period, a play that was ultimately called back due to a pass interference penalty on the underneath corner in coverage. While the flag took the “official” stat away, the play itself was hard to miss. It echoed the pattern from Day 1, when Eric Murray’s interception generated attention in a similar context. The safety competition has been one of the more compelling subplots of the opening two days. Milum and Pregnon Watch The offensive line work continues to generate questions worth monitoring. Wyatt Milum received extensive reps at right guard for the second consecutive practice, while Emmanuel Pregnon worked on the left side. The positional movement is worth tracking as the competition for the starting guard spots takes shape heading into padded practices. It’s unknown if these additional reps were a result of anything going on with starting right guard Patrick Mekari, who spent much of the early periods on the side. Cam Little’s Perfect Day Kicker Cam Little closed out the day going four for four on field goals, including a long of approximately 50-yards. That wraps up day 2 from the Miller Electric Center. Day 3 of Jaguars Training Camp kicks off on Friday, July 31 at the MEC: an exclusive practice for season ticket members. The Jaguars’ next open public practice is scheduled for Sunday, August 2, per the team’s official training camp schedule. See you there.

It wasn’t anywhere close to a sellout either. The official attendance of 61,946 is a bit generous, as there were plenty of seats to be had at the massive Coliseum. And the Packers didn’t think it would be much of a game. To hear Hall of Fame guard Jerry Kramer tell it years later, they viewed the Chiefs as somewhat of a joke. In terms of per-game production, he has flashed elite fantasy upside—he averaged almost 10 targets, over 70 receiving yards and 18.5 PPR points per game in 2025. That last number was fifth among wide receivers. These five 2026 opponents are still searching for their first win over Patrick Mahomes | Arrowhead Addict Mahomes against the 49ers The Chiefs and Mahomes will host the 49ers in Week 16 this season, two days after Christmas. By then, both teams expect to be in the thick of the playoff race once again. Of course, we had to look back at Mahomes’ outings against the 49ers first. Two of his three Super Bowl wins have come over San Francisco. Court delays for son of Chiefs coach accused of shooting his mom delayed pending mental health check | Associated Press Bieniemy remained in the Loudoun County Adult Detention Center on Thursday. He had a court date to hear motions scheduled for later in the day, and a preliminary hearing date had been set for Aug. 31. But both appearances have been continued pending a mental health evalation, according to records available from the Virginia judiciary system. Around the NFL ‘Disrespected’ Baker Mayfield voices displeasure over lack of new Bucs contract: ‘Very disappointing’ | NFL.com Mayfield is relishing the opportunity, which he knows could lead to a lucrative opportunity elsewhere as a free agent in 2027. “If you’ve waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback, that’s too bad because it’s only going to get worse from here,” Mayfield said. “I’m going to have a really good year.” A great year could command entry into the $50 million-per-year club, a desire Mayfield made known Thursday when speaking with ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Deebo Samuel returning to 49ers on 1-year deal | ESPN The one-year deal is worth up to $7 million, sources said. Samuel returns to a 49ers team that drafted him in the second round in 2019. He spent six seasons in San Francisco before playing last year with the Washington Commanders. Receiver is a position of need for the 49ers, who are dealing with injuries to Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk early in training camp. Police say Tony Romo had open alcoholic beverage in car during OWI arrest | The Athletic Romo received three citations, according to the police documents obtained by The Athletic , including for operating while intoxicated after he was arrested on suspicion of that offense on July 23. Romo was given a second citation after a deputy observed an open alcoholic beverage “on the passenger side of a vehicle when an inventory of the vehicle was conducted” because it was being towed. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs training camp: Excitement for revamped screen game is brewing As camp moves forward, the use of Walker in the screen game should continue to be monitored; he has the explosiveness in the open field that makes screen plays worth calling, to a much higher degree than Kansas City’s backfield was able to offer before. “He’s a dynamic player,” Humphrey said about Walker. “Freak athlete, great with his reads, everything like that.” After Wednesday’s practice, Walker talked about learning the balance between patience and explosiveness as a runner from doing it over and over in football from an early age, working with his father. title: Chiefs training camp: Excitement for revamped screen game is brewing
summary: Through the first two days of Kansas City Chiefs full-team practices at training camp, there has been little opportunity for running back Kenneth Walker to showcase his skills. In the “acclimation” period spanning the first three days of camp, the Chiefs don’t wear full pads, limiting the run-game work. On a few occasions, Walker has […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JUNE 09: Kenneth Walker #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs carries the ball during mandatory minicamp at The University of Kansas Hospital Arrowhead Training Complex on June 09, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through the first two days of Kansas City Chiefs full-team practices at training camp, there has been little opportunity for running back Kenneth Walker to showcase his skills. In the “acclimation” period spanning the first three days of camp, the Chiefs don’t wear full pads, limiting the run-game work. On a few occasions, Walker has flashed in the pass game. On Thursday, one particular play had quarterback Patrick Mahomes “excited,” according to Jesse Newell of The Athletic . Most excited we saw Patrick Mahomes today was when offense caught defense off-guard with a screen pass to Kenneth Walker III that went for big gain. Could hear him cheering on the play all the way from media tent. Interested to see how much screen game Walker will help KC unlock — Jesse Newell (@jessenewell) July 30, 2026 It looked to be a timing screen for Walker, with Mahomes buying the appropriate amount of time for offensive linemen to set up in lead-blocking positions in the right flat. Mahomes delivered the pass, and Walker followed right guard Trey Smith, among others, down the field for an explosive play. Observing practice, it was definitely a highlight of Thursday’s session, but the team worked on screens during Wednesday’s practice as well. Center Creed Humphrey talked about the attention that goes into working on the screen game on Thursday. “Just focusing on the details in practice,” Humphrey said at the podium. “Locking down exactly what we need to do, exactly what we’re trying to accomplish with each screen. Really, just get the reps with the new backs… to get that cohesion.” As camp moves forward, the use of Walker in the screen game should continue to be monitored; he has the explosiveness in the open field that makes screen plays worth calling, to a much higher degree than Kansas City’s backfield was able to offer before. “He’s a dynamic player,” Humphrey said about Walker. “Freak athlete, great with his reads, everything like that.” After Wednesday’s practice, Walker talked about learning the balance between patience and explosiveness as a runner from doing it over and over in football from an early age, working with his father. “I feel like it helps the offensive line,” Walker said of that skill. “Sometimes, you have to be fast, but other [times], you have to be patient and let the blocks develop, then hit the hole.” Head coach Andy Reid’s screen game has been mostly dormant since he was able to deploy running backs Jamaal Charles or Brian Westbrook as elusive playmakers in space. Walker has a chance to bring life back to one of the strongest features in Reid’s offensive scheme.

title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 2: An Offensive line shift
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ second full-team practice of training camp took place on a gloomy day in St. Joe, one that turned to a downpour by the time the Chiefs wrapped up practice with punt-team work. The Arrowhead Pride staff had boots on the ground to observe the second of three acclimation-period practices before full […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Josh Thompson #62, Pete Nygra #50 and Kahlil Benson #70 walk toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ second full-team practice of training camp took place on a gloomy day in St. Joe, one that turned to a downpour by the time the Chiefs wrapped up practice with punt-team work. The Arrowhead Pride staff had boots on the ground to observe the second of three acclimation-period practices before full pads come on Saturday. Here’s what to know from Thursday’s practice in St. Joe: Attendance report For the second consecutive day, wide receiver Rashee Rice and cornerback L’Jarius Sneed partially participated in practice due to planned rehabilitation. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott continues to be on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, not participating in practice. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane continued to participate in all phases of practice while wearing a yellow, non-contact jersey. Lineup notes A shift on the offensive line After veteran Jaylon Moore played right tackle for every starting snap on Day 1, rookie Kahlil Benson took the reins on Day 2. “Really hard worker,” Center Creed Humphrey described Benson after practice at the podium. “He’s a very hard worker; you can tell it’s important to him. He shows up every meeting, every walkthrough, every lift, everything with the right mindset. “He’s a really strong player,” Humphrey went on. “From a physical standpoint. His punching power, things like that, he’s really strong and really technical too. So we’re excited about him.” While Benson played right tackle with the first team, Moore manned the left tackle spot on the second-team offense while Esa Pole moved from left to right tackle for backup quarterback Justin Fields’ plays. Second-year left tackle Josh Simmons continued to man the blind side for quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Humphrey also commented on his prospects. “Josh’s potential is through the roof,” Humphrey said. “If he keeps working the way he is, he’s going to be a very talented player in this league.” Experimentation on defense During the first day of practice, safety Christian Roland-Wallace appeared to man the Nickel role the most for the Chiefs’ starting defense. Chamarri Conner has been manning the strong safety spot, alongside veteran free safety Alohi Gilman, but defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo provided some clarity on that spot. “[Conner] hasn’t played as much Nickel; he’s played more safety, but that’s really to get some of the other guys ready,” Spagnuolo said to reporters after Thursday’s practice. “I think we can always put him back there in a pinch, but this gives him a little bit more time deep that he didn’t have last year. I think we’ll still have some flexibility with him at both positions.” It speaks to the rotation we saw on Day 2 in practice, where free-agent signing Kader Kohou appeared to man the Nickel role more often than he did on Day 1. In the same breath, rookie Jadon Canady appeared to see more time with the third-team defense than the first-team unit, but was still active, making at least one pass breakup on a route from the slot against the third-team offense. Third-year safety Jaden Hicks has primarily watched Conner and Gilman work on the Chiefs’ starting defense, getting his reps with the second-team unit — although we haven’t seen any Dime defense from Kansas City in camp yet. Spagnuolo talked about the plan for Hicks. “Jaden played a lot of different spots last year,” Spagnuolo said. “I told him, back in the OTAs, I’d like to find one that he can just hone in on and master that while we experiment with some of the other guys. He is a guy that we’ve had a little versatility with a year ago or the last two years; that won’t change, we’ll just find out where he’s going to get slotted in.” Defensive end Ashton Gillotte is one of the patients for Spagnuolo’s defensive experiments. He has been playing a de facto Linebacker role on the ball to present a five-man front for the Chiefs’ defense, but the mad hatter is simply pushing the limits of his group, seeing what he can learn. “We’re experimenting with a bunch of things,” Spagnuolo said when asked about Gillotte.“We’ll do that with him, (linebacker) [Cooper McDonald]… unfortunately, we know Ethan Downs got hurt; he was another guy.” “I’d like to be able to see if there’s anybody in the defensive line group that can do other things,” Spagnuolo went on. “Just like… we’d take (former Chiefs linebacker) Leo [Chenal] and put him with the defensive line every once in a while, so this is part of finding the versatility in guys.” Other notes from practice Mahomes continued to shake rust off, looking to push the ball downfield more in this practice compared to the first. On one early throw in the seven-on-seven period, Mahomes put up a long ball to wide receiver Xavier Worthy towards the back corner of the end zone that landed in Worthy’s hands, but slightly out of bounds with cornerback Nohl Williams in tight, trailing coverage. Williams has been in Worthy’s hip pocket constantly through two days of work. On one red-zone pass play, Mahomes worked through his progression to a back-side route, but Williams was there to undercut it and secure an interception. Worthy and Mahomes found the deep-ball chemistry on one blitz-beating play; Worthy burned Kohou deep out of the slot without safety help, jogging after the catch the rest of the way into the end zone for a big-play touchdown. Tight end Jared Wiley continues to get a lot of work with the first-team offense, but on one play, he let a pass slip through his grasp, resulting in an interception for Mahomes against the starting defense. Backup quarterback Justin Fields was on point with his downfield passes on Thursday. One of his only off-target throws was to wide receiver Cyrus Allen, who made a spectacular catch on an in-breaking, intermediate route where the ball was severely behind him. “He’s eager to learn,” wide receiver Tyquan Thornton said of Allen after practice. “His route running is elusive; he’s very good at the catch point.”

title: Chiefs News: Mark Donovan reveals big plans for new Kansas City stadium
summary: The latest Before the Chiefs held their first full squad training camp practice at Missouri Western State University, team president Mark Donovan addressed the media. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: A general overall aerial view of Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2023 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kirby Lee/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest Before the Chiefs held their first full squad training camp practice at Missouri Western State University, team president Mark Donovan addressed the media. Predictably, the bulk of Donovan’s time was spent on the Chiefs’ new stadium set to open in 2031 in Kansas. Donovan anticipates the design of the domed field will be conducive to maintaining a natural grass field. The Chiefs also have eyes on hosting a Super Bowl and other high profile sporting events, such as the NCAA basketball tournament’s Final Four. A separate training facility in Olathe will potentially be the site of future training camps, but the Chiefs are committed to St. Joseph for at least five more seasons. Super Bowl in KC? Chiefs talk stadium possibilities | FOX 4 The Chiefs are also working with the NFL to bring a Super Bowl to Kansas City. Donovan said the franchise is discussing the possibility of hosting the league’s championship game in 2033, 2034 or 2035. The Chiefs president said he told Visit KC and Kansas City Sports Commission President and CEO Kathy Nelson that they’re going to be very aggressive in bidding on major events. “We’re probably going to be early bidders on most things,” Donovan said during the news conference. Chiefs remain committed to St. Joe through 2031; New Olathe facility could host training camp | KSHB On Wednesday, Donovan said the team’s new facilities in Olathe, which are slated to open ahead of the 2031 NFL regular season, will be designed with the ability to host future training camps. “With the training facility being built in Olathe, we as an organization have to look at everything we do with options,” Donovan said. “That training facility is going to be designed with the ability to host a training camp. We have to have that option.” Donovan said the club would review their training camp options starting around 2029-2030, with the decision based on a variety of factors, some as simple as whether the team’s head coach wants to hold training camp away from the normal facility. Five Observations from Wednesday’s Practice | The Mothership 3. Rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier recorded a pair of impressive throws. Nussmeier, a seventh-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made one of the plays of the day during an 11-on-11 segment when he rolled to his left and fired a rocket on the run toward tight end Jake Briningstool, who hauled in a toe-tap grab near the sideline. It was a great all-around play by Nussmeier, who later tallied a no-look completion to tight end Tre Watson over the middle during 7-on-7 drills. Three Patrick Mahomes observations from early Chiefs practices | The Athletic The brace will be an adjustment Mahomes said Friday that he felt comfortable playing with a knee brace after using one during part of his college career at Texas Tech. This much became clear in two practices, though: He still will need time to get used to this particular support around his left knee. While recording videos of Mahomes, I was struck by how many times he reached over to adjust the bulky brace. Sometimes, it would be a quick adjustment. Other times, he’d mess with multiple straps, pulling and tugging until he got them into a better position. 2026 NFL All-Rookie Team projections: 25 impact newcomers on offense, defense and special teams | NFL.com CB Mansoor Delane, Kansas City Chiefs DRAFTED: Round 1, No. 6 overall After both of the Chiefs’ starting cornerbacks joined the Rams — Trent McDuffie via trade, Jaylen Watson in free agency — Kansas City vaulted up the draft board for Delane. This prospect crop’s consensus CB1 was a true lockdown artist for LSU last season. According to PFF, he allowed just 165 yards over 11 games, posting a 31.3 passer rating against. (Reminder: Spiking the ball every play would produce a passer rating of 39.6.) Around the NFL Star RBs Robinson, Gibbs appear to be hold-ins while seeking deals | ESPN Neither Robinson nor Gibbs was participating Wednesday with the Atlanta Falcons or Detroit Lions, respectively, in the first training camp practice for both teams. Both players have had conversations with their teams this offseason about potential long-term contracts. Both players are expected to reset the running back market with their deals. The Philadelphia Eagles’ Saquon Barkley is currently the NFL’s highest-paid running back, with his contract worth an annual average of $20.6 million. Saints DT Bryan Bresee feared to have suffered torn ACL | NFL.com Tests are ongoing, but it’s likely the 2023 first-rounder will be ruled out for the season, Rapoport noted. Saints head coach Kellen Moore told WWL Radio that Bresee appeared to suffer a non-contact injury during one of the early team periods. Moore couldn’t confirm the exact injury, but said “it doesn’t look great.” The No. 29 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Bresee hasn’t lived up to the lofty draft status, but has flashed some improvement the past two years. The 24-year-old was poised to play a key role along Brandon Staley’s defensive line. 49ers WR Ricky Pearsall dealing with knee swelling; the team has ‘some concern’ | Yahoo Sports On Wednesday, it was reported that wide receiver Ricky Pearsall is dealing with knee swelling stemming from the PCL injury he suffered during the 2025 season. San Francisco is reportedly exploring “all options” and that there is “some concern” around the injury. The Pearsall news comes on the heels of fellow wideout Christian Kirk being diagnosed with a calf injury. The 49ers’ wide receiver corps is already dealing with injuries, a theme that lasted throughout their 2025 campaign. In a statement from his family, they said the dementia was CTE-related. “To know Billy Ray was to love Billy Ray. Yes, he […]
full_text: The Chargers and the entire fan base is mourning the loss of franchise legend Billy Ray Smith who passed away on Wednesday at the age of 64 after a bout with dementia. In a statement from his family, they said the dementia was CTE-related. “To know Billy Ray was to love Billy Ray. Yes, he was a member of our 50th Anniversary team. Yes, he was a Charger for life, playing his entire 10-year career here,” said Chargers owner Dean Spanos. “But he wasn’t merely a great football player. He was, truly, larger than life. Always smiling. Lighting up every room he walked into. Infectious laughter. The kind of friend a friend should be. That was Billy Ray.” to know Billy Ray was to love Billy Ray 💙 pic.twitter.com/sFx8gM8eUX — Los Angeles Chargers (@chargers) July 30, 2026 Smith was a 10-year NFL veteran who spent his entire career with the Chargers from 1983-1992. He was taken with the fifth-overall pick in the 1983 NFL Draft after a standout career at the University of Arkansas where he was a two-time unanimous All-American for the Razorbacks. With the Bolts, Smith was as reliable as they come in the middle of their defense. He played in 11 of 126 regular season games and was twice named the team’s defensive player of the year (1986-1987). In ‘87, he was flat out named the MVP of the entire team. By the end of his career, Smith had accumulated 598 tackles, 26.5 sacks, 15 interceptions, and 14 fumble recoveries. All of our thoughts and condolences are with his family.
