title: Will Puka Nacua be first $50 million receiver?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are content with letting Puka Nacua play this season without a contract extension, with the 2027 franchise tag as a fail safe plan, but is it a decision that will cost them millions of dollars in future cap space? Based on early training camp reports of Nacua looking better than ever, […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the Los Angeles Rams Training Camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are content with letting Puka Nacua play this season without a contract extension, with the 2027 franchise tag as a fail safe plan, but is it a decision that will cost them millions of dollars in future cap space? Based on early training camp reports of Nacua looking better than ever, and his motivation to prove that he will not become a headache again, the Rams’ hesitancy to commit now could end up leading to the first $50 million per year receiver contract in history. As opposed to attempting to settle with Nacua for $43 million in average salary today. Is it worth it? Puka Nacua no contract now NFL Networks’ Ian Rapoport reported this week that Nacua is “focused on improving off the field” and that a “contract extension is more likely to be a discussion for next season”. From The Insiders on @NFLNetwork : #Rams WR Puka Nacua is focused on improving off the field, which is one reason why a contract extension is more likely to be a discussion for next offseason — not this training camp. pic.twitter.com/yBAuW2rsLo — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) July 29, 2026 If the Rams allow Nacua to go through the entire 2027 season without a new deal, he will become an unrestricted free agent in 2027. 2027 franchise tag The 2027 franchise tag for a receiver is projected to be $31.5 million . If that sounds like a discount to you because of the average annual salary of Jaxon Smith-Njigba ($42 million), it’s not. Because the Rams can’t spread that $31 million over multiple seasons. They have to swallow it whole in 2027, a year in which they have too many free agents to sign. Fans should expect that the franchise tag would only be used in case of emergency, and as a last-ditch effort to buy time before coming to an extension agreement with Nacua before the deadline. But spending $31 million in cap space on Nacua next season would not be the plan. Justin Jefferson looming The Saints signed Chris Olave to a four-year, $132 million contract on Thursday, but right now Nacua would be worth much more than that. Nacua would instead focus on the four-year, $168.6 million deal signed by Smith-Njigba. That’s more of the benchmark for an elite, All-Pro caliber receiver. For now. Next season, Justin Jefferson is due to make $49 million in salary. The most-ever to a receiver. Which is probably while the Minnesota Vikings could go back to the table to talk extension again, three years after extending Jefferson to a four-year, $140 million deal. Money that looks paltry for a player of Jefferson’s caliber. Assuming Jefferson gets better QB play to work with in 2026, he could end up having a career-year. Maybe even challenging for 2,000 yards. If that happens, Jefferson will be trying to get a four-year, $200 million contract. The first receiver to ever make $50 million per season . If the Rams wait to pay Nacua after Jefferson’s extension, and Nacua has a career-year, the Rams may end up paying Nacua $7-$10 million more per season than they could get him for right now. Nacua having a great camp To nobody’s surprise, early camp reports about Nacua have been glowing. If you had any concerns about Puka Nacua – by all accounts he is still just destroying camp coming off his rehabilitation stint Take: He’s my WR1 for 2026 Via @NateAtkins_ pic.twitter.com/vBggknYHQW — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) July 30, 2026 Coming off of a season in which he led the NFL in catches (129) despite missing a game, Nacua could set a new franchise record for receiving yards in a single year. Matthew Stafford has no reason not to do it. Nacua also says that he recognizes his off-field mistakes, takes responsibility, and will look to grow from this experience. And who wouldn’t? Nacua’s mistakes could end up costing him hundreds of millions in earnings if he doesn’t put it in the past and keep it there. Maturity: Rams WR Puka Nacua says he's learned from his offseason mistakes and that they don't reflect who he is. He will be closing his circle of trust and implementing a better support system, including his mother and brothers. A true role model on and off the field 👏 pic.twitter.com/Iog4v5iSfl — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) July 30, 2026 For an offense so clearly designed to feed him the ball, Puka Nacua looks on track for a career-best season and he will still only be 25 when it’s time for a franchise tag in 2027. Are the Rams making a mistake? Possibly. If Nacua comes out in Week 1 against the 49ers and puts on a show for 200 yards, the time for discounts is over. All it takes is a hot start and Nacua will have $50 million per year in his sights. The Rams can tag him and try to pay him $31.5 million for one season, but with so many free agents, can they afford to do that? And if Nacua has another great season in 2027, the tag in 2028 will be beyond Nacua’s wildest dreams. They’ll end up paying him even more. However, there is the risk that Nacua will get injured, or have more immaturity issues, or simply not be worth the $50 million AAV price tag. There are no easy answers here, but there is one predictable outcome: With how he’s looking so far this camp, Puka Nacua can line himself up for a post-Jefferson pay day over $200 million. How much longer can the Rams afford to wait?
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Stetson Bennett is fighting for more than a backup spot
summary: Everything is seemingly in line for Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett to win the backup job this offseason. With Jimmy Garoppolo out of the picture and rookie QB Ty Simpson getting up to speed, it’s quick to say the job is Bennett’s to lose. His long-term NFL career will come into question if he […]
full_text: Los Angeles, CA - July 26, 2026: LA Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett run through drills with Ty Simpson, left, and Matthew Caldwell during the first day of training camp at Loyola Marymount University in Los Angeles, CA on Sunday, July 26, 2026. (Robert Gauthier/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Everything is seemingly in line for Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett to win the backup job this offseason. With Jimmy Garoppolo out of the picture and rookie QB Ty Simpson getting up to speed, it’s quick to say the job is Bennett’s to lose. His long-term NFL career will come into question if he fails to beat out the first-year signal career. The Rams have made it clear that Bennett is not the long-term answer. It was an ongoing debate for his first few seasons in the league, but the talk essentially ended the moment Simpson was taken in the first round of this year’s draft. That alone signified that the Rams see Simpson as the eventual successor to Matthew Stafford, with the clock ticking on Bennett’s time in L.A. It’s not like he wasn’t given plenty of chances either. Leading up to the Simpson pick, Bennett had three full offseasons to give the Rams’ front office reason to consider keeping him in their long-term plans, yet struggled to make the most of his opportunities. According to the Rams’ official website , he has completed 121-of-195 passes for 1,296 yards and eight touchdowns in seven preseason games, including six starts. Most of his production came during the 2025 preseason, when he tied for the most passing touchdowns (5), finished second in passing yards (512), seventh in completion percentage (68.8%) and fifth in passer rating (105.7). His improvement was noticeable last preseason, but he had an extremely low bar to clear. In his first two preseasons, he had a 3-to-8 touchdown-to-interception ratio. The lowlight of his professional career to date was a four-interception outing against the Cowboys in the 2024 preseason opener. While, yes, he did lead a miraculous late game-winning drive, it doesn’t change the fact that he was playing like a below-average NFL quarterback against the backups to the backups. Rams QB Stetson Bennett throws his fourth interception of the game vs the Cowboys. "It's just decision-making. And not seeing the field well, to be honest." – Mina Kimes "All four of those interceptions look stunningly similar." – Andrew Siciliano 🏈🎙️ pic.twitter.com/6428KEyuoI — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) August 11, 2024 Improving his preseason completion percentage from 59% in 2024 to 69% in 2025 is no doubt a promising sign. However, it ultimately didn’t matter as he wasn’t playing to win the QB2 job, as veteran Jimmy Garoppolo already had the role locked up without taking a snap. For the first time in his career, Bennett has a legitimate path to actually winning the backup role behind Stafford. His three seasons in Sean McVay’s system should give him the edge, assuming he capitalizes on the improvement he had shown last preseason. Read more: Stetson Bennett is completely expendable Bennett began training camp receiving most of the first-team reps, yet was reportedly outshined by Simpson on Day 1. Granted, it was just one day, and it’s only the first week of camp, but Bennett cannot afford to be outshined very often this offseason. Not if he intends to earn future NFL opportunities once the Rams move on one day. Simply put, Bennett desperately needs to put the rookie in his place in training camp and preseason if he wishes to stick around in the league. Eventually, the day will come when Simpson overtakes him for the backup job should Stafford and Bennett remain in L.A. after this season. Bennett just can’t let that happen, at least not right away or without a fight.
author: Evan Craig

title: Sean McVay’s 5 worst mistakes
summary: Sean McVay has built one of the NFL’s most impressive coaching résumés, transforming the Los Angeles Rams into perennial contenders while earning a Super Bowl championship and a reputation as one of football’s brightest offensive minds. Yet even the league’s best coaches are far from perfect. Across nearly a decade on the sidelines, McVay has […]
full_text: Sean McVay has built one of the NFL’s most impressive coaching résumés, transforming the Los Angeles Rams into perennial contenders while earning a Super Bowl championship and a reputation as one of football’s brightest offensive minds. Yet even the league’s best coaches are far from perfect. Across nearly a decade on the sidelines, McVay has made decisions that sparked criticism, invited second-guessing, and, in some cases, altered the trajectory of a season. Those moments don’t erase his accomplishments, but they do highlight the difficult balance every head coach faces between trusting instincts and making the right call under immense pressure. From personnel decisions to game management and long-term roster building, here are the five biggest mistakes of McVay’s coaching career and why each continues to be debated by Rams fans and NFL analysts alike. 1. Clock Usage in first half of 2026 NFC Championship Game Up 13-10 with 1:33 left in the 2nd Quarter, the Rams got the ball back after forcing a three & out. With the ball on their own 28, scoring points before the half seemed like a little bit of a stretch. But entering halftime with the lead on the road was completely feasible. Instead, Sean McVay’s three plays calls were run-pass-pass, only burning 39 seconds of clock and not forcing the Seahawks to use any of their timeouts. The Seahawks got the ball back; drove 74 yards on 6 plays and scored a touchdown in 34 seconds… Rams vs Seahawks NFC Championship, 2025. pic.twitter.com/xSmql2Ak6p — Football Classics (@ClassicsNFL) June 25, 2026 Why it belongs: It was one of the major differences in the game aside from the fumbled punt. The Rams lost 31-27. It was simply avoidable had the Rams forced the Seahawks to call timeouts. Had the Rams protected the ball, they would have been playing in Super LX and likely dominated the Patriots. 2. Super Bowl LIII The Rams offense in 2018 was the #2 scoring offense but it encounter resistance when Vic Fangio and the Chicago Bears used quarters coverage and a 6 man front to styme the Rams outside zone scheme. Sean McVay and the Rams were able to still navigate their way through the rest of the regular season and the playoffs but never figured out how to counter. Bill Belichick perfected Vic Fangio’s scheme and it resulted in the New England Patriots winning Super Bowl LIII 13-3; leaving Sean McVay befuddled and admitting he was “outcoached”. 🗓 Feb. 3, 2019: 1 year ago today. Super Bowl LIII: Rams vs Patriots (-2 | O/U 55.5) 🗣 “And it’s intercepted at the 3 yard line!” Patriots didn’t allow the Rams offense to enter the red zone once en route to a 13-3 victory. Brady + Belichick get 💍 #6. pic.twitter.com/vrxaPE0x5G — Action Network (@ActionNetworkHQ) February 3, 2020 Why it belongs: The Rams failed to capture their second Lombardi trophy and exact revenge on the Patriots from the 2001 Super Bowl. 3. Signing Jared Goff to a $134 Million Extension After the Super Bowl run, McVay and the Rams committed franchise-quarterback money to Goff before he had fully proven he could elevate the offense independently. Within two seasons, McVay had lost confidence in Goff, the offense declined significantly, and Los Angeles had to attach multiple first-round picks just to upgrade to Matthew Stafford. UPDATE: The Los Angeles Rams are signing QB Jared Goff to a 4-year/$134M contract extension worth $110M guaranteed, per adamschefter. Goff’s deal includes the highest amount of guaranteed money in NFL history.… https://t.co/QBaxvTA6V4 — Football Forever (@fballforeverhq) September 4, 2019 Why it belongs: While the Stafford trade ultimately won the Rams a Super Bowl, the Goff extension itself is often viewed as an expensive mistake and resulted in two average seasons. The Rams #1 defense in 2020 was held back by Goff’s lackluster QB play. 4. March 2022 Spending Spree Fresh off of winning Super Bowl LVI, the Rams wanted to “Run it Back” with their Super Bowl team. After losing out on the Von Miller sweepstakes to the Buffalo Bills, the Rams were determined to spend. Rather than being calculated, the Rams wanted to push their chips forward yet again. They signed Allen Robinson and Bobby Wagner while re-signing Joe Noteboom and Brian Allen. The Rams spent $154 million on the four combined players with $62.75 million guaranteed money. Did the Rams make a mistake last offseason swapping Robert Woods for Allen Robinson? https://t.co/X2tk2gE61w — TurfShowTimes (@TurfShowTimes) October 6, 2022 Why it belongs: None of the four signings were on the roster by the start of 2024. Jalen Ramsey was dealt after the 2023 season as a cost cutting move. 5. 4th & 1 play call against 49ers in Week 5 2025 McVay has made countless aggressive fourth-down decisions throughout his career, and most have been well-reasoned. However, his overtime play call against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5 of the 2025 season backfired in spectacular fashion. Facing fourth-and-1 at the San Francisco 11-yard line, McVay elected to go for the game-winning touchdown rather than kick the tying field goal. The decision itself was debatable, but the actual play call drew widespread criticism. Instead of using motion, misdirection, or one of the creative concepts that define his offense, the Rams ran a straightforward inside run into a stacked defensive front. I personally was okay with going for it on 4th & 1 against but it was the decision to put the ball in Kyren Williams’s hands rather than Matthew Stafford that drew immense criticism. BALLGAME. 🔥 Rams stuffed on 4th & 1 in OT. 49ers walk away with the W, 26-23. 🟥 #FTTB #NFL #RamsHous pic.twitter.com/ETUcD3acMH — Aggregate (@AggregateSports) October 3, 2025 Why it belongs: The Rams dropped to 3-2 and it was yet another reason the Rams failed to the win the NFC West over the Seahawks when it was all said and done. What do you think is Sean McVay’s worst decision as Head Coach of the Los Angeles Rams?
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams Players Under the Most Pressure in Training Camp
summary: Omar Speights could be benched, Davis Allen could be cut, Stetson Bennett could lose to Ty Simpson, and Taylor Decker could be signed to start for the Los Angeles Rams at tackle. Overreaction? These aren’t just one writer’s opinion, these are the results of a survey to hundreds of Rams fans this week. After asking […]
full_text: Los Angeles, CA - July 26, 2026: LA Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett, 13, stands alongside quarterback Ty Simpson at the first day of training camp at Loyola Marymount University in Los Angeles, CA on Sunday, July 26, 2026. (Robert Gauthier/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Omar Speights could be benched, Davis Allen could be cut, Stetson Bennett could lose to Ty Simpson, and Taylor Decker could be signed to start for the Los Angeles Rams at tackle. Overreaction? These aren’t just one writer’s opinion, these are the results of a survey to hundreds of Rams fans this week. After asking L.A. Rams fans to ask a series of questions about the team on Tuesday , the queries about training camp produced some of the most interesting results. Many of those answers came down to one word: “Pressure” What do these answers tell you about the Rams? Perhaps more importantly, what do they tell you about the perception of certain players in Rams camp? Omar Speights most likely to lose job “Which starter will lose his job in camp?” LB Omar Speights, 42% Nobody, 33% TE Colby Parkinson, 14% DE Braden Fiske, 9% RT Warren McClendon, 2% As you can see, fans had the option to simply choose “nobody” if they had confidence in everybody, but there’s barely any confidence in Speights at linebacker . With players like Shaun Dolac and Grant Stuard behind him, there is a lot of competition for those linebacker snaps. They’re not the only ones. Look at the results to this question: “Which surprising player will be a camp stand out?” LB Nikhai Hill-Green, 28% WR Brennan Presley, 21% Other, 16% Tim Keenan III, 15% S Alex Cook, 13% G Bill Murray, 3% QB Matthew Caldwell, 2% Could Hill-Green be a future starter for the Rams, say by 2027? But at least Speights will still be on the roster. Not everybody in the survey was so lucky. Davis Allen more likely to be cut than ‘nobody’ When asked for a surprise cut candidate, here’s what you said: TE Davis Allen, 42% Nobody, 29% CB Emmanuel Forbes, 10% RB Jarquez Hunter, 10% WR Jordan Whittingon, 7% K Harrison Mevis, 1% If none of the tight ends in front of him get traded, then Allen would be TE5 on the Rams. Is that too low on the depth chart for a player to make the 53? Many of you think so! Allen easily beat out “nobody” to be the player most likely to be cut by the Rams. But Allen will be picked up by another team if that happens. So is he the one with the most to lose? Probably not. Stetson Bennett has most at stake this month The strongest consensus choice of any question here, most of you agree that Bennett has the most to lose in this camp’s battle for QB2. If Stetson Bennett doesn’t make the Rams as the backup, will another team even call him? “Which player has the most to lose?” QB Bennett, 61% WR Whittington, 30% DE Fiske, 5% RB Kyren Williams, 4% If Bennett can’t back up Stafford, it’s hard to see how he’d help another team. Puka Nacua says that Bennett has always played with confidence. #Rams WR @AsapPuka talks backup QBs 🗣️ The early report on Stetson Bennett & Ty Simpson ✍️ #TheFanLA #PukaNacua #NFLtrainingcamp #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/UT6EoXIFVJ — 97.1 The Fan (@TheFanLA) July 29, 2026 The Rams might even sign a veteran QB to sit in front of Ty Simpson if Bennett does fail to impress Sean McVay enough. A veteran QB isn’t the only player who could join the Rams. Fans still want Taylor Decker Even though AJ Jackson hasn’t been suspended yet, Rams fans are still hopeful for more help at tackle. Jackson did rest this week because of blood clots. “Which free agent would help the most?” OT Taylor Decker, 51% WR Stefon Diggs, 15% WR Deebo Samuel, 14% LB Bobby Wagner, 13% EDGE Joey Bosa, 6% Not even close. Fans are confident enough in those other positions to want to see L.A. sign Decker, but will they be signing a $15 or $20 million insurance policy? Do they have that kind of money if Aaron Donald returns? Not that surprising when you look at these results: “What position worries you the most?” Tackle, 43% LB, 30% Receiver depth, 16% Other, 8% Center, 3% All hands on Decker. But tackle isn’t a position battle fans are watching: “Which position battle is most interesting?” WR3, 46% TE, 31% LB2, 20% EDGE depth, 3% Maybe I should have asked QB2? But if Bennett has the most to lose, who has the most to prove? Terrance Ferguson needs to step up now When asked which player on the Rams has the most to prove this camp, the winner was clear: TE Terrance Ferguson, 36% QB Ty Simpson, 22% RB Hunter, 21% QB Bennett, 18% Other, 2% Ferguson should be able to work his way into a steady role in year two. If he can’t do that, does he have much of a future with McVay? Rams TE rotation can be a mess if Tyler Higbee is still in the TE1 rotation – nothing should really suggest he isn’t Was TE1 last year until injuries zapped him Clear trust with the coaches Ferguson might play a completely different role – but this impacts Park Via @StuJRams pic.twitter.com/OVEX7em1Ec — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) July 27, 2026 It’s going to be a fascinating camp either way. Some will win, some will lose, some will be added, some will depart. But you know who never changes, even over decades? The fans.

title: TST Survey Results: Rams’ fans think Aaron Donald will be back
summary: About one week ago, I asked our readers in The Feed to share whether they/you thought Aaron Donald would be unretiring to come back to the Los Angeles Rams? Survey says: Yes, fans think AD will be coming back for 2026. Out of 56 total votes, 57% expressed the belief that AD would be back […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 15: Former Pittsburgh Panthers player Aaron Donald takes the field for his jersey retirement ceremony at halftime of the game between the Pittsburgh Panthers and the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at Acrisure Stadium on November 15, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Now, my survey was about whether or not AD would be coming back. If you want to talk about whether or not you think he should come back, then let us know in the comments below, and or check out this article here and fill out the survey! Your feedback is always appreciated! Will Aaron Donald actually be back? Will the fans be happy if Donald returns? Will Donald pick up where he left off in terms of being one of the best defensive players in the league? If Donald says, “no” to a comeback this season, then will that be the end of all the AD unretirement talk or will this come up again next year? So many questions, not many answers, yet. But one thing we do know, plenty of fans think Donald will be back for 2026. We’ll find out if they are right or wrong.

title: What players do you want to see on the next season of Netflix’s “Quarterback”?
summary: Netflix’s Quarterback has quickly become one of the NFL’s most compelling behind-the-scenes series. It gives fans a rare look beyond the highlights and press conferences, revealing everything from film study and family life to locker room leadership and the emotional highs and lows of an NFL season. Whether it’s seeing the pressure of leading a […]
full_text: Netflix’s Quarterback has quickly become one of the NFL’s most compelling behind-the-scenes series. It gives fans a rare look beyond the highlights and press conferences, revealing everything from film study and family life to locker room leadership and the emotional highs and lows of an NFL season. Whether it’s seeing the pressure of leading a franchise or the sacrifices made away from the field, the show has proven that every quarterback has a story worth telling. With another season likely on the horizon, the next group of featured quarterbacks should offer a mix of established stars, redemption stories, rising talents, and young rookies adjusting to life in the NFL. If given the choice, these four quarterbacks would be worth watching if a Season 4 is released. Matthew Stafford (Los Angeles Rams) Few quarterbacks have a career arc as fascinating as Matthew Stafford. After spending 12 seasons carrying the Detroit Lions, Stafford was traded to Los Angeles and immediately delivered a Super Bowl championship in his first season with the Rams. Since then, his journey has been filled with a 2022 injury-plagued season, roster turnover, contract negotiations, and now the challenge of extending one of the NFL’s most respected careers. What would make Stafford especially compelling is his personality. While he has largely stayed out of the spotlight, teammates consistently rave about his toughness, leadership, and football intelligence. Fans would get an inside look at Sean McVay’s offensive meetings, Stafford’s famous no-look throws during practice, and his preparation each week against elite defenses. Off the field, viewers would also enjoy seeing Stafford’s family life alongside his wife Kelly and their daughters. The balance between football and family would provide another layer that fans rarely get to witness. As one of the NFL’s last remaining pure pocket passers, every season now feels increasingly meaningful. A documentary following Stafford’s pursuit of another Super Bowl would be one of the show’s strongest storylines. Sean McVay had a brief appearance in Season 3 documenting Baker Mayfield’s brief tenure in Los Angeles. So it really just comes down to whether Matthew Stafford would be willing to be on camera. Matthew Stafford nailing this no-look pass 😎 pic.twitter.com/0ZZeu3jPC5 — Kalshi Football (@KalshiFB) March 15, 2026 Trevor Lawrence (Jacksonville Jaguars) Trevor Lawrence has experienced almost every extreme imaginable early in his career. He entered the league as one of the most highly anticipated quarterback prospects, endured a disastrous rookie season, grabbed a playoff appearance in 2025, and finished 5th in the MVP voting. Lawrence possesses immense physical gifts, but fans rarely get to see his personality outside of postgame interviews. A season of Quarterback could highlight how he handles expectations, works through adversity, and develops chemistry with a constantly evolving offense. Featuring Lawrence on the show when is on the cusp of stardom could be must-watch. Trevor Lawrence HOW?!? pic.twitter.com/K7eAqk78gl https://t.co/r9x4BU9DyM — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) December 14, 2025 Jordan Love (Green Bay Packers) Replacing a legend is one thing. Replacing two Hall of Fame quarterbacks back-to-back may be one of the toughest jobs in sports. Jordan Love has spent his career living under the shadow of Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers. Love’s calm demeanor contrasts nicely with the pressure surrounding the Packers organization. Fans would get a firsthand look at how he leads one of football’s youngest offenses while carrying the expectations of one of the league’s most historic franchises. The Packers’ passionate fan base, Lambeau Field atmosphere, and weekly preparation would provide outstanding visuals throughout the series. Netflix could seize the opportunity to add some history in its story-telling. Jordan Love on the 2026 season: “I’m excited. I love the guys we got. I love the team we got.” pic.twitter.com/qYhsd3i6s7 — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) July 26, 2026 Jaxson Dart (New York Giants) Season 3 of Quarterback provided some insight of life as a rookie quarterback in the NFL when it featured Cam Ward. Balancing some age (Joe Flacco) with youth (Ward). This year, Jaxson Dart would be the perfect choice for a younger quarterback. Dart’s personality also would be a stark contrast compared to guys like Jordan Love and Matthew Stafford. Like Green Bay, New York is one of the NFL’s most recognized organizations and markets, meaning every start, every interception, and every big throw will be heavily analyzed. Jaxson Dart 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ghwsPWbESo — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) July 29, 2026 Do you want to see these four quarterbacks? Is there someone else that would make for good tv? Make your thoughts known below!
author: Steven Ridings

title: L.A. Rams News: Dude says he just wants to play ball
summary: Puka Nacua isn’t holding out or in with the Los Angeles Rams, and is instead choosing to participate as usual. When asked about his plans, Puka basically expressed he just wants to play ball, and he wants to be with his teammates. Now, will there come a time where Nacua wants a new contract? He […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 28: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 28, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Puka Nacua isn’t holding out or in with the Los Angeles Rams, and is instead choosing to participate as usual. When asked about his plans, Puka basically expressed he just wants to play ball, and he wants to be with his teammates. Now, will there come a time where Nacua wants a new contract? He may want it now. But if he continues to ball, he’s going to get paid at the NFL level either by the Rams through a long contract, franchise tag or by another team entirely. Either way, unless something changes, Nacua will get paid more than his current rookie. So, for now, Puka can focus on football. The contract will work itself out as long as he keeps producing. And seemingly Puka being ready for 2026 is one less thing the Rams will have to worry about, for now. Please comment on whatever you want and thank you for checking out Turf Show Times! Puka Nacua says holding out for new deal ‘never crossed’ his mind (ramswire) “No, not really,” Nacua said of whether he considered a holdout, via Michael J. Duarte of the California Post. “I think the game of football is a safe place for me, and I enjoy that. There have been things outside of my control that I think have impacted the way I’ve been able to kind of focus and enjoy this game of football. But coming out here and seeing that jersey No. 12 hung up in my locker is something that I don’t take for granted and being around this group of guys, I think of all the guys that have reached out in this offseason to be there by my side, and then when we’re here in the meeting rooms, just the the level of connection that I feel like I have with all the guys out there. (It) has never crossed my mind that I don’t want to be out here with these guys.” Stetson Bennett makes ‘big time’ throw-in bid for Rams backup QB job (ajc.com) “Bennett, in the fourth and final year of his rookie contract, is looking to prove his worth as a capable backup for what’s projected to be a Super Bowl-capable team, despite his not having taken a snap in an NFL game his first three seasons in the NFL. Ty Simpson, selected 13th overall in the first round of last April’s NFL Draft recently signed a four-year, $25.4 million fully guaranteed deal, which would seem to indicate the Rams view him as their quarterback of the future.“ Betting on the Los Angeles Rams in 2026: It’s Super Bowl or bust in L.A. (espn) “But its a hallmark of good teams and well-built front offices to never be satisfied and to not get complacent, which explains why the Rams went out and traded for superstar Myles Garrett and appear to be on the brink of nudging Aaron Donald out of retirement. Last season’s squad kicked off the season with 10-1 odds to win the NFC, and they were a bounce or two away from cashing those tickets. This year, the Rams are heavy favorites to win it all, and they will likely close the preseason with the shortest title odds since 2009 for a team that didn’t win its conference the prior season. — Kevin Pulsifer ” Random Ramsdom Fandom: “It would be cool to see CJ Daniels flourish and become our next immediate impact draft steal, but this just seems like it’s typical training camp fluff reporting. Every year we get a bunch of reporting hyping up a certain player based on mildly positive coach speak. It typically doesn’t turn out to be that predictive (just like the preseason hype for Whittington and Mumpfield wasn’t)” -croaker Rams’ Feed:

title: Fernando Mendoza National Championship versus Miami, Part XVI of Las Vegas Raiders’ Mendoza Mania
summary: Shed a tear; we’ve reached the finale of Silver and Black Pride’s Mendoza Mania series, as we’ll be diving into Fernando Mendoza’s performance in the National Championship against Miami. Unlike the previous playoff games, Indiana was in a dogfight against the Hurricanes, squeaking out a 27-21 victory. That was due in part to the No. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - JANUARY 19: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Indiana Hoosiers raises the National Championship Trophy after Indiana defeated the Miami Hurricanes 27-21 in the 2026 College Football Playoff National Championship at Hard Rock Stadium on January 19, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images Shed a tear; we’ve reached the finale of Silver and Black Pride’s Mendoza Mania series, as we’ll be diving into Fernando Mendoza’s performance in the National Championship against Miami. Unlike the previous playoff games, Indiana was in a dogfight against the Hurricanes, squeaking out a 27-21 victory. That was due in part to the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft completing 16 of 27 passes (59.3%) for 187 yards with no passing touchdowns and no interceptions, but a famous 12-yard touchdown run that will be seen below. This is certainly a case where the stat line doesn’t do the performance justice because the Las Vegas Raiders’ new quarterback’s impact on the game was much bigger than what the numbers above show. Part of the reason for that is he was pressured on nearly 35 percent of his dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus . While Mendoza had moments where he was pressing too much in the National Championship, he also delivered when the lights were brightest. Almost the same throw in the Natty pic.twitter.com/z0azZ3iRom — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 23, 2026 After going through every pass attempt he made last season, one way to know if Mendoza is pressing is when he starts predetermining throws. If you’ve followed this series closely, you know that it’s one bad habit he needs to kick in the NFL. Indiana was struggling to get much going through the air early in the contest, partially because Miami’s defensive backs were sitting on and ready to defend the back shoulder passes, and this play is a good example of that. With the offense lined up in a three-by-one formation and the defense in Cover 1, Mendoza does have a one-on-one matchup with one of his favorite targets, Charlie Becker, who runs a sluggo route against press coverage. So, the quarterback is trusting that his guy is going to win with the double move. However, the cornerback has perfect coverage and is in a spot where he can defend against the back-shoulder throw or a ball over the top. In other words, Becker is never open. But Mendoza throws it anyway and misses too far inside, forcing the receiver to play defense and prevent the interception in the end zone. Mendoza is lucky this wasn’t picked because that would have taken a scoring opportunity off the board. It’s one thing to like a one-on-one matchup pre-snap, but the receiver has to at least show signs of getting open on the actual play to make the throw. Missed opportunity for Fernando Mendoza with Cooper getting wide open pic.twitter.com/kgZVTumSsN — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 23, 2026 This next one is another forced throw and a big missed opportunity. Miami is playing Cover 1 again, and Indiana dials up a bootleg with a half rollout, meaning the quarterback gets out of the pocket but settles down around midfield instead of staying on the run. It looks like his first read is to Omar Cooper Jr., who runs about a 10-yard out from the slot, and gets physical with the defensive back by running the DB over to be wide open near the sideline. However, Mendoza comes off that read for some reason. Maybe he was thinking Cooper was going to fall with the defender or was worried that the timing would be thrown off with the contact at the top of the route. Regardless, that’s a missed opportunity for an explosive play that could have tilted the momentum of the game. On top of that, the No. 1 pick ends up forcing a throw to Elijah Sarratt, who is double covered on the pylon route with the safety coming over the top to help the cornerback in a trail position. While the pass falls incomplete and the offense still has a chance to move the sticks, what should have been an easy first down ends up being a third and long situation. Great processing under pressure from Fernando Mendoza Sees LG losing and comes off his first read to find a quick answer and beat the pressure #Raiders pic.twitter.com/CCfbOcoko7 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 23, 2026 But, as mentioned in the intro, the Heisman Trophy winner had plenty of moments where he handled pressure well to earn some more hardware by night’s end. This time, the Hurricanes get more creative with their coverage by showing a two-high look pre-snap before rotating the boundary safety down to play Cover 3. Meanwhile, the Hoosiers run a concept where the two outside receivers run 10-yard outs, and the two slot receivers run curls right at the sticks. Initially, Mendoza looks to hit Sarratt on the out since it appeared as if Sarratt would have a one-on-one matchup as the single receiver. However, the safety rotating down and into the curl-to-flat zone makes that a risky throw. Additionally, that’s one of the two longer developing routes in the play call, and the left guard gets beaten in pass protection by the defensive tackle pretty quickly. Luckily, Mendoza recognizes that the pressure is coming and comes off his first read to get his quick-hitter or answer against pressure, finding the tight end on the sit/curl route right over the center right before taking a hit. That’s great processing and a great read to nullify the pass-rush, move the sticks and put the offense in scoring position. Pocket caving in, nice job by Fernando Mendoza to get this throw off and to the WR without being able to finish it #Raiders pic.twitter.com/iRsd6lLuY6 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 23, 2026 This next rep builds on the last one as it’s another good decision and throw under pressure. Miami’s coverage is simpler this time, showing a one-high look pre-snap and staying in it post-snap. It appears as if this is supposed to be a three-deep, three-under fire zone where the WILL linebacker blitzes off the edge since the defensive end loops inside and the defensive tackle stays in the B-gap on the line game up front. So, the defense is a little out of whack here, but the important aspect is that they have three deep third defenders like a Cover 3 call. Meanwhile, Indiana is in a two-by-two formation and has a mirrored passing concept where the outside receivers have go routes that they can convert into curls and the slots are attacking the seams. A mirrored concept means that the route combinations are the same on both sides of the formation and is designed so that the quarterback can pick a side and attack a matchup that he likes. Since the boundary cornerback (top of the screen here) starts bailing before the ball is hiked, while the field side corner is within five yards of the line of scrimmage, Mendoza starts his read to the wide side of the field and is likely looking to hit Sarratt on a deep shot. However, that corner ends up bailing post-snap, so he works to the other side of the read. The reason for that is there’s no opportunity for an explosive play, and with the ball on the hashmark, throwing to Sarratt would be much more difficult than attacking the same route against the same type of coverage to the short side of the field. In other words, it’s a smart decision because there’s no reason to make the pass more challenging. That being said, the pass-rush is coming with the defensive tackle pushing the center into the quarterback’s lap. So, Mendoza has to get the ball out and have enough velocity to get it to Becker without being able to finish the throw. The latter is why the pass ends up being low, but Mendoza has the arm strength to still get the ball to Becker, and the placement being low and outside actually helps the receiver use his body to keep the corner from being able to break up the pass. Another smart decision and good throw under pressure to move the sticks. The National Championship run Great read by Fernando Mendoza to work off the RB's and LG's…

title: What we know about possible Vita Vea trade
summary: Last month, we wrote that we should keep an eye on the Vita Vea situation with the Tamp Bay Buccaneers. At that point, the star defensive tackle was unhappy with his contract. We wrote it could escalate and if it did the Las Vegas Raiders could emerge as a possible trade partner. Indeed, it has […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - JULY 29: Vita Vea #50 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers holds a bag to take part in a drill during training camp at AdventHealth Training Center on July 29, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last month, we wrote that we should keep an eye on the Vita Vea situation with the Tamp Bay Buccaneers. At that point, the star defensive tackle was unhappy with his contract. We wrote it could escalate and if it did the Las Vegas Raiders could emerge as a possible trade partner. Indeed, it has taken the next step as Vea has reportedly asked for a trade. The Raiders are reportedly among the teams Vea is interested in joining. Let’s look how things currently stand: Will he be traded? It really depends. The contract dispute between Vea and the Buccaneers is clearly not going well if it has gotten to the point where the popular nine-year star has asked to leave. But there is still plenty of time for things to work out. Thursday, Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield called for the team to take care of Vea, who is not practicing. The reality is if the Buccaneers offers what he wants in terms of a new contract, he’ll probably accept it and stay. But if things continue to stall, a deal could certainly happen. Would the Raiders be interested? Yes, I’d imagine for a lot of reasons. One, he would be a great fit in the defense and fill a major role at defensive tackle. His presence would give the Raiders a serious front seven. Also, there are ties to Vea in Las Vegas. Raiders’ general manager John Spytek was in Tampa Bay with him for for Vea’s first seven seasons. Also, Raiders’ part owner Tom Brady won a Super Bowl ring with Vea as teammates and has publicly said he is a huge fan of the massive defensive tackle. A Raiders’ pursuit of Vea makes major sense. What would the cost be? It would probably take a Day 2 pick and maybe even a player to secure Vea. He is entering the final year of a four-year, $71 million deal. Vea, 31, has a few more good seasons left and he has been reasonably healthy, missing just a total of six games in the past four seasons combined. So, he will be looking for a boost in pay, probably wanting to average $23-25 million a season. So, the cost for the Raiders would be fairly steep in terms of trade and contract compensation. Who’s the competition? The Athletic has reported Vea is interested in playing for the three California teams (he’s from the Bay Area) or the Raiders. I could see the 49ers and Chargers having interest and you never know what the Rams are going to do. Plus, other teams around the league will have interest in him as well. So, Vea could go anywhere. So, if the Raiders really want Vea, the competition may be fierce. What’s the timeline? This could happen at any time. If the Buccaneers want to figure out a way to keep him, a trade may not happen until around the cut-down date of August 30. But the truth is, this is fluid situation that can change or develop at any time. Join the conversation! title: Raiders roster: Tre Tucker’s career has been let down by QB play
summary: When the Las Vegas Raiders traded Darren Waller in 2023 for a third-round pick, they had to replace a weapon on offense. The franchise decided to make that move with the same pick they acquired by drafting Tre Tucker out of Cincinnati. Tucker played in the slot during college but was asked to move outside […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 28: Tre Tucker #1 of the Las Vegas Raiders attends a news conference after an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 28, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Las Vegas Raiders traded Darren Waller in 2023 for a third-round pick, they had to replace a weapon on offense. The franchise decided to make that move with the same pick they acquired by drafting Tre Tucker out of Cincinnati. Tucker played in the slot during college but was asked to move outside by the Raiders. He was a raw route runner and had stiff hips that didn’t allow him to change directions quickly. His speed was there, and he was able to use that early on to produce as a rookie. Since then, he has improved as a route runner every year. It has led to an improvement to his statistical output every season. However, Tucker could have been more of an impact player if he had consistent quarterback play. Tucker has played with Jimmy Garappolo, Gardner Minshew, Aidan O’Connell, and Geno Smith. All four quarterbacks have struggled with the best performance coming from O’Connell. Tucker has been running wind sprints wide open down the field and even ended up throwing up on the sideline against the Browns. Against the Browns Tucker had 10 targets but only three receptions. A perfect example is the play below which was the first play of the game. Tucker wins off the line and wide open with a potential for huge play. Smith misses him by a yard on a play that should have been explosive for the Raiders offense. These types of situations have been a constant for Tucker throughout his career. Hopefully in 2026 with a better quarterback situation fans can see what Tucker truly brings to the table.

title: Raiders fans split on whether Michael Mayer will remain in Las Vegas
summary: There is a strong chance Michael Mayer may be entering his final season with the Las Vegas Raiders. The tight end, who the Raiders traded up to draft in 2023, is set to be a free agent after this season. In a post exploring whether he will return or not, we asked our readers if […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 23: Michael Mayer #87 of the Las Vegas Raiders enters the field during player introductions prior to an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Allegiant Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is a strong chance Michael Mayer may be entering his final season with the Las Vegas Raiders. The tight end, who the Raiders traded up to draft in 2023, is set to be a free agent after this season. In a post exploring whether he will return or not , we asked our readers if they think Mayer will leave the Raiders in free agency in 2027. The vote was close, but most of the voters do think he will be leaving. I tend to agree even though there is a lot still to be determined. The Raiders unexpectedly drafted fellow tight end Brock Bowers in the first round a year after Mayer was drafted and Bowers is already an elite player. Yes, the Raiders will use both players together, but still Mayer is a backup option to Bowers at the end of the day. If Mayer does finally put together a strong season, he could become a top free agent target and he could make a ton of money. However, if he doesn’t produce much and he is blocked by Bowers’ presence in the offense, Mayer may look to move on to get a better chance elsewhere albeit on a likely modest contract. So while, Mayer can return, the odds, at the moment probably point toward him being elsewhere in 2027. You can read the comments on this FEED post here. Join the conversation! title: Raiders News: Hezekiah Masses emerging as sleeper starting candidate during training camp
summary: Heading into the Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp, the expectation was that second-year pro/2025 third-round pick Darien Porter and rookie fourth-round pick Jermod McCoy would be competing for the starting outside cornerback spot opposite Eric Stokes. That’s still the case; however, rookie fifth-rounder Hezekiah “Zeke” Masses has thrown his name into the mix and received […]
full_text: LOUISVILLE, KY - NOVEMBER 08: California Golden Bears Defensive Back Hezekiah Masses (5) looks on during the college football game between the California Golden Bears and the Louisville Cardinals on November 8, 2025, at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, Kentucky. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Heading into the Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp, the expectation was that second-year pro/2025 third-round pick Darien Porter and rookie fourth-round pick Jermod McCoy would be competing for the starting outside cornerback spot opposite Eric Stokes. That’s still the case; however, rookie fifth-rounder Hezekiah “Zeke” Masses has thrown his name into the mix and received reps with the Raiders’ first-team defense during the team’s initial practice of training camp, per ESPN’s Ryan McFadden . McCoy was on a pitch count during OTAs and minicamp, and Masses took advantage of the extra opportunities. The latter was reportedly one of the standouts from the spring and played well enough to rotate with Porter during minicamp, signaling a three-man competition on the boundary of Las Vegas’ defense. Meanwhile, McFadden reported that McCoy worked with the second- and third-team defense during the 11-on-11 period of Wednesday’s practice. Obviously, it’s still very early, as yesterday was the team’s first practice of training camp. Also, Klint Kubiak said on Tuesday that the team is going to “be really smart” with McCoy’s workload during camp, suggesting they’ll be easing him into the practice plan rather than throwing him into the fire right away. The Tennessee product missed the entire 2025 College Football season after tearing an ACL during offseason workouts, and concerns about his knee led to a draft-weekend slide. But Masses has clearly made an impression on the coaching staff to earn some early first-team reps and at least be a surprise contender for a starting job. It likely helps that he has impressive ball skills, collecting five interceptions and 13 passes defended at Cal last season, while the Raiders were tied for the fourth-fewest interceptions ( eight ) in the league last year. In Other Raiders’ Links: Trade for Vita Vea?: Vote in S&BP’s poll and share your thoughts on if the Raiders should go after the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ defensive tackle who asked for a trade earlier this week. Rookie vs. Rookie battles: Speaking of McCoy-Masses, dive into four other potential training camp battles between first-year pros . No PUP or NFI to begin camp: “I’m marking every member of the Raiders active roster as a participant in their opening practice of training camp,” The Athletic’s Sam Warren posted on X/Twitter. “Includes Maxx Crosby, Jermod McCoy and Nakobe Dean. Team is remarkably healthy to begin the year.” Quay Walker catches Crosby’s eye: “I’ve never seen a linebacker that big,” the defensive end said (h/t Levi Edwards of the Raiders’ website ). “I’ve never played with a linebacker that looks like the size of me.”

title: Your 2026 Surprise Miami Dolphins Cut Candidates
summary: Every Miami Dolphins training camp ends with the cut of several players to get the team down to its final 53-man roster to begin the season. Within those cuts are always one or more players that surprise the media and the fan base. With that in mind, I asked the following question this past Monday: […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - DECEMBER 21: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Malik Washington (6) rushes with the ball during the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, December 21, 2025 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Every Miami Dolphins training camp ends with the cut of several players to get the team down to its final 53-man roster to begin the season. Within those cuts are always one or more players that surprise the media and the fan base. With that in mind, I asked the following question this past Monday: Which player currently expected by the media and fan base to make the Miami Dolphins’ final 53-man roster do you believe will be a surprise cut ahead of the 2026-2027 NFL season, and why? If you foresee multiple surprise cuts, please identify all of them and explain your reasoning. Below are some of your thoughts and answers- SlayerNation1 is bemoaning the fact that scoring via field goals has now seemingly become a game plan for some because every damn kicker can seemingly score from midfield. At least I think that’s the point that’s being made. It is officially the National SOCCER League now, ergo if any Kicker gets cut, it would be surprising… and quickly replaced with another soccer player. Teams are close to keeping 5 trick-shot Place Kickers and flopping Punters on the 53 roster as specialists. Move the ball 20 yards and then kick a ball straight and far…. how scintillating. PA phinphan points to Trey Moore as a player that could possibly unseat multiple players at different positions. Uche or Ojabo could end up on the outside looking in especially if Trey Moore gets designated as just an edge. Maybe even both depending on Ferrell. The five edges could be Robinson, Ferrell, Moore, Llewellyn, and Reiger. The same could be said of Dodson or Gay, Jr. if Moore gets an LB designation. Even if Moore stays as Edge/LB, one these guys may not make it. Unless he completely balls out, Cameron Goode is going to be looking for a new gig. Although, I don’t know if anyone is expecting him to make the team or not. Dolphster believes that despite the lack of depth in the WR room, one of the vets that were signed this offseason will be without a gig come September. Even though the WR Room is lacking talent, I think they will cut one of the veteran receivers; either Tolbert or Atwell. JKBMia has a list of guys that were held over from the last regime that may or may not make it to the start of the regular season. “Surprise” Cuts to me would be : Dodson OG3/Wright Malik Washington Marshall/Duck All holdovers from the last regime that have underwhelmed a bit and may not fit the new staff’s liking. I wouldn’t anticipate any of them getting cut, but I could see it, so that’s why they’re on this list. MIAMI235 makes the point that in the NFL, few players are truly secure in their jobs from year to year. Looking at it, in the rear view mirror….what Dolphins Fan, would have thought that Tua, Hill and Waddle would all be gone at the end of one season ? ( Not all technically cuts, but that is really just semantics for this story). Phoenix6 lists three guys, including Dodson, who might get traded away before camp is out, depending on any potential injuries that may occur before that point. My lowly take would be three. Three seemingly surprises. Tyrel Dodson: Linebacker depth is crowded with new draft additions, putting him under pressure. The pressure could make him pop to the top. But it’s a difficult camp for him. Matthew Butler: Faces an uphill battle for interior defensive line snaps behind the main rotation. The rookies & 2nd yr vets are just too much to overcome… even if he equals them. Malik Washington: Caught in a heavy wide receiver numbers crunch under the new coaching staff scheme. May be the biggest surprise. The rooks are just better, having him take a 2nd yr to be viable. He didn’t show enough last yr either. He showed he could be this no-pads-on camp, but there’s better to be had coming up. StanleyDoyle1 believes that Ewers could be on his way out. Ewers. Not on merit, but because Gronowski impresses and is no threat to their guy Willis. Just a fan points out that, despite us fans being the driving force of the league at the end of the day, we have zero say about the product on the field. Like, I have said before, seems like a million times\n It doesn’t matter what I think what the team does. That’s the real reality, because I’m just a real fan, and that’s it, no power with the exception of prayer. MiamiItaliano believes the guy with the most interesting name might be gone come the regular season. I think the surprise cut is Storm Duck. A lot of people expect him to make the team. But the DB room looks to be crowded now. Well, that’s our selection of players that may be surprise cuts, and no doubt some of these are correct; we just don’t know which ones at this point. I personally see some surprise cuts as a good thing, especially if replaced by a rookie because it means, in many cases, that the rookie was better from the start than most of us believed he would be, allowing him to unseat the veteran. Other times, I suspect if the rookie is close enough to the veteran, he will get the nod just due to the cap implications. If you missed our initial post, please share your surprise cuts in the comments section below. As always thank you to each of you who took the time to answer our Phinsider Question Of The Day.

title: Rebuilding ‘not the mentality’ for 2026 Miami Dolphins
summary: Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley met with the South Florida media ahead of the team’s second day of training camp practices in Miami Gardens on Thursday morning. He was asked about the roster’s sweeping changes this offseason and how his players and coaches are dealing with the idea of a “rebuild” for the franchise. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - JULY 30: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins speaks to media during training camp at Baptist Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley met with the South Florida media ahead of the team’s second day of training camp practices in Miami Gardens on Thursday morning. He was asked about the roster’s sweeping changes this offseason and how his players and coaches are dealing with the idea of a “rebuild” for the franchise. “I don’t know how you can have a conversation with a competitive player or a competitive coach and have it sit right with them where we’re just going to say, ‘We’re just going to rebuild this year.’ I mean, that’s just not the mentality of any competitor who’s made it to this level or any coach that’s made it to this level… Whether it’s practice or whether it’s a drill, I think we all want to win it. And our mindset is, we need to get better, we need to develop — and everything that we do is going to be about competing to get better throughout the process. And we want to win, so I just don’t think any player or any coach is going to sit here and say, ‘We’re just going to throw in the towel and just rebuild.’ So that’s probably why no one’s hearing that. I think if you had a group of players saying that, then I think we’ve got the wrong players.” It’s clear that despite the challenges that face an organization in flux, Hafley and the rest of the team are doing their best to prepare for those moments when they arrive. The 2026 Miami Dolphins may not win a lot of games due to the amount of roster turnover they’ve experienced and the cap constraints that go along with such major moves, but they’ll surely be trying their hardest to field a squad their loyal fanbase can be proud of once the season is in the books.

title: Vikings Training Camp Notes: 7/30 Edition
summary: The Minnesota Vikings had their first training camp practice open to the public today, which brought more visibility to the proceedings, at least for the day, from fans posting videos that media aren’t allowed to do (and fans aren’t supposed to do either). But it looks like the Vikings are enforcing the no video rule […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings had their first training camp practice open to the public today, which brought more visibility to the proceedings, at least for the day, from fans posting videos that media aren’t allowed to do (and fans aren’t supposed to do either). But it looks like the Vikings are enforcing the no video rule this year so that may curtail future videos of training camp. Teams across the league have been working for several years to prevent photos and videos of training camp from being disseminated to opponents via the public for competitive purposes and the Vikings appear to be enforcing that policy as a condition for fans attending training camp. Be that as it may, there are a few storylines worth mentioning in today’s training camp notes. Quarterback Competition It was a day where Kyler Murray worked through some mishaps. There were a couple of bad exchanges with Blake Brandel that led to two fumbles. There was a miscommunication with a receiver on a pass play and a couple interceptions. But he also had the most impressive passes of the day as well. He also got most of the first team reps. McCarthy didn’t have either the lows or the highs that Murray had. Mostly a steady diet of shorter passes, which reminds me a lot of what his training camp looked like last year. Vikings training camp practice day 2 is over. The quarterback report: Kyler Murray took a hefty amount of snaps with the starters. Had one deep hit to Dontae Fleming. J.J. McCarthy spent more time with the No. 2 group, fewer downfield attempts. — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) July 30, 2026 And from the StarTribune: J.J. McCarthy began with the first-team offense in an early 11-on-11 period and closed with them in a late 11-on-11 period. But most of the first-team snaps in between those reps went to Kyler Murray. Some of those were 1s-vs.-1s, others were 1s-vs.-2s. Carson Wentz got to run with the third-team offense a few times, which we didn’t see yesterday. As for how the QBs did, it was again a mix, though it felt like we saw a few more mistakes than on Day 1. Murray had back-to-back near interceptions in a full-field 11-on-11 period near the end of practice, one targeting Justin Jefferson and the other targeting Tai Felton. There were again drops by receivers, and Blake Cashman batted down a pass at the line of scrimmage. But there were also a few flashier plays than Day 1, too, like a deep pass from Murray to Dontae Fleming. If two days of training camp can make a trend, I’d say the trend is that Murray is getting familiarized with the offense and receivers and making mistakes along the way, while McCarthy seems to be playing it safe with shorter, more high percentage passing. Whether McCarthy is missing open receivers further down the field or not has not been reported. Whether or not Murray getting significantly more reps than McCarthy continues or not remains to be seen. It does makes sense for Murray to get more reps in the sense that he needs more reps being new to the scheme and personnel whereas this is McCarthy’s third training camp working with the same. It would be interesting to know on what basis Kevin O’Connell will divvy out the reps going forward. Are more reps earned by accomplishing tasks on a personal ‘to-do’ list (which might be different for each quarterback) or will they be more need based. But ultimately, I don’t see the quarterback competition being decided by which quarterback has the higher passing rating in training camp. So to some degree a close accounting of passing stats for each quarterback may be focusing on the wrong thing. Instead, I suspect the competition will be decided by which quarterback grows into being able to run the full offense, from getting the plays called on time, to getting to the right play at the line of scrimmage, to being able to aggressively take what the defense gives him. For Kyler Murray, that means mostly continuing to gain familiarity and comfort with the offense and personnel and eliminating mistakes along the way. For J.J. McCarthy, that means mostly growing his skillset to be better able to aggressively take what the defense gives him. In a short competition, whether it lasts for a week or a month from now, that favors the more experienced Murray, who should be able to slowly become more versed in the scheme and in tune with receivers. It may be more difficult for McCarthy, who has said he has improved dramatically from last season, to show more touch, layering ability, and accuracy with his throws while also being able to process faster. But over the next year, McCarthy may be able to get there. In the meantime, he needs to get out of his comfort zone and challenge himself and test his limits. That means trusting what he sees and attempting more difficult throws when available. That probably means making more mistakes too, but that is what training camp is for. For Murray, moving to a new team and scheme forces him out of his comfort zone and so the challenge for him is to grow into the new system and slowly begin to master it. That may also lead to working on some aspect(s) of how he approaches the game as well. A change of scenery can also have the benefit of a better team around him and a more positive atmosphere and a chance to change some narratives about him. So, at the end of the day, the competition may be decided not by who did the best from beginning to end, but by who progressed/improved the most with their to-do list. I would imagine that over the next week to ten days the coaching staff will have a good idea about the rate of progress for each quarterback and may be ready to make a decision on who is the starter. Update on Other Position Battles There aren’t many battles for starting positions on the Vikings’ roster at the moment, except maybe quarterback, but maybe some could emerge over the course of training camp. And of course there are battles further down the depth chart at just about every position group. Let’s take a look into those. Inside Linebacker The acquisition of Jamal Adams was a bit of a surprise and the initial response for many observers was that he may be more of a long shot to make the roster. But on the second day of training camp, he was mixing in with the first-team defense at inside linebacker- where he played last season. Adams hasn’t been a full-time player for a few years now since he injured his quad tendon, which took over two years to fully recover from according to Adams. And he appears to have signed for the veteran minimum (his contract details haven’t been released but he alluded to that in his press conference yesterday). But he played about 40% of the defensive snaps with the Raiders last season and graded higher than any of the starting linebackers for the Vikings, according to PFF. Neither of these things guarantee him a starting spot or even a roster spot, but he appears to be getting every chance to at least make the roster. So how does that affect the linebacker pecking order? A healthy Blake Cashman is still LB1 in every scenario, and it’s difficult to imagine Eric Wilson falling below LB2, but best-case scenario for Adams is that he becomes something of a LB2a, where he takes some reps from Wilson and also replaces Josh Metellus’ snaps at linebacker last season. Most look at Adams as primarily a good pass rusher, but relative to Cashman and Wilson (and Pace), Adams’ greatest value may be in coverage. Linebacker coverage was a weak link last season for the Vikings as even Cashman struggled more in coverage. And overall last season, Eric Wilson, Josh Metellus, and Ivan Pace Jr. were three of the four worst defenders still on the team in coverage according to PFF. All graded significantly below average. Adams graded above average in coverage and above average overall last season. Second round pick Jake Golday is a roster lock, so the addition of Adams appears to make Ivan Pace Jr.’s path to a roster spot even more uphill. However, Special Teams Coordinator Matt…

There will be no stopping the incessant commentary on the QB situation because, well, it does create interest (i.e., clicks). I believe he wants to continue to develop JJ and does not want to hurt his confidence in any way. At the same time he is tasked to win games and his salary dictates that that is the number 1 goal. Resurrecting Kyler Murray is a new challenge and getting him up to speed takes time. I suspect that neither QB really likes this setup but what can you do. They both are handling it very well IMO. This situation is going to create daily soap opera stories for us to regale. I wish I could give an educated opinion on whether or not this is good for the team or for the eventual starting QB. I do respect KOC for doing it his way though. If you are going to go out then you should go out doing it the way you want. But he really did not have much choice due to JJ not being able to stay healthy. If he could have played every game last year then I doubt they would have signed Murray. It sucks but it is as it should be (I do not like to say it is what it is). How would you handle the QB situation? Teasley, whom Minnesota hired June 1, emphasized how in-step he and O’Connell have been over the past two months. “Working together with this guy every day,” Teasley said, gesturing at O’Connell, “it’s become clear we’re aligned in our vision — but in terms of where we are currently and as we embark on the 2026 season, but also where we’re headed in the future and as we build this thing out.” O’Connell told Twin Cities media members he’s “really enjoyed” working alongside Teasley and his staff. “It’s been a really cool summer getting to build these relationships and see so many of the things that made us all so excited about bringing Nolan here,” O’Connell said. “It’s just awesome when it starts coming to life on a daily basis. And it’s not only Nolan, but the staff that he’s assembled has been just as good of a staff as I’ve been around, quite honestly.” O’Connell and Teasley are pleased with Minnesota’s offseason, both in player acquisitions and work accomplished during OTAs and minicamps, and now it’s time for the next level. “I know I speak on behalf of our players when I say they’re excited about what the potential of our team can be,” O’Connell said. “That’s what this time of year is for all 32 teams. There’s a wonderful opportunity out in front of all of us, and we’ve got to go to work and maximize it every single day.” K evin O’Connell Reveals How Vikings Will Split Reps Between Kyler Murray and J.J. As the first overall pick in the 2019 draft with 87 starts and more than 20,000 passing yards in his career, Murray is the clear favorite to win this competition. But O’Connell has committed to opening it up, and McCarthy has said he believes him. “My job’s to make it right for either of them, so that’s kind of all I can focus on,” right tackle Brian O’Neill said. “It’s just like any other guy and any other position battle.
