title: Caleb Lomu embracing physicality early in rookie training camp
summary: As Patriots first-round pick Caleb Lomu climbed the hill to the practice fields ahead of his first padded NFL practice, he admittedly felt some nerves. Those feelings quickly disappeared once the hitting started, reminding Lomu of one key piece of advice he received beforehand. “Just being a violent player,” Lomu said. “You’re going against another […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots tackle Caleb Lomu (74) does a drill during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As Patriots first-round pick Caleb Lomu climbed the hill to the practice fields ahead of his first padded NFL practice, he admittedly felt some nerves. Those feelings quickly disappeared once the hitting started, reminding Lomu of one key piece of advice he received beforehand. “Just being a violent player,” Lomu said. “You’re going against another guy every single play. You’re hitting someone every single play. Now, with the pads, you can just be a little bit more violent. And so, that’s the mentality going into it. “That’s what you got to have in your mind every single play. I can’t take any plays off. No rep is a coffee break. Just going out there every rep, every practice, and being violent, being a physical player.” Lomu took the advice literally. On his first rep of one-on-one pass rush drills, the rookie tackle held his ground against Bradyn Swinson before finishing the play by pushing the pass rusher to the ground. While some questioned Lomu’s physicality coming out of the University of Utah, the rookie has embraced New England’s effort-and-finish mentality. “Finishing is the biggest key as an offensive lineman. You have to be able to know what to do, and do it with a violent demeanor,” he said. “That’s my mentality going into every single rep, every play that we have, is just to finish longer than the guy.” Through five training camp practices, Lomu has remained the Patriots’ top backup behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses. Whenever the 35-year-old Moses is given time off, the rookie is often first up in his place at right tackle. “Coming up here been switching around a lot of positions, but it’s just the same thing. You just got to flip the hands and the feet and then that’s really it. I feel super comfortable at right right now,” Lomu said. “It’s just got to get down the footwork and the hand techniques, but then it’s just football at the end of the day.” To help carve out an early role for their first-round pick, the Patriots have also used Lomu as a jumbo tight end and gave him snaps at guard during the spring. “He rarely makes the same mistake twice,” Vrabel said. “He practices hard. He tries to learn. He tries to fix mistakes.”
author: Brian Hines

title: The Patriots have found their new James Develin, save for the neck roll
summary: Even with the game becoming increasingly pass-centric and despite having the greatest quarterback of all time under center, the New England Patriots of the 2010s remained steadfast in their belief in a balanced offense. Accordingly, they were one of the few teams to still employ a traditional fullback during those years. Fast forward to 2026, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 10: Reggie Gilliam #44 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 10, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Even with the game becoming increasingly pass-centric and despite having the greatest quarterback of all time under center, the New England Patriots of the 2010s remained steadfast in their belief in a balanced offense. Accordingly, they were one of the few teams to still employ a traditional fullback during those years. Fast forward to 2026, and an offense that is going back to its roots. The only difference is the lack of a neck roll. Conceptually, however, Reggie Gilliam will very much be used like James Develin was back in the day. The free agency signing, who spent the first six seasons of his career in Buffalo, said so himself on Thursday. “I love the offense. [Josh] McDaniels is a lot of fun to play for, and he uses a fullback,” Gilliam said about his new team and offensive coordinator. “He showed me a lot of film with James Develin in here. He said, ‘Watch a lot of him. What we do with him is what we’re trying to do with you.’ I’m looking forward to that.” What lessons did he draw from that film, though? “That you could be anywhere,” he said. “You could be in the backfield. You could be at tight end. You could be split out. You could be anywhere in this offense.” Gilliam is no stranger to a flexible role. During his final season with the Bills, he lined up in the backfield, as an inline blocker, in the slot and even split out wide; additionally, he also was a core member of the team’s kicking game operation. Back in the day, Develin was used similarly. During his stint in New England from 2012 to 2019, he too moved around the formation to allow McDaniels to run different plays from the same grouping. Look no further than the only touchdown drive of Super Bowl LIII against the Rams, when Develin’s presence helped the Patriots gain the upper hand in what had been a defensive battle up until this point. Whether or not Gilliam will have the same impact remains to be seen. He does have the versatility, and also offers similar levels of physical play. As for Develin’s trademark neck roll, on the other hand, it will not be making its return to Foxborough. “I don’t like something squeezing my neck,” Gilliam explained. “The neck roll — not for me.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Kayshon Boutte staying focused amid Patriots trade rumors
summary: Kayshon Boutte knows his future may not be in New England. But for now, the wide receiver is focused on where his feet are. “I think my main focus is just that I’m here today. If I’m somewhere else next week or the week after, I mean that’s kinda what it is. That’s part of […]
full_text: Jul 25, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (9) walks to the practice field at training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kayshon Boutte knows his future may not be in New England. But for now, the wide receiver is focused on where his feet are. “I think my main focus is just that I’m here today. If I’m somewhere else next week or the week after, I mean that’s kinda what it is. That’s part of the business,” Boutte said. Boutte has gotten off to a strong start in training camp, hauling in a highlight-reel deep catch from Drake Maye in each of the team’s first three competitive practices. His ability to block out the noise and perform on the practice fields has earned him praise by head coach Mike Vrabel and his teammates. “I think my attitude. I mean, we all hear a lot of the stuff that’s going on,” Boutte said. “I’m taking every day, day-by-day, not thinking about what’s next.” After acquiring A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason, Boutte entered camp lower on the Patriots’ wide receiver depth chart. That room also features Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas and second-year receivers Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III, who each made highlight-reel grabs during Thursday’s practice . “Me and Kyle were talking about it yesterday, don’t worry about the next guy,” Boutte said. “Everybody’s going to make plays. Don’t let that affect your opportunities.” Following his second straight 500-yard season, Boutte again found his name in trade speculation this offseason as he enters the final year of his rookie contract. With the Patriots adding veterans to the room and the 24-year-old looking toward his first significant payday, the two sides could ultimately decide that a fresh start is the best outcome. “I love having depth, but I would say that we’re always going to try to look to improve, whether that’s by adding draft capital, obtaining a player or keeping the guys we have. We want to try to provide competition throughout the roster at each position. I think that’s something that’s critical,” Vrabel said. “I think that’s what good teams do every year, year in and year out, that they’re making the roster as competitive as possible. So that those position battles, who’s the sixth lineman, who’s the fifth, sixth receiver, who’s the fourth tight end, all these things, you want to be as competitive as possible. That’s something that I have always — I was a part of it as a player, and I think that’s important to do here in training camp.”
author: Brian Hines

title: 7 performances of note from the Patriots’ fifth training camp practice
summary: Five days into training camp, the New England Patriots decided to up the intensity. The introduction of full pads brought an increase in physicality and competition. To recap what was a rainy session on the Gillette Stadium practice fields, please make sure to head over to our Patriots training camp notebook. In the meantime, let’s […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JULY 26: Kyle Williams #18 of the New England Patriots greets Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots Training Camp on July 26, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Five days into training camp, the New England Patriots decided to up the intensity. The introduction of full pads brought an increase in physicality and competition. To recap what was a rainy session on the Gillette Stadium practice fields, please make sure to head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, let’s take a look at who caught our eye on Thursday. Standout of the day WR Kyle Williams: He had a relatively quiet start to his second NFL training camp, but Kyle Williams managed to take his game up a notch in the first full-pads session of the summer. The 2025 third-round draft pick ran with the second-stringers, but the fact that he produced a pair of highlight-reel grabs speaks for itself: he had a very good session and seemingly has started building some momentum. His first big play came against Kobee Minor, who he beat off the line of scrimmage and later overpowered at the catch point for a touchdown. Later, Williams got the better of Minor as well when he finished a one-handed back-shoulder fade by getting his knee down before going out. “I just show up every day just ready to take advantage of the opportunities given to me,” Williams said earlier this week . On Thursday, he very much did just that. Other performances of note WR A.J. Brown: Brown’s first few practices with the Patriots were not particularly noteworthy. Thursday’s was different. His battles with Christian Gonzalez had high entertainment value, while he himself hauled in four catches on five targets from Drake Maye. The other starting WRs: While Brown had a breakout performance of sorts, the three other starter-level wide receivers were quiet on Thursday. DeMario Douglas, Kayshon Boutte and Romeo Doubs combined for just one catch, a short throw from Drake Maye to Doubs in the low red zone. Douglas and Boutte, meanwhile, both went without a single target in team drills. WR Efton Chism III: While he continues to see most of his reps with the second-stringers, Efton Chism joined fellow sophomore Kyle Williams among the top performers. The former UDFA was one of the top performers in 1-on-1s and later also caught an impressive leaping touchdown over Mike Brown on a pass from Tommy DeVito. The battle for the final roster spots at receiver is starting to heat up. DT Eric Gregory: The Patriots defensive line got its first taste of full-contact work on Thursday, and Eric Gregory made the most of it. The second-year defender won both of his 1-on-1s against Ben Brown, as charted by Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald, and later also saw some opportunities with the starting defense. All in all, a good day for heaviest D-tackle on New England’s roster. The linebackers: Thursday was a mixed bag for the Patriots’ linebackers. Led by starting duo Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss, the group was very active in run support and found itself operating in the backfield on multiple occasions. Pass coverage was a different story, though, as the quarterbacks successfully targeted the position throughout the day. CB Christian Gonzalez: Talk about iron sharpening iron because the first round of the full-pads Christian Gonzalez-A.J. Brown battle lived up to the hype. Gonzalez broke up one pass intended for Brown in 1-on-1s and later also had a pair of breakups versus Kayshon Boutte. He was beaten once by Brown on a fade in the offensive left-hand corner of the end zone, but that play was exemplary for the 24-year-old’s performance on Thursday: it needed a perfect throw and catch to beat him. Other players worth mentioning include Tanner Arkin, who continues to look like New England’s best blocking tight end. Furthermore, Cameron Dorner had in an impressive touchdown catch, Will Campbell won both of his 1-on-1s against Dre’Mont Jones and Bradyn Swinson, and the connection between Jared Wilson and Drake Maye produced a second bad center-quarterback exchange in five practices. The Patriots will hold their sixth practice of training camp on Friday. Gates are scheduled to open at 9:15 p.m. ET for that session, with practice again set to start approximately an hour later.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Things are starting to click for Eli Raridon at Patriots training camp
summary: After back-to-back training camp practices with multiple catches and securing two red. zone touchdowns on Thursday, New England Patriots rookie tight end Eli Raridon is growing more comfortable at the NFL level. “It’s going well,” Raridon said Thursday about his first training camp as a pro. “I’ve got a lot of great people in the […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots tight end Eli Raridon (82) works with a member of the coaching staff during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After back-to-back training camp practices with multiple catches and securing two red. zone touchdowns on Thursday, New England Patriots rookie tight end Eli Raridon is growing more comfortable at the NFL level. “It’s going well,” Raridon said Thursday about his first training camp as a pro. “I’ve got a lot of great people in the tight end room to learn from. Hunter Henry’s been great to me. Just learning every day, trying to apply it on the field and just playing as hard as I can.” New England’s third-round draft choice this year hauled in his first score in Thursday’s practice on an open play-action bootleg pass from quarterback Drake Maye, waltzing into the end zone from about the 5-yard line. Raridon later caught another touchdown working with Tommy DeVito’s second-team offense. Head coach Mike Vrabel spoke about having the younger athletes play fast and not worry about mistakes when asked about Raridon’s growth ahead of Monday’s practice. He explained that the coaching staff can correct mistakes, not coach someone to play faster. “[It’s] helpful,” Raridon said of that coaching approach. “It’s a great mentality to have, and to win in this league you have to play fast. And as a young player, it’s hard not to be thinking about a lot of stuff out there … I think we can play fast and obviously play smart but not worry too much about making a mistake. As an offense starts to come together, it’s going to get easier.” Raridon later added that things are slowing down for him, and although he’s not 100% acclimated to the offense, the summer is a “night-and-day difference” compared to his work in the spring sessions. During the 22-year-old’s senior season at Notre Dame, he caught 32 receptions for 482 yards (15.1 yards per reception). However, after suffering two ACL tears on the same knee early in his collegiate career, Raridon finished with only 48 catches and just 18 starts for the Fighting Irish, leaving him with less playing experience than other prospects in his draft class. “I think that it’s a learning curve for these guys,” Vrabel said about what he’s seen from the rookie class thus far. “I think that the spring is one thing. When you get to training camp, it’s something completely different … Eli’s learning and figuring this game out, and I think he can find a way to help us.” The Notre Dame product credits his time learning the offense during spring practices with helping him apply elements more quickly, allowing him to play faster in training camp. Early in the spring, free-agency signing Julian Hill suffered a season-ending knee injury , thinning out an already uncertain position group. The veteran was acquired to be a crucial blocker, and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf also saw potential for Hill in a hybrid role as a receiver. “I think as a tight end room we all need to step up,” Raridon said about whether he feels he has to take on some of Hill’s responsibilities. “We all need to play our hardest and fill in that role that’s missing.” When speaking on Caleb Lomu’s progression on Thursday, Vrabel said there are different blocking techniques the offensive tackle needs to learn because the play at the line of scrimmage is different in the NFL compared to the collegiate level. Some of those aspects also apply to Raridon in his development as a blocker. His maturation in that area could be the key to unlocking a full-time role with Henry.

title: Patriots training camp recap: Drake Maye-A.J. Brown connection comes to life
summary: Following their first off day of training camp, the New England Patriots were back to work on Thursday and donned full pads for the first time this summer as work transitioned into the red zone. Here’s what went down on the rainy practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: CB Carlton Davis (new), CB Brandon […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) makes a catch during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Following their first off day of training camp, the New England Patriots were back to work on Thursday and donned full pads for the first time this summer as work transitioned into the red zone. Here’s what went down on the rainy practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: CB Carlton Davis (new), CB Brandon Crossley (new) PUP/NFI: ED Gabe Jacas, RB Terrell Jennings, TE C.J. Dippre, ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Injuries: N/A The Patriots saw a pair of new absences in their secondary on Thursday, as Carlton Davis and Brandon Crossley were absent. Davis left Tuesday’s session early. Rhamondre Stevenson and Charles Woods, both who also left last practice early with apparent heat issues, were back on the field. Takeaways Maye and Brown: After a shaky start to the summer, Drake Maye and A.J. Brown had their best day of practice together in the red zone — where they showcased early chemistry back in minicamp. The duo was in sync for much of the day as Maye was 4-of-5 targeting Brown with at two touchdowns coming on slants, while the lone incompletion came with Christian Gonzalez in coverage. The pair also had a pretty connection in 1-on-1s with Maye perfectly dropping a fade route in the bucket as Brown was in the back left corner of the end zone. “I know everybody tracks the numbers and everything else. I’m confident that they will continue to progress,” Mike Vrabel said of the chemistry between the two prior to practice. “Again, it’s good work. It’s good competitive work out there, and guys are in tight coverage or challenging and whatever that may be. “I’m really confident that that relationship will continue to grow, and A.J. will have plenty of opportunities to help us.” Year 2 receivers: Brown was not the only receiver to shine on Thursday, as second-year pros Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III found the end zone on numerous occasions. Williams was on scene for two of the day’s highlights working with Tommy DeVito: beating Kobee Minor off the line of scrimmage before hauling in a touchdown through contact and then later snagging a one handed back shoulder fade and getting a knee in bounds for another score. Shortly after Williams’ second score, Chism got on the board by working back to the ball and going up-and-over Mike Brown for a touchdown. The shifty wideout also had multiple wins in 1-on-1 work as he remains a tough cover. Elsewhere at wide receiver, it was the quietest day of the summer for DeMario Douglas and Kayshon Boutte as they each went without a target in team work. Romeo Doubs then had just one catch from Maye, while UDFA Cameron Dorner hauled in an impressive touchdown catch from Behren Morton over Karon Prunty. Gonzo’s participation: Asked Tuesday whether he would continue to practice in full as work transitioned to full pads, Christian Gonzalez replied, “I’ll be out there.” Out there he was on Thursday and the cornerback remained a full participant in all periods. Gonzalez’s strong start to camp contemned as well as he started his day in 1-on-1s with a pass breakup against A.J. Brown, who got him back on the aforementioned fade, and forced two incompletions against Kayshon Boutte. Trench work: The full pad work allowed for our first true look at the Patriots offensive and defensive lines. New England’s starting offensive line held up well in pass protection, but it was the Patriots defensive front that largely controlled the line of scrimmage in the run game. While rookie Caleb Lomu did record a pancake on his first rep, linebackers Christian Elliss, Robert Spillane, Khalil Jacobs, and Namdi Obiazor and defensive lineman Cory Durden and Leonard Taylor were all in the backfield throughout the day. Other notes: Rookie tight end Eli Raridon continued to be active as a pass catcher hauling in a play-action bootleg touchdown from Drake Maye and a later reception in the flat from DeVito. UDFA tight end Tanner Arkin also remained with the first team at times and showcased his physicality in the run game. Jared Wilson and Drake Maye had one bad exchange where the ball ended up on the ground. UDFA edge rusher Xavier Holmes had a noticeable amount of snaps along the edge today working in with Dre’Mont Jones and Elijah Ponder. Charles Woods was again first-up to replace the injured Carlton Davis in the secondary. Woods had a pair of pass breakups in 1-on-1s and was notable in run support in full-team periods. Punt returners: Marcus Jones, DeMario Douglas, Romeo Doubs, Efton Chism, Kobe Prentice Personal protectors: Mike Brown, Peter Manuma, Craig Woodson The Patriots will be back to work on Friday where the current expectation is they will be back in full pads. Practice is set to begin at 10:15 a.m. ET.

title: DeAndre Hopkins no longer coaching for Patriots
summary: DeAndre Hopkins’ coaching tenure with the New England Patriots came and went, seemingly in an instant. Less than a week after announcing the veteran wide receiver had joined his staff, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel revealed that Hopkins’ time with the club has met its end again. “It was a great experience,” Vrabel said ahead […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 27: Wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins #8 of the Kansas City Chiefs warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders, at Allegiant Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images DeAndre Hopkins’ coaching tenure with the New England Patriots came and went, seemingly in an instant. Less than a week after announcing the veteran wide receiver had joined his staff , Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel revealed that Hopkins’ time with the club has met its end again. “It was a great experience,” Vrabel said ahead of Thursday’s practice at Gillette Stadium. “Hop’s not here, but it was a great experience for, I think, all of us.” Hopkins leaving the Patriots again after a few days was always the plan. The 34-year-old originally arrived last week to get an up-close look at the team’s coaching and scouting operations. He was on the field during all four training camp practices before Wednesday’s off-day, assisting the wide receiver group and its position coach, Todd Downing. “That’s what we’re trying to do when we have some of these unique situations where a player or former player, whatever it may be, wants to come in and help and learn and they love football,” Vrabel said. “So, I think it was good for everybody.” Whether or not Hopkins will be back with the Patriots in some capacity in the future is not known. Neither is whether the five-time All-Pro wants to continue his active career. A free agent since his contract with the Ravens expired in March, he has not yet officially announced his retirement. Hopkins originally entered the NFL as a first-round draft pick by the Texans in 2013 and has since appeared in a combined 204 regular season and playoff games. Spending time in Houston, Arizona, Tennessee, Kansas City and Baltimore, he has a total of 1,046 receptions, 13,770 receiving yards and 87 on his résumé.

summary: Before kicking off the fifth practice of this year’s training camp, the New England Patriots made their head coach available to the media again. One of the big talking points, especially with full pads being introduced to the mix on Thursday, was the injury statuses of multiple players. Vrabel provided some updates. Patriots injury updates: […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 10: Carlton Davis III #7 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 10, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Before kicking off the fifth practice of this year’s training camp, the New England Patriots made their head coach available to the media again. One of the big talking points, especially with full pads being introduced to the mix on Thursday, was the injury statuses of multiple players. Vrabel provided some updates. Patriots injury updates: 7/30 CB Carlton Davis III: The starting outside cornerback was one of multiple players banged up during the Patriots’ most recent practice on Tuesday, and as a consequence will not participate during Thursday’s session. What he is dealing with or how long he is expected to remain out, Vrabel did unsurprisingly not specify. Davis’ absence will, however, open the door for some of the depth players at the position to see extended reps with the starters. CB Charles Woods: Vrabel had a pretty straight-forward answer when asked about the other Patriots cornerback leaving practice on Tuesday: “I don’t think that was anything major.” Woods is set to practice on Thursday, possibly filling Davis’ spot in the lineup. ED Gabe Jacas: The Patriots’ second-round draft pick “continues to progress well” and that is getting “closer to return to play.” Jacas has been on the non-football injury list since he signed his rookie contract on Day 2 of camp because of a knee procedure he underwent in the offseason. Due to questions about that knee, the team added some rather unusual safety measures to his deal. Vrabel also positively mentioned Jacas’ attentiveness in meetings and doing “everything he needed to do” to get on the field and up to speed. ED Harold Landry III: While Vrabel did not give any concrete information about the team captain, he “probably would say that Gabe’s closer to coming back than Harold is.” PUP/NFI players: None of the five players on those lists — Jacas, Landry, RB Terrell Jennings, TE C.J. Dippre, S Brenden Schooler — are set to return just yet. The Patriots will hold their fifth practice of the summer on 10:30 a.m. ET on Thursday. Despite rainy conditions, the session is set to take place outdoors.

title: Patriots training camp primer: Day 5 practice preview, schedule, more
summary: Things are about to change at New England Patriots training camp. Not only is the weather worse than it had been for the first four sessions of the summer, Thursday’s practice also will see the introduction of some physicality: for the first time since the end of last season, players will wear full pads. Here’s […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 09: Offense and defense set-up during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 9, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Things are about to change at New England Patriots training camp. Not only is the weather worse than it had been for the first four sessions of the summer, Thursday’s practice also will see the introduction of some physicality: for the first time since the end of last season, players will wear full pads. Here’s everything else you need to know about training camp practice No. 5. Schedule Despite the weather, the Patriots’ fifth training camp practice of the year is scheduled to again take place on the fields behind Gillette Stadium. The session is free and open for the general public to attend. 9:30 a.m. ET: Gates open 10:30 a.m. ET: Practice ca. 12:30 p.m. ET: Player availability (FB Reggie Gilliam, WR Kayshon Boutte, TE Eli Raridon, OT Caleb Lomu, G Mike Onwenu, DT Cory Durden) As always, of course, the schedule is tentative and subject to change. For more information, please visit our Pats Pulpit Training Camp Guide . Story of the day With full pads being introduced to the mix, we are going to keep a close eye out for everything associated with them. The 1-on-1 blocking battles between offensive and defensive linemen, how receivers and cornerbacks fare in press-man coverage, the pass rush in full team drills, injuries — you name it. Long story short, Thursday’s practice will be the most intense one to date. Injuries to monitor NFI: RB Terrell Jennings, S Brenden Schooler PUP: TE C.J. Dippre, ED Harold Landry III, ED Gabe Jacas Injured: RB Rhamondre Stevenson, CB Carlton Davis III, CB Charles Woods Three players got shaken up during the Patriots’ most recent practice on Tuesday , and their availability and workload will be worth monitoring. As for the five players on the injury lists, they remain eligible to return at any point. Players to watch RB Jam Miller: The battle for the Patriots’ third running back spot is about to heat up. And while Lan Larison has held that role pretty consistently through the first four days of practice, rookie Jam Miller has looked good and could give the sophomore a run for his money. Miller, after all, projects as a true between-the-tackles early-down back and should be at his best when the bodies truly start flying around him. WR A.J. Brown and CB Christian Gonzalez : This is going to be one of the marquee battles of training camp, with two of the best players in the league at their respective positions going at each other. So far, Gonzalez has had the upper hand whenever he and Brown crossed paths. However, the introduction of pads could help level the playing field in favor of the big-bodied receiver. Then again, Gonzalez has handled all types of receivers in his career. This will be a fun one, reminiscent of the Logan Mankins-Vince Wilfork battles of yore. OT Will Campbell and OT Caleb Lomu: Finally, some full on 1-on-1s. The Patriots did do some drills of that kind before in camp, but without full pads those always need to be taken with a grain of salt. Now, it’s time for the real deal — and for an up-close look at the Patriots’ future tackle pairing in particular: Campbell will be in the spotlight given that the last full-pads impression of him in the Super Bowl was a negative, while Lomu will get his first taste of NFL physicality for the first time ever. Pats Pulpit will have you covered throughout the day, so please make sure to regularly check back to patspulpit.com for all the latest news from camp. Credentialed Patriots beat writers Brian Hines ( @iambrianhines ), Andrew Guindon ( @NestPgs ) Taylor Kyles ( @tkyles39 ) will bring you live updates from camp on their Twitter/X feeds, so please make sure to give them a follow.

full_text: New Orleans Saints Training Camp is in its very early stages, but already, one player has stood out. Kool-Aid McKinstry had a really great Day 1, leading to the media and players singing his praises throughout the day. For the Saints, improvement for McKinstry is arguably one of the most important factors for this team. The CB group is young and unproven, and if the Saints want to stay in games, they need these players to step up. If McKinstry proves to be a high-level CB1 in the NFL, the Saints could be a playoff team this season. Hopefully, this upward trajectory can continue, but a small roadblock has popped up. Today during practice, McKinstry left early with an ankle injury, per Nick Underhill. Kool-Aid didn’t finish practice. Kellen Moore said precautionary after Kool-Aid rolled his ankle a little. — Nick Underhill (@nick_underhill) July 30, 2026 The good news is this seems like a precautionary move by Kellen Moore and McKinstry should be fine, but ankles are something to pay attention to. If McKinstry is perfectly fine at next practice and it seems like there are zero injury worries, then great, but ankle injuries can pop up again and become annoying for the players. At practice, the rest of the defense did have a good day, and Quincy Riley even intercepted Tyler Shough.

title: Sean Payton set to present Drew Brees at Hall of Fame enshrinement
summary: Former San Diego Chargers and New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees will officially be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, OH, as a member of the class of 2026 on August 8. Sean Payton, former Saint and Brees’ longtime head coach in the Crescent City, was recently announced as the presenter […]
full_text: New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees (9) and New Orleans Saints head coach Sean Payton embrace each other and the Vince Lombardi Trophy as the New Orleans Saints beat the Indianapolis Colts 31-17, Sunday, February 7, 2010 in Super Bowl XLIV at Sun Life Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Former San Diego Chargers and New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees will officially be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, OH, as a member of the class of 2026 on August 8. Sean Payton, former Saint and Brees’ longtime head coach in the Crescent City, was recently announced as the presenter for No. 9 at the enshrinement ceremony. @SeanPayton to present @drewbrees for Class of 2026 Enshrinement 🏈 https://t.co/VCKkIU7NAf pic.twitter.com/mXkZZhxgca — Pro Football Hall of Fame (@ProFootballHOF) July 30, 2026 Although Brees and Payton had their own backgrounds in the NFL before joining forces in New Orleans in 2006, the QB-HC combo cemented their professional legacies within the Superdome at the heart of the Big Easy, delivering a rebirth to Saints football and aiding in the rebuild of a then-broken city. Following a 3-13 season and a 2005 campaign that saw zero home games played inside of New Orleans following the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina, the city and team required a refresh and found just what Louisiana needed in a first-year head coach and a young gunslinger coming off of a brutal shoulder injury. These guys would grow, progress, and build what would become one of the most prolific offenses in modern league history. The partnership between Brees and Payton quickly sparked a fire for the black and gold while providing a sense of hope for those still suffering from the tragic natural disaster just a year removed. In the pairing’s inaugural season in New Orleans, the Saints finished with an 11-5 overall record and made a run to the NFC Conference Championship game. Although the team would ultimately fall short of reaching the ultimate goal of playing in and winning the city’s first Super Bowl, this season was simply a foreshadowing of greater things to come. New Orleans would go on to miss the postseason in both 2007 and 2008 before a magical year in which pigs learned to fly. Brees and Payton’s offensive prowess, in addition to a multitude of weapons on both sides of the football, allowed the Saints to simply dominate opponents during the 2009 regular season. Averaging nearly 40 points a game, New Orleans would end the year 13-3, not losing until the final three weeks of the year. Victories against the Arizona Cardinals and Minnesota Vikings would lead the Saints to Miami for a chance at a title. The AFC representative? A 14-2 Indianapolis Colts team led by QB Peyton Manning. Everyone remembers the iconic plays; everybody knows about the final result, but what many look over is just how immediate the impact Drew Brees and Sean Payton had on the New Orleans Saints and the Big Easy came to be. In less than five years, the two brought a franchise from the bottom of the barrel to the top of the world following a 31-17 Super Bowl XLIV win. Although Brees and Payton never managed to bring New Orleans back to the big game, their record-shattering, game-changing, everlasting effect on the sport continued for over a decade together. The two had more than 150 regular-season victories, six division titles, three conference championship appearances, and a SB ring for the cherry on top. Drew carried a chip on his shoulder in the way he played the game, leading to his first-ballot gold jacket. He finished his career with over 80,000 passing yards, 571 touchdowns, and an absurd completion rate of 67.7%. Brees was also selected for 13 Pro Bowls, named as an AP first-team All-Pro, a two-time Offensive Player of the Year award winner, and MVP of Super Bowl XLIV. Although times have changed, with Payton now at the helm of the Denver Broncos and Brees retired and enjoying time with his wife and kids, the professional success and legendary status for both started with a losing team in a city that did not have much to offer. Now, after giving everything they possibly could and then some, Payton will give Brees his flowers in what is sure to be a moving, emotional presentation for fans everywhere. I’m sure Drew is already looking forward to being in attendance when Sean has his name called in the near future.
author: Jason Watson Jr

title: NY Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas feels the best he has in ‘a long time’
summary: There might have been some small nagging concern regarding New York Giants star left tackle Andrew Thomas as camp opened, considering he was limited in OTAs and minicamp as the coaching staff managed his reps in the spring. Thomas missed the start of the 2025 season as he recovered from a Lisfranc injury, and the […]
full_text: Andrew Thomas | Getty Images There might have been some small nagging concern regarding New York Giants star left tackle Andrew Thomas as camp opened, considering he was limited in OTAs and minicamp as the coaching staff managed his reps in the spring. Thomas missed the start of the 2025 season as he recovered from a Lisfranc injury, and the end of the season when he suffered a hamstring injury. Now, Thomas is almost a “full-go” as camp opens and says that he feels “They were kind of managing my reps today,” Thomas said when asked if he’d get to a full workload at some point in camp. “Like, Bloom (offensive line coach Mike Bloomgren) just tells me when I’m in, when I’m out, and I just try to abide by that but I feel good. This is the best I’ve felt in a long time, so I’m excited for this season.” There are several players on every roster that their team simply does not want to be without. For the Giants, there are very few on that list ahead of Thomas. The Giants obviously want Thomas out there practicing, improving, and building continuity with his linemates. However, they also have to be smart and make sure he’s ready to start the season against the Dallas Cowboys. The venue in West Virginia may help with that as well. Thomas noted that, as a southerner, the weather at Greenbrier is downright chilly. After all, it dipped into the 50’s at night and only got up to a sunny 78 during practice, which is a brand new camp experience for the Georgia product. “It’s amazing,” Thomas said. “I was talking to (offensive lineman) Jon (Runyan Jr.) and I was telling him that I don’t think I’ve ever been a part of a training camp where it’s this cold outside. I’m from the South. Even in Jersey, it gets humid, so I’m not complaining, I’m excited. It’s nice out, just going to continue getting better.” Thomas certainly had a good workout in the second practice, with multiple battles against edge defender Abdul Carter. Carter reportedly had a great practice notching two or three “sacks”, which gives Thomas more to work on and improve for the third practice. “I’ve got to look at the film,” he said. “Just from a feel thing, and just stay more square in my set, trying to stretch the rushers a little bit more. I’ll watch film and see what I can do better.” This is where health and availability really matter. Getting the reps against the Giants’ edge defenders, as well as with his linemates. The Giants haven’t had many opportunities to build continuity along their offensive line in recent years. “Continuity is everything,” Thomas said. “Plus up front, every snap we get, just working through communication and each rep we just get tighter knit and we’ll perform better in the game.” That unit now includes 10th overall pick Sisi Mauigoa, who got the ‘rookie duty’ of running around and firing up the crowd in attendance as well as working as the Giants’ starting right guard. Thomas thought Mauigoa did a good job in both endeavors, both interacting with the fans and in his work on the field. “To be a rookie, like he’s in tune to his assignments,” Thomas said. “He has really good technique. Obviously, he has the physical traits. It’s been exciting to see him put it together so far. “He (Mauigoa) definitely has confidence. Our whole offensive line is just full of personality. He’s done a great job. Like you said, the confidence that he has, you can see it on the field, just the energy he plays with and just going out there attacking, the effort that he plays with to be such a young guy. A lot of times you come out here, you’re thinking a lot when you’re a rookie just trying to understand the speed. But you can see him flying off the ball, he’s excited to get after it.” The Giants’ offensive line was solid — even good — in 2025. It sounds like Thomas thinks there’s even more reason to be excited for 2026.

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 2 of Giants training camp. For Jaxson Dart, it’s time to flip the switch at Giants training camp | The Record WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. − The road from good to greatness for quarterbacks is often not paved with perfection on the practice fields, and especially during the summer. That’s something Jaxson Dart has come to appreciate, but it’s not easy. Aaron Rodgers has always encouraged young quarterbacks to take more risks in practice. New patches for Giants practice jerseys John Harbaugh explains the jersey patches the Giants' players wore in practice today: pic.twitter.com/yVOet3kl3N — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) July 30, 2026 2026 NFL season: How Ward, Dart, Shough, Sanders can improve | ESPN.com Jaxson Dart, New York Giants Where he could get better: Consistency. Dart is an extremely frustrating watch. He has very little consistency to his process as a thrower and a pocket manager. His feet are frequently disconnected from the ground, which affects the timing of his throws and delays his reaction to pressure. His lower-body mechanics change willy-nilly, and he often looks like a kid alone on a basketball court attempting pretend buzzer-beaters, lurching to launch from odd angles for no apparent reason. I’m confident there’s a quality starting QB somewhere in Dart’s game, but it’ll take quite a bit of development to get him there. The good news is that a steady hand is at the mast. With new head coach John Harbaugh comes a legacy of quality Ravens teams. He’ll buy Dart time to grow, as the Giants should improve in all three phases under Harbaugh’s experienced gaze. The offensive brain trust has some worrying names — Matt Nagy, Brian Callahan and Greg Roman — but all three are experienced coaches who should be able to impress upon Dart the importance of a consistent process to create predictable results. Until then, Dart is still more theory than practice. Jaxson Dart has his missing piece of the Giants’ offensive puzzle | New York Post The first practice of the John Harbaugh Era had ended, and there was a bare-chested Jaxson Dart tossing footballs to Malik Nabers. The vision of the young Giants franchise quarterback having the chance to target the electric Go-To Guy he had on the field with him as a rookie for a mere 23 snaps makes Dart’s heart, and Harbaugh’s heart, and the hearts of all Giants fans, sing with joy, and allows all of them to dream, and dream big. Even in limited capacity, Malik Nabers brings ‘aura’ as Giants open training camp | SNY.tv Hope, rejuvenated. It had been 304 days since Nabers tore his ACL and lateral meniscus. Confidence that he would return for the start of the 2026-27 season had waned in the months since. But seeing Nabers there with his quarterback, hours after he took part in individual drills, changed that outlook. There is now justified optimism that the two will share the field against Dallas in 46 days. “There is an aura that he has on the field that is exhilarating,” Dart said. “It’s ‘Leek.’” Veteran DT Johnathan Hankins retires | Pro Football Talk Veteran defensive tackle Johnathan Hankins has hung up his cleats. Hankins, 34, told Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report that he is retiring after 12 seasons. A second-round pick of the Giants, he also played for the Colts, Raiders and Cowboys. Hankins appeared in 169 career games and was among the league’s premier run-stuffing interior defensive linemen, with 433 tackles, including 44 for loss. summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Abdul Carter was dominant, Malik Nabers worked again, Kayvon Thibodeaux made an impact, and fans had fun on a beautiful West Virginia day as the New York Giants held their second practice of training camp. full_text: Fans watch practice Thursday at The Greenbrier Sports Performance Center. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Abdul Carter was dominant, Malik Nabers worked again, Kayvon Thibodeaux made an impact, and fans had fun on a beautiful West Virginia day as the New York Giants held their second practice of training camp. Here are some of the winners and losers, as well as other takeaways. Winners Abdul Carter — Carter got the better of Andrew Thomas on Thursday, and let everybody know about it. [ More about Carter’s big day ] Braxton Berrios — The veteran wide receiver/return man made several catches on Wednesday. He backed that up with another productive day on Thursday. Berrios is making an early impression in the competition for one of the final roster spots. Dominic Zvada — There were no placekicking sessions in Thursday’s workout. On the final play of practice, though, Zvada walked on and drilled a 57-yard field goal after the ball had been clocked by backup quarterback Brandon Allen with :01 left on the clock. Score one for the undrafted free agent in his competition with Ben Sauls. Leki Fotu — The journeyman defensive tackle had a disruptive day. Fotu had a tackle for loss and was in the backfield on a handful of other occasions. Malik Nabers — The star wide receiver was on the field for a second straight day during individual drills. Every day that Nabers practices is a win for both him and the Giants. Kayvon Thibodeaux — For the second straight day, Thibodeaux made an impact play. This time, Thibodeaux picked off a Jameis Winston pass at the line of scrimmage and took it to the house for a score. Thibodeaux has been working with the second team, but head coach John Harbaugh said he does not consider him a backup. “He knows he’s going to play a bunch,” Harbaugh said. “We have three starters outside the linebacker. Those are all starting football players. Slice it how you want.” Giants fans — This was the first practice attended by fans, and it happened on a gorgeous, sunny, comfortable day here in West Virginia. Losers Ben Barten — The Turk came for the undrafted free agent defensive tackle on Thursday, as he was cut and replaced on the roster by linebacker Anfernee Orji. Theo Johnson — The third-year tight end, who has had an issue with drops over his first two seasons, dropped a pass for the second straight day. Dante Miller — ‘Turbo’ fumbled after catching a short pass from Jameis Winston, with the result being a scoop-and-score for linebacker Micah McFadden. Walk-throughs? What walk-throughs? One thing we have seen is that Harbaugh doesn’t believe in using a bunch of walk-through or install periods. After early special teams and individual work, the rest of practice the first two days has been full-speed 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 work. That is much more competitive and a faster pace than we have seen from the Giants in training camps during recent seasons. Rookie duties As media members were walking to our station in a far corner of the Greenbrier practice facility, we saw rookie Sisi Mauigoa running a lap while waving at the crowd trying to fire up the fans. After practice, I asked Andrew Thomas what that was about. “That was rookie duties,” Thomas said. “We made him go run around and fight the crowd. He did a good job. “Probably made him some money, too. Probably about 10,000 Twitter followers.” Quote of the day Can Nabers be as good or better after his knee injury than he was in 2024? “I got extreme confidence in myself,” Nabers said. “I’m not going to put myself in any spot that I feel like I’m not going to be better than what I was before. So, I don’t see myself being what I was before. What I was before, what you all saw my rookie year, I felt like that was basic. I got high standards for myself. I know everybody has high standards for me also. But the standard that I hold myself to is very high. title: NY Giants training camp: Abdul Carter has big day
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Abdul Carter had the kind of day at New York Giants training camp on Thursday that the Giants and their fans can only dream about him having once the 2026 regular season begins. Working against All-Pro left tackle Andrew Thomas, the second-year edge defender had at least two would-be sacks […]
full_text: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Abdul Carter had the kind of day at New York Giants training camp on Thursday that the Giants and their fans can only dream about him having once the 2026 regular season begins. Working against All-Pro left tackle Andrew Thomas, the second-year edge defender had at least two would-be sacks of Jaxson Dart, and broke through the line to bat down a tight end screen intended for Isaiah Likely. Carter also did his fair share of woofing, the cleaned-up version of which is Carter stating that Thomas was going to have to put in some work during this training camp. Thomas, one of the NFL’s best offensive tackles, wasn’t engaging in the trash talk. “That’s all defenders,” Thomas said. “They make one play, and they’re the best. You do a second, you’re All-Pro.” Thomas, though, certainly recognized that Carter, the No. 3 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, is tougher to block than he was as a rookie, when he had just 4.0 sacks and his season was marred by a pair of benchings. “He’s stringing his moves together better. He’s using his power more,” Thomas said. “And you can tell he just has a better understanding for different types of blocks, different types of attacks, recognizing play schemes.” Carter is considered a breakout candidate for the Giants. Thursday’s practice was an indication that such prognostications for the former Penn State star, who drew Micah Parsons comparisons before last year’s draft, might not be wishful thinking. “He’s had two good practices,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “He’s doing everything well right now. He was in the backfield quite a bit. “He’s going against a really good tackle too. I thought those guys were making each other better. I just appreciate that kind of competition.” Harbaugh said that Carter, whose work ethic was questioned after his benchings for missing practice and being late to meetings last season, has shown “amazing work ethic and a really deep determination” thus far this season. Thomas wasn’t thrilled about having a tough day handling the precocious young pass rusher. “I never get excited when I lose,” Thomas said. The fact that Thomas did lose to Carter on Thursday, though, has to be exciting for the Giants.

title: NY Giants Brian Burns: ‘Camp should be hard’ — even at a swanky resort
summary: Edge defender Brian Burns is in his third training camp with the New York Giants, and things are just a bit different than his previous two camps. Burns’ previous two camps were held at the Giants’ facilities at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center in East Rutherford, N.J. To start, there’s a stark difference between the […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants pass rusher Brian Burns celebrates a sack | Getty Images Edge defender Brian Burns is in his third training camp with the New York Giants, and things are just a bit different than his previous two camps. Burns’ previous two camps were held at the Giants’ facilities at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center in East Rutherford, N.J. To start, there’s a stark difference between the scenery at the Giants’ facilities, nestled between MetLife Stadium’s parking lots and New Jersey route 3, and the lush greenery at Greenbrier Country Club in West Virginia. “I definitely look into the distance,” Burns said, talking about the scenery. “It’s beautiful out here. There’s a couple cribs up there [in the mountains], it’s nice. I notice quite a bit of things, we’re trying to figure out something to do on the off day, maybe we’ll go fishing or something.” It’s a change of pace for someone born and raised in southern Florida (born in Fort Lauderdale, went to high school in Miami metropolitan area, college in Tallahassee), spent the first part of his NFL career in Charlotte, North Carolina, and the second part in northern New Jersey and New York City. “I think I’ve seen an eagle or something,” he said. “There was a big bird that flew over the practice field when we was out there. “I (didn’t) see no bears or nothing,” he added with a laugh. “I’m not trying to see that. “It’s nice. It’s peaceful, a lot of mountains, trees, wildlife. So, you know what I’m saying, it’s a peaceful view, but there’s a lot of chaos on the field.” Chaos on the field. That’s the kind of thing fans want to hear about. And that brings us to another feature of the Giants’ camp this year. The pretty, peaceful views stands in stark contrast to the intensity of camp under John Harbaugh. “He’s intense,” Burns said of Harbaugh. “I knew that from his team meetings but, I mean Harbs, he’s all about ball, and that’s what you want in a head coach.” “Every time he opens his mouth,” he added. “That’s who he is, he can’t help it. He’s got that intensity regardless. Enthusiasm I should say, not intensity.” The enthusiasm and intensity is something Burns already likes about Harbaugh’s camp. It’s the way training camp should be. “I don’t know about any of the younger guys that have been through it. Camp’s supposed to be hard,” he said. “Camps supposed to be hard, that’s how it’s supposed to be. I don’t know, man. We’re definitely going to work and I’m looking forward to it.” “(Harbaugh) makes it very clear what he expects. He expects you to work. He expects you to be a pro, show up on time, prepared. He’s not a man for excuses, he understands stuff happens, but he ain’t trying to give too much of that.” Burns noted that while the Giants only have two days off in the first 12 days of camp, there’s a good plan in place to allow players to recover. He noted that there’s a good balance between work and recovery so the players don’t “overdo” it, to use his words. “Top priorities are obviously getting in football shape,” Burns said. “being in better condition than your opponent and I would say really just getting good at your identity. What you’re going to be calling most of the time. There’s a good handful of calls that you’re going to have that you can always fall back on. You need to be able to execute them against any look, any personnel that the offense may throw at you and that’s kind of what you need to focus on.” The Giants were one of the best teams in the NFL at forcing third downs in 2025, but they were also one of the worst at getting off the field in those situations. An enthusiastic training camp and a focus on identity and a foundation that can get opponents off the field should go a long way toward helping to fix the defense.

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! The Giants hope to have Nabers, who tore his ACL and meniscus in […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day of Giants training camp. 5 QBs Highlight The NFL’s 12 Biggest Comeback Candidates For 2026 | FOX Sports 6. Malik Nabers, WR New York Giants. The Giants hope to have Nabers, who tore his ACL and meniscus in Week 4, ready for the start of the season. With a promising young quarterback in Jaxson Dart, the former LSU star receiver could put together a season that rivals or exceeds his standout rookie campaign in 2024 (109 catches, 1,204 yards, 7 TDs). Malik and OBJ Malik Nabers and Odell Beckham Jr. on the field together #giants pic.twitter.com/QKd9y5S6Us — Charlotte Carroll (@charlottecrrll) July 29, 2026 New York Giants’ Cam Skattebo ‘good to go’ as training camp opens | USAToday.com “Yeah, he’s good to go,” Schoen told reporters. “I’m sure you guys saw the video. Yeah, he’s been busting his tail. That video shows a little bit of how good his rehab’s been, that he’s able to not land it and still be okay. So yeah, he’ll be out here. He’ll be ready to go today, and he’ll be doing everything.” The video Schoen was referring to was from last week’s Fanatics Fest in New York, where Skattebo did a backflip on stage and nearly wiped out. “He’s a young man, and so he’s in the spotlight and in New York City, and you’ve got to be conscious of your actions, not only from a health standpoint but a perception standpoint,” Schoen said. “But he knows, I’d rather him not do that, especially this close to camp. But also a testament to, you know, how good of a job our training staff and medical staff did in terms of getting him back and ready to go here as we start camp.” There’s a subtle difference with ‘reenergized’ John Harbaugh as he begins new Giants chapter | New York Post Chris Horton has witnessed that for the past 12 years on Harbaugh’s staff, the past six as the Ravens special teams coordinator. It was wholly expected that Harbaugh would pluck Horton out of Baltimore and he did, adding the title of assistant head coach to his Giants job description. Horton, 41, always gets a kick out of watching and hearing Harbaugh at the annual introductory team meeting. This time around, standing in front of the Giants for the first time to open up the spring offseason workout program, Horton noticed a subtle difference. “Did I see a little more juice, more pop?’’ Horton said. “He’s excited. We’re excited. You know, we’re excited to be here. We’re the New York Football Giants. We’re all excited to be here. He was ready to go. He was fired up. It was an awesome team meeting.’’ Why the Giants are in West Virginia and how they turned a resort into a home away from home | The Athletic Largely, because The Greenbrier has proven up to the task many times before. In 2014, then-New Orleans Saints coach Sean Payton worked with the resort to establish a facility equipped for an NFL training camp. In the years since, the Denver Broncos, Houston Texans, Cleveland Browns, San Francisco 49ers, New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals have used the facility for training camp or other parts of the NFL season. This year, the venue even hosted Iraq’s national soccer team as part of the World Cup. Rosburg spoke with Abir Chaudhry, the Browns’ director of team logistics and operations, to learn how the team got the most out of its time at The Greenbrier, from small details like outfitting player lounges and commute patterns to the big-picture planning of making the excursion as easy as possible. During training camp, the Giants will stay at The Greenbrier Hotel. But the main benefit isn’t the luxury lodging; it’s what’s down the road from the historic hotel. Not only do the Giants have access to two grass fields and a FieldTurf field, but also fully equipped meeting rooms, offices, a training room and an on-site weight room, which is a big change from the Giants’ Albany days, when team meetings were held in college classrooms. They also don’t have to bring lockers or weights to set up a weight room. 1 Reason Every NFL Team Shouldn’t Be Overlooked in 2026 | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Realizing Their Collective Talent. The New York Giants are ready to emerge as a legitimate Super Bowl threat on the heels of a transformative offseason. With John Harbaugh taking over as head coach, the stage is set for this potential-laden squad to put all its high-upside pieces together and make a run. The team has an enviable young offensive nucleus built around Jaxson Dart, Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers, while the defense added a ton of veteran playmakers in free agency. The expectations for Big Blue may be unreasonably high for a program that hasn’t won more than six games since 2022, but there is every reason to trust Harbaugh can maximize the roster’s potential and get the Giants to live up to these lofty projections. title: David Bailey stars on day two of Jets training camp
summary: The Jets conducted their second practice of training camp in 2026 on Thursday, and the big winner of the day was their top pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, edge rusher David Bailey. So we can probably start carving out Bailey’s bust for the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton. Or maybe we can […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Florham Park, NJ, USA; New York Jets edge David Bailey (31) warms up during training camp at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jets conducted their second practice of training camp in 2026 on Thursday, and the big winner of the day was their top pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, edge rusher David Bailey. Practice 2 in the books: Big day for the defense, which harrassed Geno Smith. Rookie David Bailey led the way — three sacks, unofficially. His quickness and short-area acceleration jump out. It’ll be fascinating to gauge his development throughout camp, especially when the pads… — Rich Cimini (@RichCimini) July 30, 2026 David Bailey with an impressive practice. He’s fun to watch. So quick. Next step is seeing what he does when the pads come on. — Brian Costello (@BrianCoz) July 30, 2026 #Jets practice is over. David Bailey was the story today. Kingsley Enagbare was also very good. The QBs Geno Smith was 3/4 in 11 on 11 and 3/4 in 7 on 7. Cade Klubnik was 6/7 in 11 on 11 and 3/4 in 7 on 7. More coming … — Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) July 30, 2026 Aaron Glenn on David Bailey: “He’s everything that we expect him to be. It’ll be real exciting once we get the pads on.” — Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) July 30, 2026 So we can probably start carving out Bailey’s bust for the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton. Or maybe we can say it’s nice that his training camp is off to a strong start. I’ll let you choose which of the two is more appropriate. Either way, Bailey is the most important player on the Jets defense in 2026. The team needs him to be an immediate impact player. There aren’t many other players with significant pass rushing skills on this defense. In many ways I think the success or failure of the defense will be based on whether Bailey plays up to his Draft status. He certainly has the skills to be a star, and this early practice is a reminder of that.
