title: DeVonta Smith thinks Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is “doing a tremendous job”
summary: Jalen Hurts isn’t the only one in Philadelphia who has had to adjust to a new offensive coordinator each season, wide receiver DeVonta Smith is also learning yet another new system by another new guy. The WR spoke to reporters after the Eagles’ first training camp practice, and gave some insights into how new OC […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jalen Hurts isn’t the only one in Philadelphia who has had to adjust to a new offensive coordinator each season, wide receiver DeVonta Smith is also learning yet another new system by another new guy. The WR spoke to reporters after the Eagles’ first training camp practice, and gave some insights into how new OC Sean Mannion is handling the responsibility. “I think he’s doing a tremendous job getting everybody up to speed, helping everybody understand the small details of the offense.” Training camp is a really important time to learn more about a new play-caller, and Smith talked a bit about some of the things he focuses on when working with someone new. “Biggest thing is understand his flow, how he’s going to call it, the new terminology and things like that. I think that’s the biggest thing about it — when you kinda don’t know what the flow is, you kinda don’t know what to expect, you have to grow and learn. So, I think once you get to understanding how he wants to do things, it becomes easy.” The new system that Mannion is installing has been spoken about with excitement from players throughout the offense, from Lane Johnson to Jalen Hurts. The Eagles’ QB complimented the OC for how he’s teaching the group and his approach. “I think Coach [Mannion] is going to be just fine. He’s gotta lot of structure, and a lot of intentionality behind what he does.” It’ll still be some time before we get a chance to see the new offense — and as badly as we hope to see it all in the preseason, head coach Nick Sirianni notoriously holds tight to any perceived competitive advantage. Week 1 against the Commanders will be the real show to see just how different and dynamic the offense can be this season, but it’s encouraging that the players are all so bought in on the concept.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Tank Bigsby must be more involved in the offense this year!
summary: Today marked the second Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The non-padded session lasted for about 90 minutes. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Friday. They’ll return to practice at 10:00 […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JUNE 09: Philadelphia Eagles running back Tank Bigsby #8 is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles off season minicamp on June 9th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Today marked the second Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The non-padded session lasted for about 90 minutes. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Whereas the first day of training camp offered reason to be encouraged about the Eagles’ new offense , the second day was a reminder that this unit is still very much a work in progress. Especially as it relates to the passing attack. Vic Fangio’s defense dominated the first 11-on-11 series to the point where Hurts was coverage “sacked” multiple times. One of the few attempts that Hurts did get off was batted incomplete by Zack Baun, who appeared to be in zone coverage. Hurts and the offense did look sharper in 7-on-7. Hurts had good completions back-to-back to DeVonta Smith, who beat Quinyon Mitchell each time. Hurts also hit Makai Lemon on a quick slant in addition to connecting with Elijah Moore. Hurts was fortunate that a pass over the middle intended for Hollywood Brown went through Riq Woolen’s hands after the cornerback undercut a route to be in position for a pick that ultimately wasn’t made. During another 11-on-11 series, Hurts made a nice anticipatory completion to a crossing Dallas Goedert. But then he threw wide of the tight end on a screen. Hurts’ flashiest completion came when he rolled left and threw downfield to Dontayvion Wicks, who made a leaping 50/50 ball catch to beat Jakorian Bennett and Cole Wisniewski in coverage. The ball wobbled in the air and I thought there was a good chance it was going to get picked but I give Hurts credit for being willing to give his receiver a chance to make the play. Turnover avoidance is obviously prudent but not to the point where offensive ambition is completely neutered. I like to see Hurts taking some more risks, especially in a practice setting. UPDATE: Scroll down for the video of this play . I somehow missed this play but BGN alumnus Eliot Shorr-Parks noted that Hurts underthrew an open DeVonta downfield . He said that a better throw would’ve resulted in a sure touchdown. I’m less irked by that miss, which I’d classify as uncharacteristic, than what seemed to be a turn down on what might’ve been a deep touchdown to Wicks along the left sideline at one point. Of course, it’s hard to say with certainty that Wicks was in the progression, but Hurts seemed to be looking at him before checking down. Wicks seemed to be a little bummed that Hurts didn’t give him a chance there. All told, an uneven day for QB1. Which is clearly the end of the world. Season over. Play of the day from today’s Eagles training camp practice: pic.twitter.com/aKCvvRFsmk — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 30, 2026 The best part of the Eagles’ offense was their rushing attack. Fangio’s defense was all over the run during the first 11-on-11 series. After that, though, multiple running backs broke off some big runs. (Again, note that this practice was not padded and there isn’t live tackling to the ground). Tank Bigsby broke off multiple long runs to the end zone. He’s not someone you need to lock in on in order to notice him at practice; the way he moves is really eye-catching. I know I’ve been beating this drum a lot but I just can’t stop thinking about how the Eagles MUST get him more involved this season. He’s simply too electric to be an afterthought in this offense. Bigsby logged just 3.6 carries per game last season … and that’s with him benefiting from garbage time/the Eagles resting their starters in Week 18. His workload needs to be bigger in 2026. Saquon Barkley found a crease in the left side of the offensive line to find daylight, which prompted Sean Mannion to raise his hands to signal a touchdown. Dameon Pierce caught my attention for the second day in a row. At first it was for turning a dump off reception into a nice catch-and-run gain. He looked natural as a pass-catcher and made a smooth transition turning upfield. Pierce also broke off a big gain as a runner. He’s got some juice. EAGLES INJURY UPDATES: Speaking about Jonathan Greenard prior to practice , Fangio said the veteran edge rusher is going to miss a good amount of training camp. And he said Greenard’s absence isn’t ideal in part because the Eagles are going to be asking him to do some things (such as dropping into coverage) he previously hasn’t been tasked with doing. In other news, Cameron Williams suffered an injury that prompted a visit to the medical tent. A cart originally came out for Williams, who is on the roster bubble entering his second season, but he was able to walk off the field. Something to monitor. SAFETY BATTLE UPDATES: Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II both saw first-team reps again. Fangio confirmed there’s a true competition going on at that spot. Neither player has done anything to create separation thus far. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATES: Andy Dalton was the first QB2 up in 7-on-7 but Tanner McKee was the primary backup in the firsts second-team series in 11-on-11. McKee seemed to get sacked a bunch but he did have a completion to a crossing Britain Covey, who was schemed open. Dalton wasn’t bad but didn’t do anything remarkable. Early on, this competition is a mid-off. Have yet to see any “wow” factor with Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers. Again, it’s early. Johnny Mundt continues to be the second tight end in 12 personnel with the starting offense. Hollywood Brown drew a defensive pass interference penalty deep down the field. The flag was either on Ambry Thomas or Andre’ Sam. Elijah Moore took a jet sweep with the first-team offense that resulted in no gain with the defense all over him. Jordan Davis was in good position to “sack” Hurts from a rush up the middle. Rough outing for Cole Payton, who impressed on Day 1. The rookie quarterback threw three interceptions in total. The first one might not have been his fault (can’t clearly recall if the pass was high of his target); the ball bounced off Danny Gray’s hands and into the hands of a diving A.J. Epenesa. Good play by an edge defender with a lack of coverage experience (related: Fangio praised Epenesa prior to Thursday’s practice ). The second one came on a throw up the seam that looked like it may as well have been intended for linebacker Chance Campbell. The third one was a throw to fellow rookie Keyshawn James-Newby in the flat for a sure pick six. I kind of like this progression for Payton, looking good on the first day but then getting humbled. Now we’ll see if he can bounce back or not. Cam Latu, facing tight coverage from Mac McWilliams, dropped a Dalton pass up the seam. Jake Elliott attempted some field goals early in practice. BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski had the best vantage point on those kicks and he informed me that Elliott went 6/7 with makes from 33, 35, 37, 43, 43, and 46 yards out. Elliott’s sole miss was a 40-yard attempt that went wide left, which is the direction that the wind was blowing. Jake Elliott getting some pre-practice warmup kicks in. pic.twitter.com/Dzyz4Dxgpy — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 30, 2026 The Eagles finished practice with a drill where the quarterbacks threw to every player on the team save for specialists, interior defensive linemen, and offensive linemen. The legendary Brian Dawkins was in the house for today’s practice. Shout out to Rita’s, a tradition at Eagles training camp since 2013. (Feel free to send me free stuff, Rita’s.) UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Friday. They’ll return to practice at 10:00 AM Eastern on Saturday morning. Then they’re off on Sunday.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Vic Fangio says Jihaad Campbell’s edge rusher days are over
summary: The Eagles were back to work on Thursday for their second practice of training camp, and we got to hear from defensive coordinator Vic Fangio before the team took the field. He talked about some of the position battles, what he’s seen from the edge rushers, and his thoughts on individual players. He also revealed […]
full_text: The Eagles were back to work on Thursday for their second practice of training camp, and we got to hear from defensive coordinator Vic Fangio before the team took the field. He talked about some of the position battles, what he’s seen from the edge rushers, and his thoughts on individual players. He also revealed that Jihaad Campbell will no longer be getting as many reps on the outside. Here’s what the DC had to say: On the safety position Fangio said that he wouldn’t say that the starting safety spot is Marcus Epps ’ job to lose, but said that the veteran has been in with the first team in the nickel group, and it’s Cooper DeJean in the base group. “But, [Michael] Carter’s doing fine too. It’s competition.” On Jihaad Campbell Fangio explained that it’s too early to tell whether Campbell will make any sort of leap heading into his second year, noting that Campbell missed the whole offseason and only had one training camp practice under his belt up to this point. Ultimately, he’s doing fine, but it’s just too early for any kind of deep analysis. While Campbell had opportunities on the outside last year with Nakobe Dean on the roster, Fangio admitted that some of it was valuable but some was also not great. He explained that those outside reps actually set him back in developing as an inside linebacker. The DC later said that it remains to be seen how much more they can put on Campbell’s plate, but that they were confident he’ll be able to step up. Fangio also said that the LB’s days of cross-training as an edge rusher are pretty much over, and while there might be a few times they ask him to move to the outside, it won’t be anything long term. On the DE group The DC expects Jonathan Greenard to miss most of training camp due to his pec strain, and while he’s a veteran in the league, the Eagles are asking him to do some new things — like dropping back in coverage — and those missed reps could be meaningful. Fangio thinks Greenard is capable of what they’re asking, and the edge rusher is doing a good job in meetings, but it’s not the same as practice experience. Fangio was also asked about AJ Epenesa and how he helps fill that gap without Greenard. He explained that it remains to be seen, but also gave the DE a huge compliment (by Fangio standards). “I told AJ [Epenesa] this — I told it to him in front of the whole team, too — for a guy that’s being asked to do a few things that he’s never done before, I thought he did a nice job yesterday with it.” And as for whether Greenard’s injury also opens the door for Brandon Graham to return to the roster, Fangio pointed to Howie Roseman as the person who can answer that. He later talked about how he has high expectations for Jalyx Hunt as he heads into his third year, saying that the DE is capable of being an exceptional player. Staying healthy is the big priority for Nolan Smith this season, with Fangio saying last season was choppy for the DE because he was dealing with some injuries and missed a lot of time. Still, he’s confident in Smith, and said both Smith and Hunt had good days in their first training camp practice. On Quinyon Mitchell “He’s got a great work ethic, demeanor, and he just picked up yesterday where he left off last year.” Other notables Fangio said that it’s helpful to be seeing a different offense this season, there’s a lot more moving parts which helps the Eagles defense. The DC joked that he’s on the PP plan with Uar Bernard — lots of patience, and lots of persistence. He noted that the first day of practice in the spring was the first time Bernard ever put a helmet on, and now pads will be a whole new thing, so it’s important that he and the team temper their expectations. It’s going to be a process. ILB Zack Baun will wear the green dot helmet and be the main signal caller this season — something he had experience doing the first half of last season when Nakobe Dean was injured. Fangio said that if they were to ever ask Baun to do something he’s not familiar with, he’ll fight through until he’s good at it, so he can do anything that’s needed. The DC said that Howie Roseman needs to save some money to pay DT Moro Ojomo next year, because he’s someone Fangio wants in this defense.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Jalen Carter’s teammates celebrate his new contract
summary: The Eagles made Jalen Carter the highest paid DT in NFL history, and his teammates couldn’t contain their excitement for an achievement they feel is well-deserved. Several players spoke to reporters following their first training camp and everyone was so happy for the DT, with Jalen Hurts telling a funny story, Jordan Davis talking about […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 28: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with Jordan Davis #90 after sacking Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills (not pictured) in the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles made Jalen Carter the highest paid DT in NFL history, and his teammates couldn’t contain their excitement for an achievement they feel is well-deserved. Several players spoke to reporters following their first training camp and everyone was so happy for the DT, with Jalen Hurts telling a funny story, Jordan Davis talking about how deserving Carter is, and Saquon Barkley saying the deal reflects how well the Eagles conduct business. Here’s some of what they said: Jalen Hurts The quarterback said that Carter is a great player and a great competitor, and he’s really happy for the young DT earning this new contract. Hurts went on to share that his wife put a $5 bill in his bag the first day of training camp — an inside joke between the couple — so the QB took the money and had jokes for Carter after his new deal was revealed. "I took that five-dollar bill, and I went and gave it to Jalen Carter, and I smacked it on his chest, and I said, 'Let me put five on top of that.'" 😂 pic.twitter.com/C9o7dzcUIi — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) July 29, 2026 Carter later smiled really big when asked abut Hurts giving him the $5 bill, and said it kept falling out of his pocket all day, but now he’s got it safely at home. The DT also joked that it would probably be worth $500 if the QB would have signed it first. On a serious note, though, Carter called Hurts “My guy” and talked about how they’ll sit together and have real serious conversations, saying the QB is like a big brother figure. Jordan Davis “I know he’s super excited about the whole process, and we always try to leave the league better than we found it — obviously, [Jalen Carter] reset the market. He’s the highest paid [DT] in NFL history, and that sets the bar for everybody else and the people behind him. So, I think that’s important and we love everything about it.” Davis said that Carter was excited about getting back to work and everyone knows the caliber of player he is, which is why he was drafted and then signed to a big deal. “Coming into the league, it’s a learning process. You have to learn to be a professional, you have to learn to navigate things — how to navigate problems we didn’t have in college, that we didn’t have in high school. Obviously, football is going to take care of itself, we have great coach in Coach Hurtt, but seeing him with all the off-the-field things, and seeing him persevere through everything he’s been through, that’s really the biggest thing that I can really give him a take away from.” Davis’ big thing was that he was proud of Carter, and he saw the DT attack his rehab this offseason with intention and focused on getting healthy. Saquon Barkley “[Jalen Carter] hasn’t even scratched — you guys don’t understand how scary it actually can be. So, I’m excited for him and his family and everything.” Barkley commented that it was a big contract but was also well-deserved, and he looks forward to seeing the next level Carter takes things to this season. He also was very complimentary to the Eagles and how they handle their business when it comes to paying players. “Something about this organization, something about Howie [Roseman], they just do it the right way in my opinion. There’s a reason this team’s been successful.” Barkley went on to say that he and Dallas Goedert were recently talking about being in Year 9, and the TE mentioned only missing the playoffs one season of his career. That’s all a reflection of how the organization handles things, including their roster building and approach to contracts — Barkley was also sure to note that his compliments for the Eagles were not meant to be a diss toward the Giants. “Obviously, Howie [Roseman] does a great job, but just from everybody up there on the top, it’s actually very impressive. And, if I ever became a GM or got enough money to own a team, I would run it how they do it here.” Other comments DeVonta Smith “I think it’s great. I like seeing guys get paid, and I told Howie [Roseman] he did a great job.” Lane Johnson “I was happy. I told him his rookie year that this is where he was headed. He had the potential to obviously be a great, dominating player in this league.” Zack Baun “The first thing I said was ‘Congratulations,’ and then I said, ‘They’re not paying you for what you did, but for what you’re about to do.‘”

title: Eagles Film Review: Betting on Jalen Carter makes sense
summary: The Eagles just agreed to a record-breaking contract extension with Jalen Carter this week, so I feel inspired to write about him. There are plenty of ways to analyze the deal. Others will break down the numbers, discuss the salary cap implications, and debate whether he was worth it. Those conversations are important, but they […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Detroit Lions at Lincoln Financial Field on November 16, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles just agreed to a record-breaking contract extension with Jalen Carter this week, so I feel inspired to write about him. There are plenty of ways to analyze the deal. Others will break down the numbers, discuss the salary cap implications, and debate whether he was worth it. Those conversations are important, but they aren’t the ones that I want to focus on here. Instead, I just want to focus on the film. It’s easy to forget that’s what it’s all about… When the Eagles traded up to draft Carter in 2023, I made my feelings pretty clear. This was from my rookie film review! “The most talented player in the class, regardless of position. An elite prospect as a disruptive three-technique, but he can do it all. He could play anywhere along the defensive line and would be fine. He’s a high-level prospect with outstanding traits and the film to back it up. He has an explosive element to his game and can win in so many ways. T he upside is as high as anyone in this class.” I actually don’t think Carter has already become the complete player I thought he could be. If anything, I still believe there’s another level for him to reach. His 2025 season was fine, but by the incredibly high standards he had already set, it wasn’t quite as dominant or consistent as I hoped. Injuries undoubtedly played a part, but when I watched his film again, the flashes are still extraordinary. The ability to completely take over a football game is still there. In my opinion, there is only one defensive lineman in the NFL whose overall talent level I would place above Carter’s today, and that’s Myles Garrett. Garrett has earned that status through years of elite production and remarkable consistency, and Carter still has to prove he can sustain that level over the course of a full season. Outside of Garrett, I don’t think there is another defensive lineman in football with a higher ceiling. Carter possesses an incredibly rare combination of explosiveness, power, flexibility, hand usage, and football intelligence that very few players have. That’s exactly why the Eagles were so comfortable making him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history. So rather than discussing the contract itself, let’s just talk about the player. Elite athletic profile Everything about Jalen Carter’s game starts with his athletic ability. There are plenty of powerful defensive tackles in the NFL, and there are plenty who win with quickness, but it is exceptionally rare to find a player who combines both traits at Carter’s size. At over 310 pounds, he possesses the explosiveness of a lightweight speed rusher whilst retaining the power to overwhelm interior offensive linemen. It is the foundation of everything he does as a pass rusher. I know this play doesn’t matter, but he’s above 310 pounds… Eagles Defense All22 thread vs. Washington. 1) Jalen Carter. Lol. That's one way to deal with a cut block. He's not a bad athlete is he?! Oren Burks was excellent coming downhill at avoiding blocks and making plays against the run. The Eagles' LB coach deserves a lot of credit! pic.twitter.com/5PcRZAFusD — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) January 28, 2025 One of the play-style comparisons I made during the 2023 draft process was Aaron Donald. That wasn’t because they are identical players, but because they create the same reaction when you study the film. Donald’s movement skills always looked unnatural for an interior defensive lineman. Carter gives me a similar feeling, only in a bigger frame. His combination of first-step explosiveness, lower-body power, flexibility and balance simply shouldn’t exist in a player of his size. 3) How many defensive tackles have you ever seen that look this athletic? Seriously, Carter weighed 314 pounds at the combine. He's a freak! The quickness and burst on this play just remind me so much of Aaron Donald. You don't see many linemen make this play. Donald weighed 285… pic.twitter.com/U4UNxKwRTi — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) December 2, 2024 It wasn’t a one-off, either… 10) Jalen Carter. Lol. He was so good in this game. The Eagles have a superstar. pic.twitter.com/MrrMzN45Nf — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 28, 2023 When you see him at his best, you remember what a physical freak he is. His burst forces offensive linemen onto the back foot immediately after the snap. His flexibility allows him to reduce his surface area and squeeze through gaps that most defensive tackles cannot exploit. His balance enables him to recover when blockers appear to have gained leverage, whilst his lower-body explosion allows him to transition from speed to power almost instantly. There are more explosive players in the league at other positions, but very few interior defenders possess Carter’s complete athletic profile. Elite first-step explosiveness If I had to identify one defining trait, it would be Carter’s first step. Hence, the Donald comparison. His get-off is exceptional and, when he times the snap correctly, he is almost impossible to block one-on-one. His burst off the football immediately forces offensive linemen into recovery mode. Rather than being able to dictate the rep, they are reacting almost instantly, opening their hips earlier than they would like and exposing themselves to inside counters. Carter’s first step doesn’t just help him penetrate the pocket. It creates the conditions for every other aspect of his pass-rush game. What makes his get-off even more dangerous is his timing. Carter has an outstanding feel for the snap count and repeatedly leaves the line of scrimmage a fraction before the offensive line is fully engaged. Half a step can be the difference between a clean punch from the guard and Carter already working past his shoulder. Few defensive tackles consistently win the race off the ball in the way Carter does, and it remains the defining characteristic of his game. I’ve always wondered if snap timing is something you can really coach, or if some players just have it. Jalen Carter just seems to have it. I mean, just stick him at edge and he can still time the snap… Jalen Carter on the EDGE 👀 pic.twitter.com/pEA4TCBtrX — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 27, 2023 A complete pass-rush toolbox Many elite pass rushers have one signature move that they repeatedly return to. Carter is different because he has answers for almost every situation an offensive lineman presents. His favorite move remains the violent inside club, where he attacks the guard’s outside shoulder before knocking away the hands and working back inside, but that is only one part of his pass-rush arsenal. Eagles' Defense Al22 thread vs. Packers. 1) I think the bye week came at the right time for Jalen Carter. This was the most '2024' version of Carter I have seen this year. I still think he's playing so many snaps that he can't consistently dominate, but he had some freaky-looking… pic.twitter.com/jNC8mTPrZL — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 12, 2025 Carter is equally comfortable winning with a club-swim, a long-arm bull rush, converting speed-to-power, or just bursting through a gap before the offensive linemen have time to think. He can pull offensive linemen off balance before swimming over the top, chain together multiple counters within the same rep or collapse the pocket by driving straight through the middle of a blocker. The variety is what makes him so difficult to prepare for. Offensive linemen cannot simply sit on one move because Carter is constantly adapting to the picture in front of him. One more club move? Oh, go on then. 2) There's a lot of bad clips I could post of Cunningham in coverage… but just watch Jalen Carter. My word. Backup OL or not, this guy is going to be a complete star. The speed and explosiveness he has is next…

title: Eagles News: Jalyx Hunt starts training camp strong
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 1: An initial look at Sean Mannion’s offense – PhillyVoiceJalyx Hunt had a great day. On one rep he had a 1-on-1 vs. Mailata, who was on an island. Hunt got Mailata leaning outside before jumping back inside […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Jalyx Hunt #58 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after an interception against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 1: An initial look at Sean Mannion’s offense – PhillyVoice Jalyx Hunt had a great day. On one rep he had a 1-on-1 vs. Mailata, who was on an island. Hunt got Mailata leaning outside before jumping back inside with a free path to Hurts, and he got the “sack.” On the next play Hunt then beat Mailata to the outside for another “sack,” although that one was more of a coverage sack. Hunt also had a tackle for loss on Tank Bigsby, and he just generally he set the edge well against the run. 10 Eagles camp observations: Jonathan Greenard’s injury, Jalen Hurts’ new offense – The Athletic Two buzzworthy players who stood out in practice: Hunt and running back Tank Bigsby. Jalyx Hunt forced pressure against the Eagles’ first-team offensive line. Bigsby showed some juice catching the ball out of the backfield and could carve a role on offense. Eagles practice observations: Sean Mannion’s offense starts clicking; Jalen Hurts under center; Jalyx Hunt hunts – Inquirer Hunting season. Greenard’s absence pushed Jalyx Hunt into the starting spot at right outside linebacker opposite Nolan Smith Jr. Hunt will likely play as many snaps as the other two this season. There’s an argument to be made that he should get more playing time than Smith. Nevertheless, he took advantage of his opportunities with Greenard out. Hunt shot into the backfield unblocked and forced Hurts to check down to Cooper on one play-action pass that came from under center. He blew up tight end Dallas Goedert with an edge rush and Hurts had to hurry a dump to Bigsby that wasn’t caught. And he beat Mailata on back-to-back rushes — one with an inside move and the other from the outside — that blew up pass plays. Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts and new offense show encouraging signs – BGN JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Just like the headline says, there were encouraging signs from the Eagles’ quarterback and the team’s new offense. Was it perfect? No, it wasn’t. There were drops. There were procedural penalties, as Lane Johnson brought up during his post-practice press conference. But this offense looked much more functional than the version that was largely dominated by Vic Fangio’s defense during the team’s spring practices. Training Camp Observations, Day 1: A Good, Boring Practice – Go Birds! Podcast Eliot Shorr-Parks is joined by Brandon Lee Gowton and Tucker Bagley to help break down the first day of 2026 Training Camp. The guys dive in to a solid day for Jalen Hurts, a slow day for the defense and express concern for a couple of the team’s rookies. Updated Roster Prediction – Iggles Blitz QB – 3 – Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton. The team has four QBs for now. Andy Dalton is the odd man out in my projection. The Eagles could look to trade him if some team wants a veteran this summer. They could also trade McKee, but only for a good return. The only way that happens is if another team loses a key QB due to injury and still wants to be competitive this season. I’m guessing McKee remains with the Eagles. Payton has to play his way onto the roster. Kyle McCord couldn’t do that last year. I think Payton is a better prospect and the team will do what they can to hold onto him because of his upside. Eagles training camp diary: The Sean Mannion era begins with a bang – PHLY Jalen Hurts has a new mantra. Listening to Nick Sirianni’s team address at the start of training camp, Jalen Hurts wrote down what will likely be his mantra for 2026: 100% alignment, 0% entitlement. Whether the phrase originated from Sirianni or if it was Hurts’ interpretation, Hurts opened his first press conference of the season emphasizing “discipline and unity” at the center of everything. Parse that how you choose, but it’s a message that underscores something Sirianni also harped on during the spring. When everyone is rowing in the same direction, this team has been more successful than just about anyone. Hurts seems to be acknowledging that from the jump this year. It’s fair to wonder if correlation doesn’t equal causation here. The 2024 Eagles had plenty of tension before going on to win Super Bowl LIX and the 2022 may have had the best “vibes” of any team I’ve covered, but it’s noteworthy nonetheless that Hurts and Sirianni are keying in on this so much at the start of the season in reflection of last year. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates – ESPN There were some encouraging signs from the Eagles’ new-look offense on Day 1 of camp. The learning curve they’re working through is obvious — there was one sequence where a pre-snap penalty was followed by a botched running play when Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley were on different pages. But there were also moments where things clicked, like on a hookup between Hurts and DeVonta Smith where Hurts dropped to his right and zipped a strike to his now-No. 1 receiver down the left seam with Quinyon Mitchell tight in coverage. Hurts worked primarily under center and targeted the middle of the field a good amount, departures from how he has generally operated to this point in the NFL. There was enough good mixed in to consider it a positive opening to the summer. Jalen Carter vows huge contract will only motivate him to work harder than ever – NBCSP He swears nothing will change. Nothing at all. Jalen Carter, $152 million wealthier than he was a couple days ago, promised Wednesday that becoming the highest-paid interior lineman in NFL history won’t change who he is or how he goes about his business. “I don’t really think the money is ever gonna change me,” Davis said after the first practice of training camp. When you get picked in the first round and you’re a top-10 pick, you kind of get a little bit of decent money. And that didn’t change me. I still came in, I had a goal, let the team know and the fans know that the goal was to get a championship. And it happened. But it’s a new contract and it’s time to get more championships for the city of Philly.” 2026 NFL All-Rookie Team projections: 25 impact newcomers on offense, defense and special teams – NFL.com TE Eli Stowers. In his four-year run with the Eagles, A.J. Brown averaged 130 targets per season. So, in the wake of Brown’s trade to New England, Philadelphia has an obvious pass-catching vacuum. Who will fill it? First-round receiver Makai Lemon certainly factors in as a slot machine to complement DeVonta Smith, but I wouldn’t overlook the potential impact of this second-round tight end. Truth be told, Stowers feels more like a supersized receiver at 6-4, 239 pounds. A converted quarterback who showcased rare athleticism at the NFL Scouting Combine, the reigning John Mackey Award winner (college football’s most outstanding tight end) wasn’t drafted to be an in-line blocker. But in an NFL that’s increasingly obsessed with multi-TE formations, new Eagles OC Sean Mannion could deploy the rookie in a playmaking role to complement veteran mainstay Dallas Goedert and recently inked blocking tight end Johnny Mundt. Spadaro: The Eagles once again ‘just do it the right way’ – PhiladelphiaEagles.com It has been a minute, hasn’t it? The “E-A-G-L-E-S, EAGLES” chants. The intensity of practice. The voices of coaches. Players chirping. On a picture-perfect Wednesday at the Jefferson Health Training Complex, your favorite football team returned to the practice fields for Day 1 of the 2026 Training Camp and it was everything you’d hoped it would be. Good, crisp football. Obvious competition throughout the roster. Optimism throughout, along with the understanding that it is a small step in a series of many, and that there is a whole…

summary: LATROBE – The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to ease into the season as it was another fairly laid-back practice to begin training camp. The team emphasized individual drills today, in between giving us some telling team period and two-minute drill reps. It’s time for us to look at who helped their stock and those whose stock […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers Roman Wilson (14) participates in training camp drills at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE – The Pittsburgh Steelers continue to ease into the season as it was another fairly laid-back practice to begin training camp. The team emphasized individual drills today, in between giving us some telling team period and two-minute drill reps. It’s time for us to look at who helped their stock and those whose stock is trending down after the second training camp practice of 2026. Stock up WR Roman Wilson It’s impossible to deny how Roman Wilson has performed through two practices in Latrobe. Wilson is the third receiver, primarily lining up in the slot in 11-personnel sets, and has been Aaron Rodgers’ most common target through the first few practices. Both Rodgers and DK Metcalf were complimentary of the work Wilson has put in this offseason on Tuesday, and the former third-round pick has backed it up so far. Although it is early and pads have not come on yet, Wilson seems to have a strong hold of the WR3 role for now. QB Will Howard Second-year quarterback Will Howard took a major step up today. He had several quality layered throws over the middle of the field between defenders. In what was one of the bigger plays of the entire practice, Howard found a wide-open Kaden Wetjen on what appeared to be a broken coverage down the right sideline that would have gone for a 60-yard touchdown in a game. Will Howard connects with Kaden Wetjen on a downfield shot for what would have been about a 60 yard touchdown. — Joey Bray (@byjoeybray) July 30, 2026 Howard was given the honors to quarterback the second and final two-minute drill of practice. He appeared to be in control, making several quick throws across the middle of the field to get the offense over midfield. However, the drive ended poorly with an interception of a double-clutched throw of Howard by safety Sebastian Castro that ended practice. Although it the day didn’t end well for Howard, there was far more good than bad for the young quarterback. WR Kaden Wetjen The rookie fourth-rounder out of Iowa has been first in line to catch punts from Cameron Johnston in each of the first two practices. We also got to see our first flash of him as a receiver, as he was on the receiving end of a Will Howard throw downfield as I mentioned above. Wetjen did not have much usage as a receiver in college, and when he did, it was often screen passes. It was encouraging to see Wetjen on the receiving end of a downfield shot, as he figures to be the team’s featured return man as well. Stock down QB Mason Rudolph Through two practices, we have seen young quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar step up and make big time throws over the middle and down the field. While Mason Rudolph has not done anything particularly bad thus far, he has not had a “wow” throw, if you will. The quarterback had what would have been a big play down the field to Pat Freiermuth batted down by Asante Samuel Jr. who made a diving play to break up the pass. Asante Samuel Jr. with a nice downfield pass breakup on a pass from Mason Rudolph intended for Pat Freiermuth. Samuel is stepping up in these first two days of practice. — Joey Bray (@byjoeybray) July 30, 2026 For Rudolph, it seems to be backup or bust in a battle with Howard. While Howard put together several nice plays today and was rewarded with quarterbacking the second two-minute drill to end practice, Rudolph could only watch. It will come down to the preseason games and become clearer who the Steelers prefer once pads go on, but Howard was favored more than Rudolph on this day. RB/WR Eli Heidenreich It’s not so much about what Heidenreich has done; it’s simply the fact that he isn’t getting much run through the first few practices. The seventh-round pick had a lot of hype coming into camp, and I had thought he could potentially challenge Kaleb Johnson for the RB3 role, but it has been Johnson getting those reps over Heidenreich consistently to start camp. It is very early on, and Heidenreich has been getting work as a punt returner. His versatility as a runner, receiver, and returner should give him a good shot to make the team; it’s just a matter of getting those opportunities and making the most of them. No reason to have any concerns about him yet, but the lack of usage gives his stock a downward trend. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers training camp: Will Howard takes command of backup QB battle
summary: LATROBE — If a quarterback battle is what you wanted, you’ve certainly got it. In each of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ first two practices of training camp, a young quarterback has stepped up and made noteworthy plays to raise their respective stocks. Yesterday was rookie Drew Allar, today was second-year signal-caller Will Howard’s turn. Plus, a […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard (18) participates in training camp drills at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE — If a quarterback battle is what you wanted, you’ve certainly got it. In each of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ first two practices of training camp, a young quarterback has stepped up and made noteworthy plays to raise their respective stocks. Yesterday was rookie Drew Allar, today was second-year signal-caller Will Howard’s turn. Plus, a defensive back continues to show he is worthy of a high snap count while Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf have a strong day. Let’s dive into today’s training camp notebook. Will Howard has a big day After a quiet Day One, Howard made several high-quality throws throughout the second practice. He had a nice rip over the middle of the field to Robert Tonyan during a team drill and hit Levi Wentz on a sideline shot for a gain of 15. The highlight of the day, though – and of camp thus far – was a deep pass to the right side that was caught by Kaden Wetjen for a 60 yard touchdown. Like Allar on Day One, he did have some errors. Leading the second two-minute drill, Howard double clutched a throw, letting it go a bit late, which allowed Sebastian Castro to pick it off and win the second two-minute drill for the defense. That said, it was still a day where there was far more good than bad for the Ohio State product. It’s obviously still very early, but with Howard’s big second day compared to a somewhat pedestrian start for Mason Rudolph, the QB2 battle is heating up, and the second-year quarterback may have just put himself in the early lead. Asante Samuel Jr continues hot start Samuel had two big plays on Day One of training camp , and he picked up where he left off on Day Two. During team drills, Pat Freiermuth sprung open down the right sideline. Mason Rudolph launched a pass in his direction, but Samuel made a break on the ball, getting over and beating Freiermuth to the pass to bat it down and prevent a big gain. The depth in the secondary was a big talking point all offseason, and Samuel is stacking high-quality days together and showing he should be a high-volume player come September. Drew Allar has another solid day While Howard stole the show with several high-quality throws, Allar had another strong day himself. He ripped a throw over the middle to Brandon Smith on a crosser that went for a big gain, and had multiple connections with A.T. Perry throughout the day, including a layered pass over the top of one linebacker and underneath a safety for a chunk play. The footwork and rhythm are getting better, and if you were to compare his feet now to his Penn State film, the improvement is clear. Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf’s growing chemistry QB1 and WR1 of the Steelers should look more in lockstep entering Year Two together, and they look far better now than they did at this time a year ago. The pair connected several times during team drills for chunk plays over the middle of the field, and a long pass down the sideline where Rodgers fit the ball in over Jamel Dean. The final toss-and-catch came with Metcalf going up and over Daylen Everette for a touchdown to give the offense a win in the first two-minute drill. If the offense is going to take a step forward, Rodgers and Metcalf being in sync with one another will be a big reason why. Other notes I alluded to it earlier, but the constant targeting of the middle of the field is promising and hopefully something that carries over into actual games being played. Roman Wilson continues to get a ton of targets. He made a nice leaping catch on the sideline during the two-minute drill. Rodgers ripped a seed between Cole Holcomb and Payton Wilson to Pat Freiermuth for a nice gain. That arm talent hasn’t fallen off at all. DeShon Elliott returned in a more heavy workload capacity after being limited on Wednesday. Let us know what you think in the comments . It was the first time Steelers fans could watch favorites, newcomers, and the 2026 draft […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 11: Drew Allar #16 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in action at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on June 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve made it. It’s here. Football is back and the shiny new toys are being taken out of the box. The Steelers took the field for the first organized practice of training camp at St. Vincent College on Wednesday morning. It was the first time Steelers fans could watch favorites, newcomers, and the 2026 draft class at the same time, including third-round pick and former Penn State quarterback Drew Allar. Allar underwent significant changes to his processing and footwork during OTAs and minicamp, being broken down and built back up again by new head coach Mike McCarthy. Following a strong career at Penn State, but one that left much to be desired, Allar explained after practice how McCarthy is impacting his season. “Definitely makes you be very detail oriented and have a purpose behind every rep,” Allar said . “I think that’s the biggest thing I’ve learned.” Allar missed half the season with a broken ankle but was the first of three players taken by the Steelers in the third round. In 45 career games, 35 starts from his sophomore to senior year, Allar threw for 7,402 yards, 61 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. The lack of accuracy and clutch performances in big games hurt Allar’s stock and was never able to win the big game at Penn State. The slate is wiped clean in the NFL, especially with a more accomplished and well respected offensive head coach. “Have a purpose and intent behind everything in those individual drills where you’re throwing to stationary targets and do all the hard work there,” Allar said, describing what he’s been working on. “When it’s time to go play 7-on-7 or 11-on-11 football just go play ball and coach it up after.” Allar began his college career with an FBS record 311 passes before throwing an interception. He finished his career with the Nittany Lions first all-time in completion percentage 63.2%. McCarthy had success working with Aaron Rodgers, Dak Prescott, and other quarterbacks in the past to get the most out of their potential. Allar has all the tools necessary to be a starting quarterback, but significant work remains. “When it’s in those [individual] drills, making sure I’m doing the correct footwork, correct reads, whatever the case is, and being very intentional with that,” Allar said. The Steelers’ first preseason game is Thursday, August 13 at 7:00 p.m. against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium and will be the first time Allar takes the field inside their home stadium.

title: Seahawks 2026 training camp: Day 5 news, notes and injury updates
summary: The Seattle Seahawks returned to the practice field after taking Wednesday off. Thursday marked the first padded practice of training camp, which means the intensity can ramp up and the feel of real football is getting closer. full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JULY 25: AJ Barner #88 of the Seattle Seahawks runs with the ball during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on July 25, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks returned to the practice field after taking Wednesday off. Thursday marked the first padded practice of training camp, which means the intensity can ramp up and the feel of real football is getting closer. Fans won’t get a glimpse of padded reps until Friday, so media-only accounts will have to suffice for today. Let’s go through the notable events from Day 5 of Seahawks training camp! Seahawks training camp news and notes Deven Eastern returns to practice Seahawks rookie nose tackle Deven Eastern had been largely absent from mandatory minicamp and OTAs due to injury, and started this year on the PUP list. He passed a physical on Thursday and is all good to go, which means just Nick Emmanwori and Zach Charbonnet are still on PUP. Rookie Deven Eastern has been activated from PUP list. #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/K7i9J7yeBi — Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) July 30, 2026 Mike Macdonald: Tyrice Knight having a great training camp After taking over as a midseason starter as a rookie, Tyrice Knight’s injury issues in 2025 led to some early season struggles before Drake Thomas took over his starting job. The third-year player out of UTEP has started camp well enough for Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald to sing his praises. “Tyrice has had a great camp. He really has. He’s done a great job. There’s ways to get him out there. That’s a great example of how you don’t need to be counting the people ahead of you and where do I stand in depth chart and all this. Just put my best foot forward and let us figure out how to get you on the field. Put that burden on the coaches to make sure that we got the best guys out there. He’s definitely applying pressure right now, which is really great.” Mike Macdonald addresses currently injured Seahawks players The likes of Jake Bobo and Julian Neal have been absent from recent practices due to injury. It doesn’t sounds like Mike Macdonald is too concerned about any of the injuries. “Nothing long term. Just a couple of things they’re working through, camp type of stuff. It’s a bummer, but we will get them back soon.” Brandon Pili, Jamie Sheriff, and Jared Ivey were new non-participants on Thursday, and similarly there doesn’t seem to be reason to sound the alarm bells. “Well, they’re dealing with some things. Some training camp things, but they’ll be back. Nothing crazy going on right now, just some training camp stuff.” Nick Emmanwori attends practice from the sidelines Seattle’s star defensive back is on the mend after ankle surgery, which is why he’s on PUP . While it’s been reported that it won’t likely be a long-term absence for Emmanwori, Coach Macdonald is playing it close to the vest as far as a timetable for his return. “He’s in an adverse situation. He’s attacking it. That’s all you can ask him to do. He’s made a lot of progress, which is exciting. It’s one of these things where you don’t want to put a timetable on it because you don’t want to limit him but just go rip it every day. We got great people surrounded by him and let’s go see where we get. He’s returned so far. He’s done a great job. It’s not going to be easy, but he’s just the man for the job.” Andre Fuller, Michael Dansby level up in pads While Julian Neal did not practice, Seattle’s other two rookie corners did participate. Dansby has raised eyebrows with his ball skills and general performances in 1-on-1s and in team reps. Here’s what Coach Macdonald had to say about their first practice in pads. “To see them make plays, playing football, it’s great. It’s an indication of the work they have put in. They’ve done a great job up to this point. They’re rookies, so they are swimming a little bit schematically, but that’s as expected, and they just got to kind of work through the fog until we start making plays, like today, and gain more confidence and just keep rolling.” Sam Darnold on having running backs more involved as receivers For the first time during camp, Sam Darnold had a media availability session. The Seahawks’ second-year starting quarterback was asked about his stable of running backs and the benefits of having them as legitimate receiving threats. “I think it helps the quarterback a ton because it does present a different problem for the defense. Sometimes the defense assumes, especially on third down, that the running back’s going to stay in and protect so they can build their pressures off of that. But when you’re getting five guys out on a route and you’re in scat protection, sometimes you’ve got to throw hot, and the defense is going to make it hot. If you get the protections right, you’re not hot, and the running back’s out on a route, sometimes that’s a mismatch with a linebacker, especially with a guy like [Jadarian Price] or George [Holani]. We’ve got a ton of backs in the backfield this year that can make linebackers and safeties miss. So, it’s going to be really fun to see what those guys can do coming out of the backfield.” O-line vs. D-line gets more competitive You love to see the give-and-take. And you love to read about both of these things regarding Rylie Mills and Anthony Bradford… especially Mills. 1-on-1 pass-rush drills in full pads=the most real football in #Seahawks training camp. Byron Murphy bull-rushed into Christian Haynes' chest, blew him into the backfield Rylie Mills beat Anthony Bradford with an inside rip move. Bradford came back, stopped Mills' spin move💪 — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) July 30, 2026 George Holani shows off his pass protection chops It’s expected that third-year Seahawks running back George Holani will feature more in the offense. One of the reasons? His pass protection. One of the reasons John Schneider raved about George Holani after the Super Bowl was how he fared in pass protection during the playoffs. The GM called it “elite.” A good example in this blitz pickup drill during the Seahawks’ first padded practice of camp. Holani is first up. pic.twitter.com/W61PnZFJ0m — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) July 30, 2026 George Holani going against Ernest Jones in pass pro 1-on-1s. #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/FJyt5pzYo7 — Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) July 30, 2026 Some familiar work for Robbie Ouzts Robbie Ouzts was a tight end in college and a fullback in the NFL. With Brian Fleury as offensive coordinator, I would anticipate Ouzts having more of a role outside of being an I-formation fullback. Fullback Robbie Ouzts, whom the #Seahawks converted from tight end last year as a rookie, is getting back to his University of Alabama position at his second #Seahawks training camp. Ouzts getting right-end work on duo blocks with offensive tackles in position drills. pic.twitter.com/kl0yJ5UoAY — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) July 30, 2026 As noted earlier, fans return to practice on Friday, July 31 at 1 pm PT. Reminder: Field Gulls live at Seahawks training camp! In just a few days Field Gulls will be on site as part of the Seahawks Syndicate crew, which features myself, Bryce Coutts, Dan Viens, and Brandon Cain (who won’t be attending in-person this year). We’ll be at three practices on Aug. 5, 7, and 8, with live podcasts streaming from Fast Fashion Brewing in SoDo! You’re invited to a special Town Hall style show on Aug. 7 at 7:30 pm. Myself, Bryce, and Josh Hite are among the Field Gulls staff that will be at camp in some capacity during these days. title: NFL insider Mike Garofalo: Leonard Williams extension coming ‘before Week 1’
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have some big contract decisions coming up on their big defensive tackles. While time is on their side regarding Byron Murphy II, who isn’t even extension eligible until next offseason, this year is the last of Leonard Williams’ three-year contract. Williams confirmed that extension talks have been opened, but he didn’t go […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JUNE 11: Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks talks with the media at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on June 11, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have some big contract decisions coming up on their big defensive tackles. While time is on their side regarding Byron Murphy II, who isn’t even extension eligible until next offseason, this year is the last of Leonard Williams’ three-year contract. Williams confirmed that extension talks have been opened, but he didn’t go into any real details beyond that. If you’re already antsy regarding the future of one of Seattle’s most important players, perhaps this will put you at ease. In a guest appearance on Daily Puck Drop with Jason Puckett, longtime NFL insider Mike Garofalo indicated that a deal is imminent. How imminent? We shouldn’t be worrying about it by the time the Seahawks hang their latest Super Bowl banner. “It is going to be a big number,” Garofalo said. “It’ll be before Week 1, I’ll put it to you like that, and it’s going to be a big number from my understanding. “A lot of teams now are playing defenses that are really relying upon defensive tackles. The Eagles paid both of their guys [Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis] a combined $64 million per year at defensive tackle. It used to be the defensive ends were getting all the money—I mean DTs got paid along the way, but now it’s like really big money for these guys because a lot of these defenses, particularly the Eagles, rely upon these defensive tackles to create havoc up front. Same for the Seahawks and what they’re doing.” Garofalo is referencing Jalen Carter’s $38 million/year extension, which makes him (for now) the highest paid defensive tackle in the league. Jordan Davis’ contract extension was three years for $78 million, or $26 million/year. Williams’ existing deal is worth $64.5 million and averages out to a little bit over $21 million/year, which is a bargain given his productivity. Presumably, a big boost in pay is coming for the 32-year-old if/when that new contract is agreed to.

title: Celebrating 25 seasons of Seahawks football at Lumen Field
summary: We are less than two months away from another season of Seattle Seahawks football, and this year is going to carry some additional meaning for the team. 2026 will be the Seahawks’ 25th season at Lumen Field, which has become a haven for football fans across the Pacific Northwest since its opening in 2002. Over […]
full_text: We are less than two months away from another season of Seattle Seahawks football, and this year is going to carry some additional meaning for the team. 2026 will be the Seahawks’ 25th season at Lumen Field, which has become a haven for football fans across the Pacific Northwest since its opening in 2002. Over that time, Seattle has accumulated a record of 140-68 at the stadium, including a 12-2 mark in the postseason. From Matt Hasselbeck and Mike Holmgren to Sam Darnold and Mike Macdonald, the Seahawks have had a lot of noteworthy names be a part of their organization since the early aughts, all of whom have helped to make Lumen Field a special place to watch a football game. For starters, it’s important to note the sense of stability that the stadium has provided for the ‘Hawks over the last few decades. The franchise’s latter years at the Kingdome were not great, especially after Chuck Knox departed for a second stint with the Los Angeles Rams in 1992. That same year, the Seahawks finished with a franchise-worst 2-14 record under former Raiders head coach Tom Flores, and the team would not climb above .500 again until 1999. Amidst this stretch of mediocrity, the Seahawks’ future in the Emerald City was anything but certain. In 1995, then-owner Ken Behring tried to move the team elsewhere before the NFL threatened to heavily fine him after he failed to properly apply for relocation. Even still, the Seahawks’ long-term future at the Kingdome was not certain. With the help of new owner Paul Allen, construction on the then-named Seahawks Stadium began in 1998. As the new stadium was being built, the team played its last two seasons at the Kingdome before temporarily moving to the University of Washington’s Husky Stadium for the next two years, beginning in 2000. In 2002, Seahawks Stadium finally opened, ending a years-long battle to keep the Seahawks in Seattle and build them a new stadium. The team’s move to the new stadium coincided with a move from the AFC West back to the NFC West following 25 years in the AFC. In the NFC’s revamped Western division, Seattle would host the 49ers, Cardinals, and Rams for one regular season game at Seahawks Stadium every year for the foreseeable future. After going 3-5 at home in 2002, the Seahawks would rocket to the top of the NFC West between 2003 and 2007, reaching the playoffs every year and winning four consecutive division titles along the way. Seattle went undefeated at home in 2003 and ‘05, going 10-0 at the then-named Qwest Field in the latter season between the regular season and playoffs. This included the first-ever conference title victory in Seahawks history, a 34-14 rout of the Carolina Panthers in the 2005 NFC Championship Game. All in all, Seattle went 42-14 at home during the stadium’s seven years with Holmgren as head coach, including a 38-13 mark in the regular season and a 4-1 record in postseason play. If you’re curious, here’s a year-by-year look at the Seahawks’ home records between 2002 and 2008: Seahawks’ home records at Seahawks Stadium/Qwest Field under Mike Holmgren (2002-2008) 2002: 3-5 2003: 8-0 2004: 5-4 (5-3 regular season, 0-1 playoffs) 2005: 10-0 (8-0 regular season, 2-0 playoffs) 2006: 6-3 (5-3 regular season, 1-0 playoffs) 2007: 8-1 (7-1 regular season, 1-0 playoffs) 2008: 2-6 Total: 42-14 (38-13 regular season, 4-1 playoffs) Jim L. Mora’s one-year stint as HC in 2009 ended with a mediocre 4-4 finish at home, but Seattle got back to defending its home turf under former USC head coach Pete Carroll in 2010. That year, the Seahawks won the NFC West at 7-9 and knocked off the defending champion New Orleans Saints in the electric wild-card win that was the Beast Quake game. As the Legion of Boom rose to prominence in the early 2010s, the then-named CenturyLink Field became one of the toughest places to play in the NFL. The Seahawks went 26-2 at home from 2012 to 2014, clinching back-to-back NFC titles there in 2013 and ‘14 before heading to the Meadowlands to win Super Bowl 48 at the close of 2013. Around this time, CenturyLink Field battled with Kansas City’s Arrowhead Stadium for the loudest stadium in the world. In September of 2013, the 12s set the Guinness World Record for crowd noise at 131.9 decibels during a game against the 49ers. Throughout the season, CenturyLink Field went toe-to-toe with Arrowhead’s noise levels, with the 12s setting a new record of 137.6 decibels while facing the Saints that December. Although Arrowhead later reclaimed this record in 2014, the 12s remain among the loudest sports fans around. Beginning with the 2015 season, the Seahawks’ home advantage began to fade a bit, going 4-4 at CenturyLink Field in both 2017 and 2019. Despite Seattle winning at least seven of its home games in both 2016 and 2020, these would be the last high points of the Pete Carroll era. The 2021 season was the worst of the worst, as the Seahawks went 3-5 at Lumen Field en route to a 7-10 finish overall. After 2020, Seattle never won more than five home games in a season again under Carroll, going 5-4 in 2022 and 5-3 in ‘23. Seahawks’ home records at Qwest/CenturyLink/Lumen Field under Pete Carroll (2010-2023) 2010: 6-3 (5-3 regular season, 1-0 playoffs) 2011: 4-4 2012: 8-0 2013: 9-1 (7-1 regular season, 2-0 playoffs) 2014: 9-1 (7-1 regular season, 2-0 playoffs) 2015: 5-3 2016: 8-1 (7-1 regular season, 1-0 playoffs) 2017: 4-4 2018: 6-2 2019: 4-4 2020: 7-2 (7-1 regular season, 0-1 playoffs) 2021: 3-5 2022: 5-4 2023: 5-3 Total: 83-37 (77-36 regular season, 6-1 playoffs) The Seahawks’ struggles at home continued under Mike Macdonald in 2024, going 3-6 at Lumen Field in the first year of the post-Pete Carroll era. However, Seattle flipped the script in 2025, winning six of its last seven home games in the regular season to climb to a 14-3 finish and the NFC’s first-round bye. The renewed dominance at Lumen Field continued into the postseason, with the Seahawks taking care of business against the 49ers and Rams at home on the way to their third conference title and winning their second Super Bowl championship in the Niners’ building . With another Super Bowl title in tow, Seattle is poised to keep up the home momentum from last year. Much like the glory days of years past, Lumen Field is once again among the most difficult places for opposing teams to play. What is your favorite Seahawks memory at Lumen Field? Jordan Schultz reported on Wednesday that the Cleveland Browns have met with Clowney for their own possible reunion. He noted that an NFC West team had also expressed […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 11: Defensive end Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Seattle Seahawks recovers a fumble to score a touchdown over the San Francisco 49ers during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium on November 11, 2019 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are apparently still monitoring the veteran edge rusher market, including someone who has a history with both the Seahawks and head coach Mike Macdonald. Jordan Schultz reported on Wednesday that the Cleveland Browns have met with Clowney for their own possible reunion. He noted that an NFC West team had also expressed interest in his services, then fellow NFL insider Aaron Wilson went a step further and said both the Seahawks and Houston Texans have kept tabs on the 33-year-old. Former top overall #NFLDraft pick, three-time Pro Bowl edge Jadeveon Clowney visited #Browns today and has interest from #Texans and #Seahawks among several other teams as his market continues to grow, per league sources Clowney lives and trains in Houston and told @KPRC2 this… https://t.co/kSeRPpKttk pic.twitter.com/99FSbWzW1I — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) July 29, 2026 Clowney last played for the Dallas Cowboys, appearing in 13 games and recording 8.5 sacks, only one sack behind his career high, which he managed with both the Texans and his one season in Mike Macdonald’s Baltimore Ravens defense. The former number one overall pick has played for six teams since the Texans traded him to the Seahawks in 2019, when he had just three sacks but recorded a pick-six, a fumble return touchdown, and led the team with 13 QB hits. Unlike in 2019, when Clowney was effectively tasked to be Seattle’s primary pass rusher on a sub-par defense, he wouldn’t have such a situation in a second go-round. Add in his ability to play the run and it’s easy to see why, despite Clowney’s injury history and bouncing around the league, the Seahawks might kick the tires on a Clowney reunion. Ultimately, the interest may just max out at exactly that, especially when Seattle already signed Dante Fowler Jr earlier in the offseason. We’ll keep tabs on whether or not the Seahawks make a move for one more veteran before the regular season starts.

full_text: TAMPA, FL - NOVEMBER 10: The San Francisco 49ers head to the field before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on November 10, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. The 49ers defeated the Buccaneers 23-20. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Why Deebo Samuel’s surprising return to Bay makes sense for receiver-needy 49ers “The agreement was reached with the free-agent wide receiver just one year after the team granted Samuel’s trade request with a deal that sent him to the Washington Commanders. NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport was first to report the news of the agreement.” 49ers insider: It’s reasonable to expect Ricky Pearsall to miss the 2026 season “If they had decided to have the surgery, say in February or March or whenever, you’re not giving it the full time to recover on its own, but also you’re probably going to miss the season anyway,” Maiocco said. “So I think that they made a calculated attempt to hope that thing would heal on its own, like it often does. And once it didn’t, or it hasn’t, now it’s time for the 49ers and Ricky Pearsall to decide what they want to do.” Raheem Morris is giving 49ers’ defense a makeover: ‘I think everything’s different’ (paywall) “I think everything’s different,” Williams said. “We’ve been going against the same defense in a team environment since I’ve been here. It’s always been the four-down front.” Early signs of a defensive makeover under new 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris have been hard to miss. Five-man fronts. Sticky coverage. Disguised shells. “I was talking to Fred about that,” quarterback Brock Purdy said. “Like it’s just, it is different. In camp, it’s usually the four-down traditional stud defensive lineman with three linebackers and a strong quarter shell defense. Now it’s like, all right, we got five down. He gives us all these different kinds of looks and the shell’s always changing. Raheem’s done a good job with, I think, trying to disguise things against the quarterback but also the techniques that the DBs are playing with now, too, that’s a whole other thing.” ….A big emphasis for Morris since the spring has been about affording his players enough schematic simplicity to play fast. Saleh preached the same thing last season. Returning cornerback Renardo Green was asked about the differences, as the incumbent starter at a position that Morris has specifically coached before across multiple stops as an assistant. “It’s easier to play faster,” Green said as a credit to Morris, “and I feel like he’s finer, more detailed with just realistic things. It’s a lot less thinking.” 49ers work out three running backs after Jordan James injury “Blackshear entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Buffalo Bills in 2022 but has spent his regular-season career with the Carolina Panthers. Over 41 games (two starts), he has rushed for 203 yards and three touchdowns while adding 16 receptions for 138 receiving yards. title: Deebo Samuel is back with the 49ers on a one-year deal
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are bringing back an old friend. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel is signing a 1-year deal worth up to $7 million. This comes after the news that Ricky Pearsall might not play in 2026. Earlier on Thursday, we asked what Deebo was up to. We’re about to find out. The “up to” […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 04: Washington Commanders wide receiver Deebo Samuel (1) enters the field before the game between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles on January 04, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are bringing back an old friend. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel is signing a 1-year deal worth up to $7 million. This comes after the news that Ricky Pearsall might not play in 2026 . Earlier on Thursday, we asked what Deebo was up to . We’re about to find out. The “up to” $7 million is important, as it’s a sign that Samuel signed an incentive-laden deal where he’ll have to reach specific benchmarks to earn the full $7 million. Deebo needs no introduction. He spent the entirety of his career in the Bay Area before a one-year stint with the Commanders last year. Samuel saw more targets last season than he had since 2021. He finished the season with 72 receptions for 727 yards and five touchdowns. Most of Deebo’s targets came near the line of scrimmage. His average air yards per target was the lowest since 2022, at 5.3. Of those 99 targets, 67 came under 10 yards. Washington used Samuel primarily as a slot receiver. He ran 260 routes in the slot, compared to 141 out wide. It’s worth noting that Samuel also ran 15 routes from the backfield. If the 49ers are looking for somebody to take some of the workload off Christian McCaffrey with Jordan James sidelined, who better than the player for whom we coined the term “wideback”? We’re projecting here, but Samuel would likely play in the slot while Stribling gets familiar with “Z.” That is, unless Demarcus Robinson or Christian Kirk prove that they can contribute as outside receivers in this offense. It’ll be interesting to see how much Deebo plays over the likes of Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Kirk (once he’s healthy), and Robinson. The good news is Stribling is versatile, and Deebo knows the offense, so you can use both players in multiple spots, with Mike Evans as the true “X” receiver.

title: 49ers work out 3 RBs, including former Bears starter
summary: The San Francisco 49ers announced that they hosted three running backs for a workout on Thursday: Raheem Blackshear, Khalil Herbert, and Owen Wright. The news comes after second-year back Jordan James suffered a rib injury earlier this week during Monday’s practice, which will cause him to miss some time. James was projected as the team’s […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Khalil Herbert #26 of the Indianapolis Colts runs against Odafe Oweh #98 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the first quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced that they hosted three running backs for a workout on Thursday: Raheem Blackshear, Khalil Herbert, and Owen Wright. The news comes after second-year back Jordan James suffered a rib injury earlier this week during Monday’s practice, which will cause him to miss some time. James was projected as the team’s No. 2 running back before the injury, and the opportunity will allow for rookie Kaelon Black and veterans Patrick Taylor Jr. and Sincere McCormick to get more opportunities in camp. But with the injury, San Francisco is also looking for more depth, which is where Thursday’s workout comes in. Of the three running backs brought in, Khalil Herbert is easily the most accomplished in the NFL, having accumulated nearly 2,000 rushing yards over five NFL seasons. Herbert was a sixth-round pick of the Chicago Bears in the 2021 NFL Draft, and he quickly received opportunities as a rookie. He played in all 17 games in 2021, starting two, while rushing for 433 yards and two touchdowns in 103 carries. He followed that up with the two best years of his career. In 2022, Herbert rushed for 731 yards and four touchdowns on 5.7 yards per carry in 13 games, while starting one. Then, in 2023, the running back went for 611 yards and two touchdowns in 132 carries. Herbert’s role dwindled after that as he was traded to the Cincinnati Bengals in 2024 during the year, getting only 36 carries during the year. Then, last season, he played seven games for the New York Jets, rushing for 52 total yards. Blackshear went undrafted in the 2022 NFL Draft and was signed by the Carolina Panthers during the 2022 season. He spent three years with the team, rushing for 203 yards and three touchdowns. He’s since spent time on several practice squads, including with the Jets last year. Wright was undrafted in the 2023 NFL Draft, and has bounced around several practice squads throughout his three-year career. His lone NFL action came last season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he played in three games.
